The deserters describe hiding from patrols, relying on smugglers and volunteer networks, and enduring days in forests and on the road with little food or shelter before reaching safety. Their stories also capture the fear of being caught: desertion in wartime Russia can mean years in prison, and the men say they knew capture would likely mean being sent back to the front or jailed. The feature comes as Russia's manpower strain grows, with Meduza and Mediazona estimating at least 490,000 Russian soldiers dead by late September 2026 and 700,000 including the missing. While desertion remains a small fraction of Russia's total force, the accounts suggest the routes out are becoming more organised, with established networks helping soldiers disappear. For readers, the piece offers a human counterpoint to the casualty statistics — the individual decisions behind the numbers.

articles.title: Ukrainian drones strike rocket-fuel plant in Russia's Tula region
articles.description: Ukrainian drones struck the Yefremov synthetic rubber plant in Russia's Tula region overnight on November 27, Ukrainska Pravda reported. The plant produces materials used in rocket fuel, making it a strategic target in Ukraine's campaign against Russia's military industry. The strike was part of a wider overnight operation that also reached St. Petersburg, where Russian authorities said 44 drones were shot down.
articles.body: Ukraine's Defence Forces struck the Yefremov synthetic rubber plant in Russia's Tula region with drones overnight on November 27, Ukrainska Pravda reported. The plant produces materials used in rocket fuel, making it a strategic target in Ukraine's campaign against the Russian military-industrial complex. The strike was part of a wider overnight drone operation that also reached St. Petersburg and Leningrad region, where Russian authorities reported shooting down 44 drones. Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russian chemical plants, refineries and explosives factories in recent months, aiming to choke off the supplies that sustain Russia's missile and drone production. Russian officials have not yet confirmed damage at the Yefremov plant, and details of the impact remain unclear. The attack follows Ukrainian drone strikes on Rosneft refineries in the Samara region earlier this week, which Kyiv said disrupted fuel supplies for the Russian military. The Tula strike shows Ukraine extending its reach to industrial targets deeper inside Russia, well beyond the border regions that bore the brunt of earlier attacks.

articles.title: Ukrainska Pravda editor-in-chief reports systematic pressure and surveillance of journalists
articles.description: Ukrainska Pravda editor-in-chief Sevgil Musaeva said on November 27 that the outlet's leadership and investigative journalists face systematic pressure and surveillance, which she links to their reporting on Davyd Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People faction. She cited cars with operative plates tailing crews and appearing near journalists' parents' homes, and a smear campaign by the Trukha Telegram network since August. She has informed international rights groups, and parliament's free-speech committee is gathering information.
articles.body: Sevgil Musaeva, editor-in-chief of Ukrainska Pravda, said on November 27 that the outlet's leadership and investigative journalists face systematic pressure and surveillance, which she links to their work on materials about Davyd Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction. Musaeva said staff have repeatedly noticed cars with operative number plates following film crews in Kyiv and beyond, and that such cars appeared near the homes of journalists' parents. In one case, a member of the investigations team noticed surveillance during a trip to visit his wife's parents in Lviv, where the outlet believes three Security Service (SBU) crews may have been involved. Since August, the Telegram channel Trukha Ukraina and its regional outlets have regularly published material targeting Ukrainska Pravda and its investigations chief Mykhailo Tkach, with the campaign intensifying after the outlet's November 18 investigation into pressure on the anti-corruption bodies NABU and SAPO. The outlet's publisher also received a parliamentary inquiry from Danylo Hetmantsev, head of the finance committee, about the outlet's cooperation with 350 sole proprietors — which Musaeva described as pressure, since the sum was named publicly before the publisher could respond. Musaeva said she has informed international human rights organisations about the situation, and the parliamentary committee on freedom of speech is gathering information on a possible response. The outlet says it will continue its investigations into Arakhamia's influence on state decisions.

articles.title: Government orders verification of all men aged 17–60 in the Oberih military register
articles.description: Ukraine's Cabinet has ordered a verification of the data of all men aged 17 to 60 in the Oberih military register, under resolution No. 1466 of November 25. The Defence Ministry has 120 days to update the records once the checks are done. The move tightens mobilisation administration as the war nears its fifth year, cross-checking Oberih against other state registers.
articles.body: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has ordered a verification of data on men aged 17 to 60 in the Oberih military register, under resolution No. 1466 dated November 25. The government gave the Defence Ministry 120 days to update the records after the checks are completed. Oberih is the central register of conscripts and reservists, and the verification is part of Kyiv's tightening of mobilisation administration as the war approaches its fifth year. The move comes as Ukraine works to close gaps in its military records and ensure that call-up data is accurate, amid continued Russian pressure on the front and warnings of new large-scale strikes. The resolution was one of the most discussed domestic decisions of the day, drawing attention from both supporters, who see it as necessary housekeeping for the war effort, and critics, who worry about how the data will be used. The verification will involve cross-checking Oberih against other state registers, including migration and tax records. The government has not said what consequences, if any, will follow for men whose data is found to be out of date, beyond the requirement to update it.

articles.title: Russian strikes on Nizhyn and Malyn kill three people at civilian enterprises
articles.description: Russian forces struck an enterprise in Nizhyn, Chernihiv region, on Friday, November 27, killing two people, and hit a civilian enterprise in the Malynska community of Zhytomyr region, killing one more. The strikes were part of a day of continued Russian attacks on civilian and industrial targets, following the overnight drone barrage on nine regions. They bring the day's reported death toll across Ukraine to six.
articles.body: Russian forces struck the city of Nizhyn in Chernihiv region on Friday, November 27, killing two people at one of the city's enterprises, Ukrainska Pravda reported. On the same day, Russian troops attacked a civilian enterprise in the Malynska community of Zhytomyr region, killing one person. The two strikes were part of a day of continued Russian attacks on civilian and industrial targets across Ukraine, following the overnight drone barrage that hit nine regions. Nizhyn, a historic city in northern Ukraine, has been repeatedly targeted during the war, and the strike on a working enterprise underlines the risk to civilians far from the front line. Details of the damage in both cases remain limited, with emergency services working at the sites. The deaths add to the day's toll of six killed across Ukraine over the past 24 hours, with victims also reported in Kharkiv, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions. The strikes came as Ukraine's air defences and energy workers continued to deal with the aftermath of the overnight attack, which left six regions partly without power.

articles.title: Death toll in Sloviansk apartment strike rises to eight as more bodies are recovered
articles.description: Rescuers pulled three more bodies from the rubble of an apartment building in Sloviansk hit by a Russian FAB-500 bomb on November 22, bringing the death toll to eight, Ukrainian media reported on November 27. Emergency crews have worked at the site for five days. Sloviansk, in Donetsk region near the front line, has been under near-constant attack, and the toll from Russian strikes often rises for days as rescue work continues.
articles.body: Rescuers recovered the bodies of three more people from the rubble of an apartment building in Sloviansk destroyed by a Russian air strike on November 22, bringing the death toll to eight, Ukrainian media reported on November 27. The building was hit by a FAB-500 guided bomb, which collapsed part of the multi-storey block and trapped residents under the rubble. Emergency crews have been working at the site for five days, clearing debris floor by floor as hopes of finding survivors faded. Sloviansk, in Donetsk region, sits close to the front line and has been under near-constant attack, but the November 22 strike was one of the deadliest on the city in recent weeks. The rising toll is a reminder of how the casualty figures from Russian strikes often climb for days after the attack, as rescue work continues. The eight dead include residents who were at home when the bomb hit in the evening. The strike has added to the mounting civilian toll in Donetsk region, where Russian attacks killed and injured people in several towns over the past day alone.

articles.title: Cabinet finalises 2027 draft budget for second reading
articles.description: Ukraine's Cabinet has finalised the draft state budget for 2027 and approved it for a second reading, sending it to parliament on November 27. The budget comes as EU leaders failed to agree a €45 billion loan for Ukraine at their summit, and the Accounting Chamber warns the state still lacks over 102 billion hryvnias for military pay this year. The World Bank has meanwhile provided $450 million to the general fund, split between business support and public finance management.
articles.body: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has finalised the draft state budget for 2027 and approved it for its second reading in parliament, with the document to be sent to the Verkhovna Rada on November 27. The budget is being drawn up under extraordinary pressure: EU leaders at their November 26–27 summit failed to agree on a €45 billion loan for Ukraine or on the bloc's 2028–2034 budget, with Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria demanding exemptions, and a final deal now expected at a December 17–18 meeting. Meanwhile, the World Bank has provided $450 million to Ukraine's general fund, with $225 million earmarked for business support under the RISE programme and $225 million for public finance management under SURGE. Ukraine's Accounting Chamber has warned that the state still lacks more than 102 billion hryvnias for military pay by the end of this year, underlining how tight the finances are. The 2027 budget will have to balance defence spending, which consumes the largest share of the budget, against social payments and reconstruction needs. Parliament is expected to debate the draft in the coming weeks, with the government under pressure to show both the EU and the IMF that its finances are under control.

articles.title: Diablo 4 Season 16 'Season of Tyrael's Gambit' starts December 1 — and Old Tristram is staying for good
articles.description: Blizzard has detailed Diablo 4's Season 16, 'Season of Tyrael's Gambit', launching December 1 with a merged dual Reaper boss, two new progression trees and reworked Helltides. The bigger news: Blizzard is breaking tradition and keeping much of the Diablo 2 anniversary season permanent — Old Tristram, Deckard Cain and the Diablo boss fight are staying in the game for good.
articles.body: Blizzard has revealed Diablo 4's 16th season, 'Season of Tyrael's Gambit', which starts on December 1, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. PT alongside patch 3.3.0, with pre-downloads opening November 30 on Battle.net, Xbox and PlayStation. The seasonal quest continues the war against the Úllo Sar death cult, with Tyrael returning to help players uncover who leads the sect. The headline threat is a merged dual Reaper boss: the Corrupted Reaper joins forces with the Fractured Reaper, combining their abilities into a single fight, first in the questline and then as a repeatable Lair Boss in Zarbinzet dropping Mythic Uniques. Two new progression trees arrive — War Plans Tactics, which lets players steer which activities and rewards appear, and Tyrael's Boons, offering non-combat bonuses — alongside new Horadric items and reworked Helltides that now always have one event live, with Aberrant Cinders carrying over up to 5,000. The bigger surprise is what is staying: Blizzard is making a large part of the popular Season 15 'Hell's Legacy' content permanent, reversing its usual practice of deleting seasonal content. Old Tristram and Deckard Cain remain in the game for good, along with the Prime Evil Council fight in Uber Tristram, Capstone Dungeons, the World Boss Diablo summon and the Moophisto boss on Cow Island. The move follows loud player demand after the Diablo 2 anniversary season, and Blizzard has also confirmed Diablo 4 will keep getting seasons even after Diablo 5 launches.

articles.title: Demo of Russian RPG 'Saturn: Legacy' from ex-Baldur's Gate 3 developers to be shown at Comic Con Igromir
articles.description: Astrum Entertainment will show a playable demo of 'Saturn: Legacy', a sci-fi action RPG from St. Petersburg studio Ninsar Games, at Comic Con Igromir in Moscow on December 3–6. Set in 2065, it stars a neurointerface operator who can possess robots on Saturn's moons after a machine uprising. The studio's staff includes former Baldur's Gate 3 developers; release is planned for 2027.
articles.body: Publisher Astrum Entertainment has partnered with St. Petersburg studio Ninsar Games and will bring a playable demo of the sci-fi action RPG 'Saturn: Legacy' (Сатурн. Наследие) to Comic Con Igromir in Moscow, which runs December 3–6, 2026 at the Timiryazev Centre. The game is set in Russia in 2065, three years after the events of the first game, and stars Alexey Vengerov, the operator of a neurointerface called 'Reflection' that can transfer a person's consciousness into a machine's body. An experiment in an underground science complex in the Urals goes wrong, the robots rise up, and Vengerov is blamed — so he must clear his name and expose a technological conspiracy. On Earth the hero survives in labs overrun by the machine uprising, while through 'Reflection' he can take control of robots on Saturn's moons. Tasks can be solved by force, intellect or cunning, and choices shape the story. The full release is planned for 2027, with the project backed by Russia's Internet Development Institute, whose funding terms require it to launch before October 29, 2027. Ninsar Games employs former developers of Divinity: Original Sin 2, Baldur's Gate 3 and Encased, and the studio's first game, the tactical RPG 'Saturn', launched on October 29, 2024 and is distributed for free. Astrum's stand will also feature Throne and Liberty, Crystal of Atlan and several mobile titles.

articles.title: Dead or Alive 6 opens all 25 paid fighters for free — but only for a week
articles.description: The free version of Dead or Alive 6 has unlocked all 25 paid fighters for free — but only for a week. Normally the free Core Fighters edition offers just a small roster, with the rest sold as DLC. It is a rare chance to try the full cast at no cost, timed to the Black Friday sale season.
articles.body: The free version of Dead or Alive 6 is running a limited giveaway: all 25 paid fighters have been unlocked for free, but only for one week. Normally the free-to-play Dead or Alive 6: Core Fighters edition includes just a small rotating roster, with the rest of the cast sold as paid DLC, so this is a rare chance to try the full lineup without paying. The offer covers the entire paid roster of 25 fighters, letting newcomers sample every character's moves and playstyle before deciding whether to buy anyone permanently. For a fighting game that lives or dies by its roster variety, a full-cast trial week is a meaningful window — especially for players who never picked up the game at launch. The timing lines up with the Black Friday sale season, when the full game and its DLC are typically discounted across storefronts. Anyone curious should jump in quickly, though: once the week is over, the paid fighters lock again and the free version returns to its usual limited selection.

articles.title: First teaser for Gremlins 3 hides in an AT&T Christmas ad — film due in 2028
articles.description: The first teaser for Gremlins 3 has surfaced inside an AT&T Christmas ad made with Skydance, showing updated designs for Gizmo and Stripe watching TV. The tagline is 'Some holiday rules are meant to be broken.' Chris Columbus is directing the threequel, with a premiere planned for 2028.
articles.body: The first teaser for Gremlins 3 has arrived in an unlikely place: a new AT&T Christmas commercial made with Skydance. The ad, promoting the telecom's services for the holidays, doubles as a first look at the updated designs of the Mogwai Gizmo and the villainous Stripe, who are shown watching television together. Its slogan is 'Some holiday rules are meant to be broken' — a nod to the franchise's famous rules about Mogwai care. Skydance is preparing the third film with director Chris Columbus, who directed the original 1984 Gremlins, at the helm. The premiere of the threequel is planned for 2028, more than 35 years after Gremlins 2: The New Batch. The teaser-by-ad approach is a deliberately low-key way to reintroduce the creatures before a full marketing push, and the refreshed character designs are already drawing attention from fans of the original films. For now, the short commercial is the only footage of the new film in existence.

articles.title: Software glitch disrupts spacecraft's long-awaited arrival at Mercury
articles.description: A software glitch has disrupted BepiColombo's long-awaited arrival at Mercury, just as the joint European-Japanese spacecraft was closing in after an eight-year journey. The probe was approaching the planet on November 21 for the delicate task of entering a lasting orbit. Getting into orbit around Mercury is one of the hardest maneuvers in spaceflight.
articles.body: BepiColombo, the joint mission of the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, has run into trouble at the very end of its long journey to Mercury. After eight years in space, the spacecraft was hurtling toward its destination on November 21, ready for the delicate task of securing a lasting orbit around the smallest planet in the solar system. A software glitch has now disrupted that long-awaited arrival, interrupting the carefully choreographed sequence meant to place BepiColombo into orbit around Mercury. Orbit insertion around Mercury is one of the hardest maneuvers in spaceflight: the planet sits deep in the Sun's gravity well, so a spacecraft must shed enormous speed without burning up or flying past. BepiColombo has spent eight years using planetary flybys to brake gradually, making the timing of this final approach critical. The mission is a flagship European-Japanese collaboration designed to study Mercury's surface, magnetic field and exosphere up close. Engineers will now be working to understand what the glitch did to the arrival sequence and whether the orbit insertion can be recovered or retried.

articles.title: Black Friday is officially live: CNN Underscored picks 150 deals worth shopping
articles.description: Black Friday is officially live, and CNN Underscored has handpicked 150 deals it says are worth shopping, from Apple AirTags at a new all-time low of $18 to AirPods Pro 3 at $100 off. The deals team says the year's lowest prices are already up and will keep updating them through the weekend. Shoppers still camped outside stores overnight for in-person doorbusters.
articles.body: Black Friday is officially here, and CNN Underscored's deals team has handpicked 150 discounts it says are actually worth shopping, after combing the web around the clock for the past week. The editors say the year's lowest prices are already live on everything from gifts and household essentials to tech and winter gear, and they will keep hunting for new offers through the end of the long weekend, breaking them down by category. Among the standouts: Apple's newest AirTags (2nd Gen) have fallen to a new all-time low of $18 at Amazon, and AirPods Pro 3 are $100 off for the first time at $149. The Shark TurboBlade Cool + Heat Fan, a winner of CNN Underscored's inaugural Innovation Awards, is half price, and a HexClad 10-inch hybrid frying pan is down to under $120 for only the second time this year. Nintendo gear features among the deals, alongside brands like Hoka, Anker and The North Face. Senior deals editor Rikka Altland, who has covered the event for 12 years, says shoppers no longer need to wait for midnight doorbusters — top retailers now run their best prices for days. Shoppers still turned out in person overnight: CNN footage showed people camping in tents and sleeping bags outside stores on Thanksgiving evening, with Target offering the first 100 guests a chance at $25, $50 or $100 gift cards, and one $1,000 card.

articles.title: Two missed Olympics, two devastating injuries, one world title: Skye Blakely's long road back
articles.description: Skye Blakely, 21, has completed one of gymnastics' great comebacks, winning the all-around world title in October after a torn elbow ligament and a torn Achilles cost her two Olympic teams. She is the ninth American woman to win the crown and the first since Simone Biles in 2023. With two years to the Los Angeles Games, she is now Team USA's brightest hope.
articles.body: Skye Blakely is dreaming again — and at 21, after two catastrophic injuries and two missed Olympics, that counts as daring. A torn ulnar collateral ligament in her elbow required Tommy John surgery, and a torn Achilles tendon later robbed her of a second shot at an Olympic team, leaving her to struggle through the physical toll of recovery and the mental anguish of wondering whether the path she had envisioned since childhood was blocked for good. Blakely, who started gymnastics at seven after watching Gabby Douglas win all-around gold at London 2012, ruptured the UCL in her elbow during warmups on vault, her first apparatus, and needed a seven-month recovery. Now firmly on the other side of it all, she won the all-around world championship crown in October in Rotterdam, becoming the ninth American woman to do so and the first since Simone Biles in 2023. She entered the final in second place before opening with a 14.200 on vault, the second-highest score of the final, and finished four rotations mistake-free and injury-free on one of the sport's biggest stages. With Jordan Chiles and Sunisa Lee working on comebacks and Biles still silent about her future, Blakely emerges — at least for now — as the brightest hope for Team USA heading toward the Los Angeles Games in 2028, even if she insists it feels like being little again.

articles.title: Tyson Fury's wife clarifies he has not been diagnosed with schizophrenia
articles.description: Tyson Fury's wife Paris has clarified that her husband has 'never' been diagnosed with schizophrenia, correcting a remark in Netflix's new documentary 'Tyson Fury', released Friday. Netflix says it has edited the film following the family's clarification. Fury faces Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11, and British boxing authorities are looking into his earlier comments.
articles.body: Tyson Fury's wife Paris has said her husband has 'never' been diagnosed with schizophrenia, days after the couple discussed an apparent diagnosis in quotes shared by Netflix ahead of the release of a documentary about the former heavyweight champion. The feature-length film 'Tyson Fury', released on Netflix on Friday, details years of mental health struggles and addiction. 'I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,' Paris said in a statement shared by Netflix with CNN on Friday. 'I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word schizophrenic.' She continued: 'Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love.' Netflix confirmed it has edited the documentary in response: 'Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.' In the film, Fury describes the decline in his mental health after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, recalling crippling anxiety and sleepless nights, and says a psychiatrist assessed him for depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. Fury is set to face Anthony Joshua at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11 Eastern time (December 12 in the UK), and the British Boxing Board of Control told BBC Sport it was looking into his comments about schizophrenia ahead of the fight.

articles.title: Believe fully acquires Lili Louise Musique, parent of French indie tôt Ou tard, after buying 49% stake in 2018
articles.description: Believe has fully acquired Lili Louise Musique, the parent of French independent label tôt Ou tard, becoming the group's sole shareholder. The deal, announced November 25, completes a partnership that began in 2018 when Believe bought a 49% stake for €12.3 million. Founder Vincent Frèrebeau stays in charge, and each brand keeps its identity and artistic autonomy.
articles.body: Believe has fully acquired Lili Louise Musique, the parent company of French label tôt Ou tard, becoming the group's sole shareholder, the Paris-headquartered company announced on Wednesday, November 25. The deal is described as a natural continuation of a partnership that began in 2018, when Believe acquired a 49% stake from Wagram Music — a stake its pre-IPO filings later showed cost €12.3 million. Financial terms of the full buyout were not disclosed. The acquisition covers all of Lili Louise Musique's activities, including tôt Ou tard, live performance company Zouave, publishing arm LLM, the innovative-projects company Guess What and stakes in live music company Uni-t. Founder Vincent Frèrebeau will continue to lead the group and retain full control over its direction and artistic choices, while each brand keeps its identity, organisation, teams, premises and corporate culture. Frèrebeau said the deal protects what makes the group unique in a market moving faster and faster, calling long-term thinking more valuable than ever. Believe CEO Denis Ladegaillerie called it an immense pride and joy, praising Frèrebeau's rare ability to discover talents and support them over decades — tôt Ou tard celebrated its 30th anniversary this year. The move follows Believe's October decision to expand Romain Vivien's role, putting him in direct charge of its EMEA, Americas and APAC regions. Believe operates in more than 50 countries and employs more than 2,000 people.

articles.title: PRS for Music signs Roblox licensing deal — including royalty payments for songwriters
articles.description: PRS for Music has signed a licensing agreement with Roblox covering music use across the gaming and creation platform, with royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers starting in 2027. Roblox averaged 138 million daily active users in Q3 2026. The deal is a landmark for PRS's push to license music in games, after it sued Steam operator Valve in March over alleged unlicensed use.
articles.body: PRS for Music has signed a licensing agreement with Roblox covering the use of music across the gaming and creation platform, the UK collection society announced on Wednesday, November 25. PRS says it will start distributing royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers in 2027, and framed the deal as establishing an important principle: when music helps create value within online worlds, the people who write and compose it should share in that value. Financial terms were not disclosed. Roblox hosts millions of user-built games and virtual worlds and reported an average of 138 million daily active users in Q3 2026 — up 12% quarter-over-quarter but down 9% year-over-year. PRS chief commercial officer Dan Gopal said games are now among the world's most consumed entertainment media, and partnerships like this establish foundations for how the industry moves forward. The deal forms part of a wider PRS effort to license music use in video games: in March it launched legal action against Steam operator Valve, alleging Valve has never obtained a licence for PRS members' music since the store launched in 2003. In a May 2025 op-ed, PRS executives called for a shift away from buyouts towards a consistent royalty model for music in games, pointing to Roblox and Fortnite. Roblox has also struck music deals with distributors, including Symphonic earlier this month and Too Lost in July, and settled a $200 million-plus NMPA publishers' lawsuit in 2021. PRS paid out £1.07 billion ($1.41 billion) to songwriters, composers and publishers in 2025, up 4.9% year-on-year, and represents more than 190,000 members.

articles.title: City of Baltimore sues Vivid Seats over alleged 'bait-and-switch' ticket pricing
articles.description: The City of Baltimore is suing Vivid Seats, alleging the resale platform advertises ticket prices fans can never actually pay. Filed November 23, the suit cites a J. Cole ticket at CFG Bank Arena advertised at $156 that cost $238 at checkout, and a Trevor Noah ticket rising from $125 to $205. Vivid Seats denies the allegations, saying it has shown all-in pricing nationwide since the FTC rule took effect in May 2025.
articles.body: The City of Baltimore is suing Vivid Seats, alleging that the ticket resale platform advertises prices Baltimore fans can never actually pay. The lawsuit, brought under the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance, was filed in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City on Monday, November 23. The city wants a court order stopping four pricing practices — misleading search ads, drip pricing, two-ticket bundling and late-disclosed fees — plus civil penalties for each violation and attorneys' fees. A pre-suit investigation identified the practices: paid Google listings allegedly showed prices fans could not get on the Vivid Seats site until at least July 2026; prices allegedly climbed screen by screen through checkout; some per-ticket prices applied only to buyers purchasing at least two tickets; and mandatory service and delivery fees were shown only after the first page until at least April 2026. The complaint cites examples from shows by J. Cole, BTS, Megan Moroney and Trevor Noah: a J. Cole ticket at CFG Bank Arena advertised at $156 cost $238 by the final checkout screen, and a Trevor Noah ticket rose from $125 to $205 — increases of roughly 53% and 64%. City Solicitor Ebony M. Thompson said that when a family sees a $98 ticket advertised and ends up paying $154, that is not a fee, it is a bait-and-switch. Vivid Seats, headquartered in Chicago, denies the allegations and says it has presented all-in pricing nationwide since the FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect in May 2025. Baltimore is not the first public body to sue: Pennsylvania prosecutors sued in May 2025 alleging checkout fees could add up to 80%, and in April rival StubHub agreed to refund $10 million in fees to settle FTC allegations. The UK's Competition and Markets Authority fined StubHub UK close to £900,000 in June over similar checkout fees.

articles.title: Beatles attraction at former Apple Corps HQ — where the band played its final public concert — approved by London council
articles.description: Westminster City Council has approved plans for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former Apple Corps headquarters where the band played its famous rooftop concert in 1969. The attraction, called The Beatles at 3 Savile Row, is expected to open in 2027 with archive exhibitions, a recreated basement studio and access to the rooftop. Apple Corps expects up to 900 visitors a day on weekdays and 1,140 on weekends.
articles.body: Westminster City Council has approved plans for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former London headquarters of Apple Corps. The council's Planning Committee signed off on the plans on Tuesday, November 24. Apple Corps, which manages The Beatles' creative and business interests, first unveiled the project in May under the name The Beatles at 3 Savile Row. The plans cover exhibitions drawn from the Apple Corps archives, a recreated version of the basement recording studio and access to the rooftop, and the attraction is expected to open in 2027. The Beatles worked on Let It Be in the building's basement studio in 1969, and on January 30 that year John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, joined by Billy Preston, played on the roof — the band's last public live performance, later featured in Peter Jackson's 2021 documentary Get Back. Apple Corps CEO Tom Greene told the committee the company wants to return the front of the building to how it looked and felt in 1969, right down to the Apple green carpet, supplemented with the latest AV technology, and to host bookable evening events plus a cafe and bar in the basement. Draft planning conditions reportedly included a ban on live music on the rooftop terrace, and the BBC reported Apple Corps expects as many as 900 visitors a day on weekdays and 1,140 on weekends. The Savile Row Bespoke Association objected, warning the street's narrow sidewalks could become congested. In October, Apple Corps announced plans to take over The Beatles Story in Liverpool and move it to a 100,000-square-foot site in the city centre in 2028. In August, Universal Music Group signed a global partnership with Apple Corps covering Beatles merchandise, licensing and e-commerce.

articles.title: Mary Bono asks appeals court to overturn Cher's win in Sonny Bono song royalties fight
articles.description: Mary Bono, the widow of Sonny Bono, has asked the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit to overturn Cher's win in their fight over royalties from Sonny's songs, including 'I Got You Babe'. Her brief, filed November 24, argues Cher already received nearly fifty years of royalties and that the reclaimed rights belong to Sonny's heirs alone. A federal judge ruled in November 2025 that Cher remains entitled to half of Sonny's income from pre-1974 songs.
articles.body: Mary Bono, the widow of Sonny Bono, has asked a federal appeals court to overturn Cher's win in their fight over royalties from Sonny's songs. Her lawyers filed a 59-page opening brief with the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit on Tuesday, November 24. A federal judge ruled in November 2025 that Cher remains entitled to half of Sonny's income from songs he wrote before February 1, 1974, including 'I Got You Babe', and awarded her more than $187,000 plus interest for withheld publishing royalties. Mary Bono's brief asks the court to rule that the US rights and royalties in those songs now belong to Sonny's widow and four children free and clear of the rights granted to Cher under the pair's 1978 divorce settlement. The dispute turns on copyright termination: in 2016, Mary Bono and two of the children served notice reclaiming, on behalf of all five heirs, rights Sonny had granted to his music publishers in 1966, with effective dates from 2018 to 2026. The heirs then stopped paying Cher her 50% share, arguing the reclaimed rights belonged entirely to them; Cher sued in October 2021. The brief's main argument is that Sonny could not sign away rights that did not yet exist — the termination rights vested in the heirs, not him, in 2016 — and that Cher, who already received nearly fifty years of royalties, is legally equivalent to any third party who obtained a royalty right by contract. As a fallback, it argues only the publishers' 30% share should go to the heirs alone, leaving Cher with the 31.5 cents per dollar she received before the terminations, rather than the roughly 45 cents the ruling gives her. The brief also appeals the ruling on who administers the royalties and notes Cher sold her divorce-settlement rights in January 2023 to Irving Azoff's Iconic Artists Group. Cher's appeal over denied attorneys' fees has been consolidated with Mary Bono's.

articles.title: Musixmatch launches enhanced Pro for Artists platform with fan analytics, lyric merch and optional AI licensing coming soon
articles.description: Musixmatch has launched a new version of its Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform, used by more than 1.5 million artists. The update adds lyric merchandise sales, a Wallet for managing earnings, and an analytics dashboard tracking how listeners engage with lyrics. Optional AI licensing is coming soon, letting artists earn from authorized use of their lyrics by AI platforms.
articles.body: Musixmatch has launched a new version of its Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform, the Bologna-based company announced, with the update going live on Wednesday, November 25. The platform is now used by more than 1.5 million artists, and the new version moves it beyond lyric distribution into fan insights, promotion and new ways to earn: artists can sell lyric merchandise to fans via the Musixmatch app and website, manage those earnings in a new Wallet, and track how listeners engage with their lyrics through an Insights & Analytics dashboard combining streaming activity, follower data and lyric views. Musixmatch says optional AI licensing is coming soon to the Wallet, giving artists an additional opportunity to earn from the authorized use of their lyrics by AI platforms — though it did not name the AI platforms or give a launch date. Co-president Marco Paglia said lyrics are one of the most powerful ways people connect with music, and the company is now putting tools built for the world's biggest labels into the hands of independent artists. The platform's AI Enrichment tool transcribes lyrics and synchronizes them line by line and word by word, and also produces AI-generated meanings and themes for songs. Artists also get Music Lens, an AI agent unveiled in November 2025 that helps them explore their catalogs. The planned AI licensing follows deals Musixmatch signed in October 2025 with the publishing arms of all three majors — Sony Music Publishing, Universal Music Publishing Group and Warner Chappell Music — giving it access to catalogs of more than 15 million works. In October, Musixmatch also acquired Music Reports, the Los Angeles company behind the Songdex copyright registry, describing the deal as making it a full-stack rights and royalties platform.

articles.title: The Killers' Dave Keuning reveals he suffered a 'major stroke': 'I am alive and well'
articles.description: The Killers guitarist Dave Keuning, 50, has revealed he suffered a major stroke two weeks ago that left him with only a 40% chance of survival. Writing on Instagram on Thanksgiving, he said a blood clot cut off blood supply to the right side of his brain, leaving him blind in one eye and without function on his left side before emergency surgery. He says he has miraculously recovered fully — and can still play guitar just as well as before.
articles.body: The Killers guitarist Dave Keuning has revealed he suffered a major stroke two weeks ago that nearly cost him his life. In an Instagram post shared on Thanksgiving, November 26, the 50-year-old founding member of the band said his wife Emilie acted fast, getting him straight to hospital and into surgery. He had a blood clot in his brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of his brain, and by the time he arrived he was blind in one eye and had lost function on his left side — though he still was not able to realise he was having a stroke. Doctors told him he had a 40% chance of survival and would have disabilities afterwards, but, he wrote, by some miracle I am fine. He reassured fans that his guitar playing is intact — it was the first thing he checked when he woke up from surgery — and that he can use his hands and feet and talk just like before. The post also shared happier news: he and Emilie welcomed a daughter, Odette, three months ago, and he has a 21-year-old son, Kyler, from a past relationship. Keuning formed The Killers with Brandon Flowers in 2001, stepped off the road in 2017 to spend more time with his family, and returned in 2021 to help record the band's album Pressure Machine. Flowers recently unveiled a solo album, Thrasher, and has teased a new Killers album, saying it is more likely early 2028 than the end of 2027. Keuning stressed the lesson of his scare in the post: the first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital.

articles.title: Former Buzzcocks drummer Phil Barker dead at 65
articles.description: Phil Barker, drummer for pioneering British punk band Buzzcocks from 1992 to 2006, has died at 65. The band announced on November 26 that he died peacefully in his sleep on Saturday, November 21, on the Isle of Wight, after a five-year battle with cancer. He is survived by Deb, his wife of 26 years.
articles.body: Phil Barker, the former drummer of pioneering British punk band Buzzcocks, has died at 65. The band announced his passing on its official website on November 26, saying he died peacefully in his sleep on Saturday, November 21, 2026, on the Isle of Wight, after a five-year battle with cancer. Barker sat behind the drum kit for Buzzcocks from 1992 to 2006, a 14-year tenure that covered the band's busy 1990s and early 2000s period, and he was described by the band as a key figure in the group's success during those years. The cancer battle had been kept largely private. He is survived by Deb, his wife of 26 years. Tributes have poured in from across the British music press and from fans remembering Barker's driving, melodic drumming on the band's later albums and reunion-era tours. Buzzcocks, formed in Manchester in 1976, were one of the bands that helped pioneer British punk rock, and Barker joined long after the original lineup's heyday, anchoring the band through its second act. News of his death travelled quickly through outlets including Page Six, Far Out Magazine and American Songwriter, all relaying the band's statement. His passing comes in a week of losses for British music, with Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor also dying at 65 and King Crimson co-founder Michael Giles dying at 84.

articles.title: Justin Timberlake says making upcoming doc series was 'really cathartic'
articles.description: Justin Timberlake says making his upcoming Apple TV docuseries was really cathartic. The pop star took over The Tonight Show on Thanksgiving, with an interview, performances and sketches, and talked about the series, his new music and how David Bowie influenced 'SexyBack'. The series follows a busy period for Timberlake, who has been back in the spotlight with new material and live shows.
articles.body: Justin Timberlake says making his upcoming docuseries was really cathartic. The pop star took over The Tonight Show on Thanksgiving, November 26, for an interview, performances and sketches, and spoke about the new Apple TV series, which looks back at his life and career. Timberlake described the process of making the series as an emotional one, revisiting decades of music, fame and personal change on camera. During the Tonight Show appearance he also discussed his new music and how David Bowie influenced 'SexyBack', one of his signature hits, and performed some of his dance classics. The docuseries arrives as Timberlake continues a busy comeback stretch, with new material and live performances keeping him in the spotlight. The Thanksgiving takeover gave him a full evening on late-night television to set the tone for the series, mixing nostalgia with new work. For fans, the series promises a candid, behind-the-scenes account from an artist who has spent more than 25 years at the top of pop, from his boy-band beginnings to his solo career and acting work. Timberlake's framing of the project as cathartic suggests it goes deeper than a standard promotional film, with the singer reflecting on the highs and the harder chapters of his career.

articles.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie settle bitter winery war that detailed abuse claims
articles.description: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled their years-long legal battle over Château Miraval, the French winery they once co-owned, a decade after their split. In a joint statement on November 25, the actors said they had settled out of court in the best interests of our family and would not comment further. The settlement ends a four-year lawsuit, though Pitt's separate litigation involving the Stoli Group continues.
articles.body: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled their bitter, years-long legal battle over Château Miraval, the French winery they once owned together, a decade after the A-list couple split. Representatives for Pitt, 62, and Jolie, 51, shared a joint statement on Wednesday, November 25: We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further. The dispute began in 2021 when Jolie sold her 50% stake in the 1,200-acre winery in the South of France — which the couple bought together in 2008 and where they married in 2014 — to Tenute del Mondo, the wine division of the Stoli Group. Pitt sued in February 2022, saying she had abandoned an agreement that he would buy her half and calling the sale vindictive and unlawful, made without his consent. The case grew increasingly contentious, with both sides seeking private communications and financial records, and the winery lawsuit became a way for details of their dispute to become public, including Jolie's abuse allegations from a 2016 private flight, which Pitt has denied. The case had been scheduled to go to trial beginning August 4, 2027. The terms of the settlement were not disclosed, and it is unclear how it affects Pitt's separate ongoing litigation involving the Stoli Group. The settlement closes the last major legal battle between the former couple, whose divorce was finalised at the end of 2024 after an eight-year process.

articles.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for weather — performers scramble as Texas band raises $350,000 to stay
articles.description: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed for the first time ever, moved from Thursday to Saturday, November 28, because of a storm bringing wind gusts up to 60 mph and heavy rain to New York. NBC will air a rerun of the 2025 parade on Thursday instead. Performers are scrambling to extend hotel stays — a high school marching band from Pearland, Texas raised $350,000 in a few hours to stay in New York for the weekend.
articles.body: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in its 100-year history, moved from Thanksgiving Day to Saturday, November 28, because of a storm forecast to hit New York. Organisers said on Wednesday that the parade would be held on Saturday, citing conversations with the city and concerns over the safety of participants and spectators, with wind gusts of up to 60 mph and moderate to heavy rain expected on Thursday. NBC, which airs the parade, will instead broadcast a rerun of the 2025 edition on Thursday, and the rescheduled parade will kick off at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on Saturday. The postponement has thrown the parade's expansive roster of performers into chaos: marching bands, dancers and acts that travelled to Manhattan for the festivities are now changing plans, checking flight schedules and trying to extend hotel stays so they can stick around for the weekend. One high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, raised $350,000 in just a few hours to extend its stay, helped by quick donations from businesses and almost 2,000 other donors. Staying in New York is expensive, especially during the holiday season, and the band's fundraising success became one of the feel-good stories of the postponement. The 100th-anniversary parade was set to celebrate the milestone with a special appearance by Blue Hippo, a 30-foot-long inflatable recreated from old photos. The storm also prompted a state of emergency across southern New York and moved Philadelphia's parade indoors.

articles.title: Ginuwine releases ridiculous videogame about stealing his masters back
articles.description: R&B veteran Ginuwine has released a free AI-generated video game, 'MY RIDE: The Ginuwine Story Game', in which players help him steal his master recordings back from his label. The four-chapter game, made by creator Anderson Westfield (LMG), sends players into a fictional Sony Music headquarters with help from Timbaland, Missy Elliott, Tank, Tweet and the late Aaliyah. It is free to play at PlayTheRide.com.
articles.body: Ginuwine has released a free video game in which fans help him steal his master recordings back from his label. The game, 'MY RIDE: The Ginuwine Story Game', was created by Anderson Westfield, known as LMG, who also offers a course on making videogames with AI, and Ginuwine promoted it on Instagram this week. The premise, in his own words: to get my masters back from my label and live free and get what's owed to me after over 30 years. The game is split into four chapters: players track down a villainous music executive named Mr. Vance, steal the masters back, bring them to the studio, broadcast them to the world and finally perform for a massive crowd. In the game, Ginuwine walks into a fictional version of Sony Music headquarters — home of Epic Records, the label he was signed to for roughly a decade, where he released five albums including 'Ginuwine… the Bachelor' (1996), '100% Ginuwine' (1999) and 'The Life' (2001) — and, after being told to leave, enlists help from his old collaborators Timbaland, Missy Elliott, Tank, Tweet and the late Aaliyah, the crew from the Supafriendz collective. The final level puts him on stage in front of 12,000 fans, and the end credits dedicate the game to late Supafriendz members Static Major, Magoo and Aaliyah. The title is a nod to 'Pony', his 1996 breakthrough hit. The game is free and playable on desktop and mobile at PlayTheRide.com, and a creator's review of it has been going viral this week. The stunt turns the long-running artist-versus-label fight over master ownership — the same battle Prince fought publicly with Warner Bros. in the 1990s — into something fans can actually play.

articles.title: John Lennon plays sax in previously unseen 1968 Beatles photos
articles.description: Previously unpublished photographs show John Lennon experimenting with a saxophone during the Beatles' September 1968 recording sessions for 'Helter Skelter'. The images come from the archive of Mal Evans, the band's devoted roadie, and feature in Kenneth Womack's forthcoming book 'With the Beatles: Mal Evans's Illustrated Journey', published December 1. Lennon had never played sax before — and neither had Evans on the trumpet he had bought the day before — yet both can be heard in the final mix.
articles.body: Previously unpublished photographs show John Lennon playing saxophone during the Beatles' September 1968 recording sessions for 'Helter Skelter', published for the first time by Rolling Stone. The images come from the personal archive of Mal Evans, the band's longtime assistant and roadie, and feature in Kenneth Womack's forthcoming book, 'With the Beatles: Mal Evans's Illustrated Journey', scheduled for publication on December 1 through Harper Pop. The photographs date from the night of September 10 into September 11, 1968, when the Beatles were adding further instrumental and vocal parts to 'Helter Skelter' in Studio Two at Abbey Road, during the sessions for the self-titled double album known as the White Album. The band had already finished the basic track the night before, but Lennon got the urge to try something completely different and picked up an alto sax — an instrument he had no idea how to play. Evans joined on trumpet, an instrument he had acquired the previous day in a second-hand shop, and neither man had ever tried his instrument before. In his diary, Evans dubbed them 'The Two Hairies on brass: John sax, self trumpet.' Remarkably, both can be heard in the final mix of 'Helter Skelter'. The 432-page book includes hundreds of previously unpublished photographs alongside annotated excerpts from Evans' memoir, diary entries, manuscripts and other items documenting the private lives of John, Paul, George and Ringo. Evans was more than a roadie — he was one of the only trusted friends in the Beatles' inner circle, a Liverpool telephone engineer who became their roadie, bodyguard, assistant and friend from the Cavern days to the end. Womack calls Lennon and Evans one of the craziest duets in rock music.

articles.title: Chart Rewind: In 2021, Taylor Swift's rerecorded 'All Too Well' ruled the Hot 100
articles.description: Billboard's Chart Rewind looks back five years to November 2021, when Taylor Swift's 10-minute version of 'All Too Well (Taylor's Version)' topped the Hot 100. The track, from the rerecorded 'Red (Taylor's Version)', became the longest song ever to reach No. 1, at 10 minutes 13 seconds, breaking a record held since 1971. It was Swift's eighth Hot 100 No. 1.
articles.body: Billboard's Chart Rewind turns the clock back five years to November 2021, when Taylor Swift's rerecorded 'All Too Well' ruled the Hot 100. The 10-minute version of the song, released as part of 'Red (Taylor's Version)', debuted at No. 1 on the chart dated November 27, 2021, giving Swift her eighth Hot 100 chart-topper. At 10 minutes and 13 seconds, it became the longest song ever to top the Hot 100, breaking a record that had stood for half a century: Don McLean's 'American Pie', which ran 8 minutes 37 seconds and spent four weeks at No. 1 in 1972. The achievement capped a huge week for Swift, whose rerecorded 'Red' also topped the Billboard 200, and it showed the commercial power of her rerecording project, which she undertook to reclaim ownership of her early catalog. 'All Too Well' had long been a fan favourite from the original 2012 'Red' album, and the extended 10-minute version — long whispered about by fans who knew a longer cut existed — became a cultural event in its own right, accompanied by a short film written and directed by Swift starring Sadie Sink and Dylan O'Brien. The Chart Rewind series revisits the chart landmarks of years past, and this week's entry lands as Swift's catalog continues to dominate: her songs remain fixtures of the charts five years on, and the rerecording project she began in 2021 reshaped how the industry thinks about catalog ownership. The record for longest No. 1 still stands.

articles.title: Watch 'Sesame Street' get festive with an adorable spoof of Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'
articles.description: Sesame Street has shared a festive music video spoof of Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You', first with Billboard on Friday, November 27. Abby Cadabby, Grover, Elmo and Cookie Monster sing about the importance of the letter U — as in unwrap, underneath, untie and unbox. The video lands as Carey's 1994 hit, which has spent 22 weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, surges back up the chart for the holidays.
articles.body: The Muppets of Sesame Street don't want a lot for Christmas — there's just one thing they need: literally U. In an adorable music video spoof of Mariah Carey's mega Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 holiday hit 'All I Want for Christmas Is You', shared first with Billboard on Friday, November 27, Abby Cadabby, Grover, Elmo and Cookie Monster croon happily about the importance of the letter U as Christmas scenes play out. A green letter U wearing a Santa hat bounces along to the music as the quartet sings that without U there would be no U words for Christmas — unwrap, underneath, untie, untangle, unbox and understand. The Muppets also reveal the U-themed Christmas gifts they hope to find under the tree: Abby Cadabby wants a unicorn, Elmo hopes for a UFO and Grover would like a ukulele, while Cookie Monster gets a pair of white underwear decorated with purple hearts, which he celebrates as a letter U Christmas miracle. The video is a classic piece of Sesame Street literacy smuggling, turning one of the most famous pop songs of all time into an alphabet lesson. It arrives at the peak of Carey's annual Christmas takeover: her 1994 hit has spent 22 weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100, first reaching the summit on the chart dated December 19, 2019, a full 25 years after its release, and it is climbing the chart again this week alongside Wham!'s 'Last Christmas'. Sesame Street is available via Netflix and PBS Kids.

articles.title: John Farnham's family gives rare update on legendary singer's health
articles.description: John Farnham's family has given a rare update on the legendary Australian singer's health, more than two years after he underwent extensive surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his throat. His son Rob says Farnham's spirits remain high and his mind is sharp, but his body is failing: he is at home in a wheelchair, requires oxygen and has 24-hour care. Farnham, 77, will never sing again, his representatives confirmed.
articles.body: John Farnham's family has given a rare update on the legendary Australian singer's health, more than two years after he underwent extensive surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his throat. His spirits remain high, his mind is sharp, but his body is failing — that is the gist of the update shared by his family. These days, the 77-year-old veteran singer is at home, where he gets around in a wheelchair and requires oxygen, and he has 24-hour care. His son Rob Farnham told 102.5 ABC Perth Breakfast: His mental state is really good. He's spending a lot of time with his grandson whom he loves. He's doing a lot of physical therapy. He's happy, he's laughing, he's joking. Rob also praised his mother Jill, who is constantly by his side: Mum definitely sacrifices herself for dad and to help dad and she's an amazing woman. The update came as the family attended the opening night of 'Whispering Jack: The John Farnham Musical' in Sydney on November 25 without him — his wife Jill and sons James and Rob represented him, and his absence was keenly felt. Farnham has largely remained away from public view since the 2022 procedure, and his representatives confirmed he will never sing again. His time away has not diminished his superstar status in Australia: an all-star tribute concert at Melbourne's Rod Laver Arena on September 20 featured 120 artists and musicians, all selected by Farnham, and raised funds for Head and Neck Cancer Australia. Fans have flooded social media with messages of love, many saying they simply want him kept comfortable.

articles.title: 'True family': Nile Rodgers remembers Duran Duran's Andy Taylor
articles.description: Nile Rodgers has paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor, who died at 65 after a battle with stage 4 prostate cancer. Rodgers, who produced Duran Duran's 1983 hit 'The Reflex' and worked closely with the band, called them true family. His tribute comes as the music world mourns Taylor, whose riffs powered 'Rio' and 'Hungry Like the Wolf'.
articles.body: Nile Rodgers has paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor, who died at 65 after a years-long battle with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer. Rodgers, the Chic co-founder and legendary producer, called the band true family in his remembrance, reflecting a relationship that goes back more than four decades. Rodgers produced Duran Duran's 1983 single 'The Reflex', which became the band's first US No. 1, and his sleek, funk-inflected production helped define the band's sound at the height of their fame. Taylor, the band's original guitarist, died peacefully at home on Monday, November 23, surrounded by his family, after revealing his stage 4 prostate cancer diagnosis in 2022. His bandmates said his no-nonsense outlook kept them grounded and gave the band its edge. Rodgers' tribute is one of many pouring in from across the music world, from fellow musicians who worked with Taylor to fans who grew up on the band's MTV-era hits. Billboard also marked his passing with a rundown of Duran Duran's biggest chart hits: the band scored 15 top-40 Hot 100 hits between 1983 and 1993, including 'Hungry Like the Wolf', 'Rio' and 'The Reflex'. Taylor was also known for his work with the supergroup Power Station alongside Robert Palmer, John Taylor and Tony Thompson. His death, alongside Buzzcocks drummer Phil Barker and King Crimson co-founder Michael Giles, has made this a week of heavy losses for British music.

articles.title: 2027 BRIT Awards trophy designed by 'one of Britain's greatest living artists': see photos
articles.description: The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread, Billboard reports. Her design is a minimalist silver Britannia figure, cast in resin and covered in holes to expose the statue's interior — a signature Whiteread move. The trophy will be handed to winners at the ceremony on February 27, 2027, at Manchester's Co-op Live.
articles.body: The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by former Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread, Billboard reports. Whiteread, 63, was the first woman to win the Turner Prize, in 1993, and in 1997 became the first woman to represent Britain at the Venice Biennale. Her design is a minimalist silver statuette of Britannia, the helmeted warrior who is the traditional symbol of Britain, cast in resin, hand-painted in a silver hue and covered in holes to expose the interior of the statue. Whiteread explained: I used the motif of the BRIT Award and tried to change it in some way. I exposed the interior of the statue — as an artist would do with their music. The approach is characteristically hers: her career has been built on casting the space around and inside familiar things. Since 1992, a different creative has been selected each year to design the handheld trophy, and Whiteread follows an acclaimed line including Dame Zaha Hadid, Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin, Dame Vivienne Westwood, Es Devlin, Yinka Ilori, Slawn, Gabriel Moses and last year's designer Matthew Williamson, whose amber trophy referenced Manchester's worker-bee emblem. The 2027 BRIT Awards take place on Saturday, February 27, 2027, returning to Manchester's Co-op Live for a second consecutive year, with the ceremony broadcast on ITV1 and ITVX. The trophy reveal, announced on November 27, is one of the first major milestones on the road to next year's ceremony.

articles.title: Live Nation adds venue on Australia's Gold Coast
articles.description: Live Nation will operate a new 2,500-capacity live music venue, Surfers Music Hall, in Surfers Paradise on Australia's Gold Coast, with opening targeted for mid-2028. The City of Gold Coast will own the venue, and Live Nation will run it. The deal expands Live Nation's footprint in Queensland and adds a major new room to one of Australia's busiest tourist strips.
articles.body: Live Nation will operate a new live music venue on Australia's Gold Coast, Billboard reports. Surfers Music Hall is planned as a 2,500-capacity venue in Surfers Paradise, with opening targeted for mid-2028. The City of Gold Coast will own the venue, and Live Nation will operate it under the new arrangement. The deal expands Live Nation's footprint in Queensland and adds a major new room to one of Australia's busiest tourist strips, a location that draws millions of visitors a year. A dedicated 2,500-capacity hall fills a gap in the Gold Coast's live music infrastructure, giving touring artists a mid-sized room between clubs and arenas in a market that has long relied on festivals and larger venues. For Live Nation, the venue adds to a growing Australian portfolio and strengthens its position in a live market that has been booming since the pandemic, with Australian audiences turning out in record numbers for concerts. The City of Gold Coast's ownership model, with a global promoter as operator, mirrors arrangements used for major venues around the world. Construction and programming details are expected to follow as the mid-2028 opening approaches, but the announcement alone signals confidence in the Gold Coast as a touring destination. The venue is expected to host a mix of domestic and international acts, comedy and community events.

articles.title: 'Hunger Games' series returns to No. 1 on Soundtracks chart after more than a decade
articles.description: The Hunger Games franchise is back on top of Billboard's Soundtracks chart, as the soundtrack for 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' debuts at No. 1 on the chart dated November 28. It is the franchise's third chart-topping soundtrack album, and its first in more than a decade. The film's release has revived interest in the series' music across streaming.
articles.body: The Hunger Games franchise is back on top of Billboard's Soundtracks chart. The soundtrack for 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' has debuted at No. 1 on the chart dated November 28, returning the series to the summit after more than a decade away. It is the franchise's third chart-topping soundtrack album, following the successes of the original film series' music in the early 2010s, when Hunger Games soundtracks were among the biggest-selling film albums of their era. The new film's release has revived interest in the series' music across streaming, with the soundtrack performing like a major album release rather than a mere tie-in. The No. 1 debut is a reminder of the franchise's enduring commercial power: more than a decade after the original films, a new Hunger Games entry can still command the top of the chart. The soundtrack chart has been a reliable barometer of film-driven music consumption, and the Sunrise on the Reaping album's debut at No. 1 shows the film's audience is listening as well as watching. For the artists featured on the album, the chart-topper is a major showcase, and for the franchise it is proof that the Hunger Games brand still resonates with a new generation of fans. The achievement comes in a week of big chart stories, with holiday classics surging and U2's 'Carnaval de Luz' debuting at No. 1 on three Billboard album charts.

articles.title: Russia opposes NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine involving US backing for European troops
articles.description: Moscow opposes NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine that would involve US backing for European troops, RBC-Ukraine reports via Meduza. The objection lands just as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the Coalition of the Willing and the US are united on Article 5-like guarantees for Kyiv. Guarantees are now one of the central sticking points as US-brokered talks head toward a new round in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body: Russia has made clear it opposes NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine that would involve American backing for European troops, according to RBC-Ukraine, as reported by Meduza. The position was stated the same week German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the Coalition of the Willing and the United States are united on security guarantees for Ukraine similar to NATO's Article 5. Such guarantees — European troops on the ground in Ukraine, backed by American airpower, intelligence and logistics — have been discussed as the key to making any ceasefire hold, since Kyiv fears Russia would simply rearm and attack again without a credible deterrent. Moscow has consistently rejected any Western military presence in Ukraine, and its opposition to US-backed guarantees narrows the space for a deal even as Washington pushes for an agreement by January. The dispute also exposes the gap between the American and European positions: the Trump administration has shifted back to a 'land for peace' formula, while European leaders insist that territory cannot be traded without security commitments that would actually bind. For Kyiv, guarantees are the difference between a pause and a peace — and Russia's rejection of them is a reminder of how far apart the sides remain on the substance, even as the diplomacy accelerates.

articles.title: Murmansk names its second acting governor in two days after Chibis arrest — with no explanation
articles.description: Russia's Murmansk region has named its second acting governor in two days, with no explanation for the switch. Nadezhda Aksyonova was put in charge on November 23 before Governor Andrei Chibis left for Moscow, where he was detained; on November 25 the regional government website said health minister Dmitry Panychev was now acting governor. The confusion follows Chibis's arrest on embezzlement and bribery charges, with investigators now also hearing claims of around 100 million rubles in cash bribes.
articles.body: Murmansk region has had two different acting governors in the space of 48 hours, and the authorities have not explained why. When Governor Andrei Chibis left for a work trip to Moscow on November 23, deputy governor Nadezhda Aksyonova was named acting head of the region — and hours later Chibis was detained at Sheremetyevo Airport. On November 25, the day a Moscow court remanded Chibis in custody until January 23, 2027, the regional government's website announced that a different official, health minister Dmitry Panychev, was now acting governor, and said he would lead the region until the Kremlin appoints a permanent replacement. The same day, Vladimir Putin's decree dismissing Chibis appeared on the legal information portal, dated November 24 — the day before it was published. Investigators accuse Chibis of embezzling more than 1 billion rubles allocated to rebuild the Apatity–Kirovsk road, stealing over 39 million rubles from the regional construction ministry, illegal currency operations, and taking an airboat worth 8.5 million rubles as a bribe. New testimony has now surfaced in the case: a businessman involved in the investigation has told police about possible cash bribes to the former governor of around 100 million rubles. The double appointment is unusual even by the standards of Russia's choreographed regional politics, and it leaves open the question of who is actually running the strategically important Arctic region, home to Russia's Northern Fleet, while the Kremlin decides on a successor.

articles.title: Russia has spent an extra 18.6 trillion rubles on arms since 2022 — money lost to the economy for good, study finds
articles.description: Russia has spent 18.6 trillion rubles (about $230.8 billion) more on weapons and ammunition since 2022 than it would have without the full-scale war, according to calculations by Novaya Gazeta Europe reported by Meduza. The authors call that sum an irrecoverable loss to the economy: it is roughly equal to all Russian budget spending on healthcare in 2022–2024, or nearly all spending on education in the same period. Total extra military spending over 2022–2026 reached 43.6 trillion rubles once payments to soldiers, their families and defence workers are included.
articles.body: Since the full-scale invasion began, Russia has spent 18.6 trillion rubles — around $230.8 billion — extra on weapons and ammunition, above the level it would have spent had pre-war defence spending simply continued, according to a study by Novaya Gazeta Europe published on November 26 and reported by Meduza. The figure is part of a larger total: the study puts all additional military spending in 2022–2026 at 43.6 trillion rubles, of which 25 trillion went to extra payments to soldiers, their families and defence-industry workers, while the remaining 18.6 trillion funded arms production above the pre-war level — including equipment already destroyed on the battlefield and weapons still to be delivered. The authors, using SIPRI methodology and a 2017 baseline indexed at 4% a year, call the 18.6 trillion an irrecoverable loss to public welfare: it works out at 242,500 rubles for every economically active Russian, or almost four median monthly salaries, and it matches the entire Russian budget system's current spending on healthcare in 2022–2024. The study also shows how the war economy now dominates: in the first half of 2026, military-related sectors accounted for all of Russia's modest GDP growth, and in January–September 2026 defence and classified spending reached about 40% of all federal budget expenditure. Meanwhile the liquid assets of the National Wealth Fund have shrunk from 9.7 trillion rubles in February 2022 to 3.6 trillion by the end of October 2026. For 2027 the government plans 17.15 trillion rubles for national defence, with total military spending possibly reaching 22.8 trillion once other budget lines are counted — a sign the arms bill is still rising.

articles.title: Putin tells Sber AI conference the leader in AI will become 'ruler of the world', orders strategy updated to 2036
articles.description: Vladimir Putin has told Sber's AI conference that whoever leads in artificial intelligence will become the 'ruler of the world', and ordered Russia's national AI strategy updated through 2036. The president, who admitted he does not use a smartphone, also insisted AI development must not forget 'traditional values'. The speech comes as Russia tries to keep pace in AI despite sanctions cutting off access to advanced chips.
articles.body: Vladimir Putin used his appearance at Sber's artificial intelligence conference on November 26 to declare that the country that leads in AI will become the 'ruler of the world', and to order Russia's national AI strategy updated through 2036. The president, who admitted in his remarks that he does not use a smartphone, told the conference that AI is now the decisive technology of the age, and that Russia must not fall behind — while also insisting that development should not forget what he called traditional values. Sber, Russia's largest bank, is also the country's main AI developer, and its annual AI Journey conference has become the showcase for Moscow's ambitions in the field. But the ambitions sit uneasily with reality: sanctions have cut Russia off from the advanced chips that power modern AI, and Russian firms have struggled to build domestic alternatives at scale. Putin's framing of AI as a contest for world domination echoes his 2017 remark that the leader in AI 'will become the ruler of the world', and it underlines how the Kremlin now treats the technology as a matter of national security rather than just economics. The order to extend the strategy to 2036 gives the project a decade-long horizon — and a decade in which Russia will have to find a way around the hardware gap if the rhetoric is to mean anything.

articles.title: Arseny Turbin, jailed at 15 on terrorism charges, to be moved to an adult penal colony now he is 18
articles.description: Russian political prisoner Arseny Turbin, jailed at 15 on terrorism charges after distributing anti-Putin leaflets and allegedly seeking to join the Freedom of Russia Legion, will be transferred to an adult penal colony now that he has turned 18. His case has become one of the starkest examples of wartime repression reaching minors. Adult colonies are far harsher than the juvenile facility where he has been held.
articles.body: Arseny Turbin, one of Russia's youngest political prisoners, will be transferred to an adult penal colony now that he has turned 18, Meduza reports. Turbin was jailed at 15 on terrorism charges after distributing anti-Putin leaflets and allegedly trying to join the Freedom of Russia Legion, a unit of Russians fighting on Ukraine's side. He has spent his teenage years in a juvenile penal colony, and the move to an adult facility marks a grim milestone: conditions in adult colonies are far harsher, with stricter regimes, older and often violent cellmates, and far less access to education. His case has drawn attention well beyond Russia as an example of how wartime repression has reached children — prosecuted as terrorists for leaflets and for a plan to join a foreign legion that, as far as the public record shows, he never carried out. The transfer also raises a practical question about what happens to the growing number of teenagers convicted in political cases as they come of age: the juvenile system at least pretends at rehabilitation, while the adult system does not. For Turbin's family and supporters, the move means harder conditions, fewer visits and less contact with the outside world, just as he enters adulthood behind bars.

articles.title: Missiles over Europe: propaganda banner hangs by the Dutch embassy in Moscow
articles.description: A building next to the Dutch embassy in Moscow has for months carried a propaganda banner showing three missiles flying over Europe, decorated with tulips and with contrails in the colours of the Dutch flag, captioned 'Flowers of Dutch diplomacy'. Russian Telegram channels only noticed it on November 26, but photos of the same banner were posted on Facebook as early as June. The banner follows Ukraine's use of Dutch-made Ruta missiles against the Crimean Bridge and a Russian drone falling near the Dutch embassy in Kyiv.
articles.body: For months, a building standing next to the Dutch embassy in Moscow has displayed a propaganda banner showing three missiles flying over Europe, Meduza reports in a photo piece published on November 27. The missiles are decorated with tulips and their vapour trails repeat the red, white and blue of the Dutch flag, under the caption 'Flowers of Dutch diplomacy'. Russian Telegram channels drew attention to the banner on November 26, but it is not new: photographs of it were posted on Facebook back in June, and an earlier propaganda banner hung in the same spot, asking where the Netherlands had been 'for eight years while innocent children died' in Donbas. The timing of the renewed attention is no accident. On November 17, Ukraine said it had used Ruta cruise missiles to strike the Crimean Bridge; the Ruta is made in the Netherlands by Destinus, a company founded by Russian émigré Mikhail Kokorich. Two days later, on November 19, a Russian drone fell near the Dutch embassy in Kyiv, lightly damaging the building without injuring staff, and Russia's ambassador in The Hague was summoned to the Dutch Foreign Ministry. The banner is a small, ugly piece of the wider confrontation: a threat, dressed up as a joke about tulips, aimed at a NATO country's diplomats in the centre of Moscow.

articles.title: Zelensky on 'Vova' in the Dynasty tapes: 'Ask the anti-corruption bodies — they said they have no questions for me'
