articles.description: In a BBC interview published November 26, Volodymyr Zelensky was asked who 'Vova' is on the tapes in the Dynasty corruption case — and deflected the question to investigators: 'You can ask the anti-corruption institutions. They publicly said they have no questions for me. I think that is the answer.' He also denied obstructing NABU and SAP, saying the agencies are independent and he cannot intervene, though he acknowledged checks into some security-service officials and said some had already been dismissed.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelensky has finally been asked on camera who 'Vova' is — the figure named on audio recordings in the Dynasty corruption case — and he declined to answer directly. In an interview with the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, published on November 26, he said: 'You can ask the anti-corruption institutions. They publicly said they have no questions for me. I think that is the answer.' Rainsford explained that Ukrainian colleagues had asked her to put the question, since no Ukrainian journalist had managed to ask the president about it in person. The Dynasty case centres on an organised group that investigators say laundered more than 460 million hryvnias (about $9 million) through the construction of luxury homes in the Kozyn cottage settlement; suspects named in May 2026 include former chief of staff Andriy Yermak, former deputy prime minister Oleksii Chernyshov and businessman Tymur Mindich, and the recordings are linked to the wider Energoatom 'Midas' investigation. NABU director Semen Kryvonos has said Zelensky does not and did not feature in the pre-trial investigation. Rainsford also pressed Zelensky on whether Ukraine is losing the war on corruption, citing cases involving drug cartels, a fugitive prosecutor general and suspicions against the president's close friends. 'Of course not,' he replied. 'We are fighting corruption, and that is why you know about it — because we are not trying to close our eyes to such challenges.' On the SAP's claim that the SBU is pressuring the anti-corruption bodies, Zelensky insisted NABU and SAP are independent institutions he cannot interfere with, while conceding that 'there are questions for some representatives of the special services' and that prosecutors' checks and investigations are under way, with some people already dismissed. The interview matters because it is Zelensky's first direct public response to the 'Vova' question — and because the pressure on NABU and SAP has become a test of whether Ukraine's anti-corruption system can survive wartime politics.

articles.title: Russia attacks Ukraine with 155 drones overnight; two killed, 23 injured as Izyum, Kharkiv and Vinnytsia are hit
articles.description: Russia attacked Ukraine overnight on November 26–27 with ballistic missiles and 155 drones, 83 of them jet-powered, Ukraine's Air Force said. Air defences shot down or suppressed 110 of the drones, but hits were recorded at 27 locations. Two people were killed and at least 23 injured, with Izyum in Kharkiv region, the city of Kharkiv itself, Dnipropetrovsk region and Vinnytsia region among the worst hit.
articles.body: Russia launched another mass overnight attack on Ukraine on the night of November 26–27, firing Iskander-M, Tsirkon and S-400 ballistic missiles alongside 155 Shahed-type attack drones — 83 of them jet-powered — plus Gerbera and Parodiya decoys, launched from seven directions including occupied Donetsk and Crimea. By 08:00 on November 27, Ukraine's Air Force said air defences had shot down or suppressed 110 of the drones, 51 of them jet-powered, but impacts were recorded at 27 locations and debris fell at four more. Two people were killed and at least 23 injured across Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia and Kirovohrad regions. In Izyum, in Kharkiv region, Russian forces launched a combined strike with multiple-launch rocket systems and drones: six people were injured, apartment blocks and private homes, administrative buildings, a municipal utility building and cars were damaged, and fires broke out in several parts of the city. In Kharkiv itself, morning drone strikes on the Shevchenkivskyi and Kyivskyi districts injured three people, and a petrol station in the Shevchenkivskyi district was hit; an 86-year-old woman was killed in the city. In Dnipropetrovsk region, Russian forces struck more than 20 times across five districts, killing one person and injuring at least two. In Vinnytsia region, energy and railway infrastructure were damaged, though no one was reported injured there. The night before, Russian strikes killed four people and injured 14 in Kharkiv region, Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk region — a reminder that the nightly toll is now measured in deaths almost every day, even as US-brokered talks approach.

articles.title: EU leaders end summit early with no deal on €45bn Ukraine loan or the 2028–2034 budget
articles.description: EU leaders ended their extraordinary summit in Brussels early, in the night of November 26–27, without agreeing either the €45 billion additional loan for Ukraine in 2027 or the bloc's long-term budget for 2028–2034. Twenty-four of the 27 member states backed the Commission's loan proposal — €25 billion for defence and €20 billion for the budget — but Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia refused, and Bulgaria would join only the non-military part. Both issues return to the European Council on December 17–18.
articles.body: European Union leaders have failed to agree on financing for Ukraine, ending their extraordinary summit in Brussels early in the night of November 26–27 with both big decisions postponed to December. Twenty-four of the 27 member states supported the European Commission's proposal for an additional €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027 — €25 billion for defence and €20 billion to support the state budget — but Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia refused to join, and Bulgaria said it would take part only in the non-military component, focused on regions where its national minority lives. European Council President António Costa confirmed the split at the closing press conference, saying leaders would return to the question at the next European Council on December 17–18. The leaders also failed to agree the EU's next seven-year budget for 2028–2034, in which the Commission proposes a dedicated €100 billion Ukraine Reserve; the budget needs unanimity, and Costa said it must be settled by the end of the year to take effect on January 1, 2028. The €45 billion would come on top of the €90 billion EU loan for 2026–2027 already agreed, and the delay is painful for Kyiv: the state is short more than 102 billion hryvnias for military pay by the end of the year, according to the Accounting Chamber. On the diplomatic side, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on November 26 that the Coalition of the Willing and the United States are united on Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine — but the summit's outcome shows that Europe's money, like its guarantees, still depends on persuading a handful of holdouts.

articles.title: Russian sabotage in Europe is intensifying and risks a mass-casualty event, IISS warns
articles.description: Russian-linked sabotage across Europe has risen 16% in the past year, with the use of arson and explosives nearly doubling, and a mass-casualty incident is now a real risk, the International Institute for Strategic Studies warns in a report published November 26. Germany and Poland, the countries whose logistics matter most for supplying Ukraine, account for more than half of the incidents recorded between October 2025 and September 2026. The report says Moscow is waging an 'unconventional war' on Europe through recruited proxies, aimed at raising the cost of supporting Kyiv.
articles.body: Alleged Russian-directed sabotage in Europe is intensifying, and a single attack could cause mass casualties, a new report from the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) warns. The report, 'Russia's Unconventional War on Europe: Sabotage, Deterrence, and Future Scenarios', published on November 26, finds sabotage operations rose 16% in the year to September 2026, while the use of arson and explosives nearly doubled. Poland suffered 24% of the incidents, Germany 20% and the Baltic states 20%; in Poland alone, 29 Moscow-linked incidents were recorded between October 2025 and September 2026, including a November 2025 explosive charge that damaged a rail line linking Warsaw to the Ukrainian border. The most targeted sectors were military-industrial sites (28% of targets), transport (22%) and energy (7%). The report says Russian intelligence services have recruited networks of proxies who are becoming more skilled, using 'more complex methods, including improvised explosive devices armed with timers and detonators', and that attacks come in surges across the continent, suggesting central planning in Moscow. The authors warn that 'a single operation that caused fatalities or prolonged disruption would generate demands for retaliation and likely expose divisions between European governments', and that 'sabotage has not yet achieved a strategic effect, but a mass-casualty incident is possible as the space for miscalculation narrows'. The report also sets out four scenarios for how the threat could develop by 2029, including in the event of a ceasefire in Ukraine. The warning comes the same week MI5 and the UK Ministry of Defence issued a joint alert about Kremlin proxies behind sabotage plots at European defence firms supplying Ukraine — and days after two Ukrainians were accused of railway sabotage in Poland on behalf of Russian intelligence.

articles.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange bodies of the fallen: 250 Ukrainian soldiers returned, 22 Russian
articles.description: Ukraine and Russia carried out another exchange of the bodies of fallen soldiers on November 26, at the Novaya Guta crossing on the Belarus–Ukraine border. Ukraine received the bodies of 250 people Russia says were Ukrainian soldiers; Russia received the remains of 22 of its soldiers. It is the first such exchange since October 22, when the ratio was 252 to 25 — a lopsided pattern that mirrors the casualty imbalance in the war.
articles.body: Ukraine has brought home the bodies of 250 fallen soldiers in the latest repatriation exchange with Russia, the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War announced on November 26. The exchange took place at the Novaya Guta crossing on the Belarus–Ukraine border, with Belarusian agency BelTA reporting the handover; Russia received the bodies and remains of 22 of its soldiers in return. The Ukrainian dead were recovered from the Kharkiv, Donetsk, Kherson, Zaporizhzhia and Kursk directions, and will now be taken to specialised state institutions, where forensic experts and investigators will work to identify each one — a process that can take months, since the Russian side's identifications are not always reliable. The previous exchange took place on October 22, when Ukraine received 252 bodies and returned 25; earlier in 2026, repatriations included 501 bodies in July and 1,000 in April. The lopsided ratios have become a grim, recurring feature of these exchanges, and they point in the same direction as Meduza and Mediazona's estimate this week of more than 720,000 Russian war dead: the human cost of the war is enormous on both sides, but the flow of bodies runs overwhelmingly one way. The exchange comes as work continues on the lists for a large prisoner-of-war swap: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russian and Ukrainian intelligence services are finalising them, and US envoy Jared Kushner has said the exchange should happen 'very soon, before the holidays'. Presidential chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov said in October that Ukraine has already recovered more than 26,000 bodies and remains through exchanges.

articles.title: Starlink and Starshield are back to normal in Ukrainian-held territory, Zelensky says — but not in occupied areas
articles.description: Starlink and its military version Starshield have returned to normal operation in territory controlled by Ukraine, President Zelensky said in his BBC interview, after the US sent 'positive signals' on the restrictions. But limits remain in Russian-occupied territory, where Ukrainian interceptor drones cannot pursue fast jet-powered Shaheds — often reaching them only once they are already over Ukrainian-held ground, too late to stop strikes on infrastructure and energy facilities.
articles.body: Starlink and Starshield communications have returned to normal in Ukrainian-controlled territory, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his BBC interview, published on November 26 — but restrictions remain in the Russian-occupied areas, and they are still costing Ukraine. 'We had more problems before, but the American side has sent some positive signals,' Zelensky said, adding that the systems are now functioning normally over territory controlled by Kyiv. The problem, he explained, is on the other side of the front line: Ukrainian interceptor drones cannot pursue jet-powered Shahed drones across occupied territory, because the satellite link cuts out there. 'We can do it on controlled territory, but often it is already too late. They strike our infrastructure, energy facilities and so on,' he said. The restrictions matter more than ever because Russia's drone campaign now leans heavily on jet-powered Shaheds — 83 of the 155 drones launched on the night of November 26–27 were jet-powered, flying at more than 450 km/h. When asked who imposed the limits, Zelensky said SpaceX implemented them on a technical level, but politically he did not know who decided: 'It is like ping-pong. We ask one side, they say it is the others; we ask the others, they say it is not them.' He had already reported renewed major disruptions to Starshield on November 12. Ukrainian drone units near the front have complained for weeks that the restrictions interfere with their operations, and a Ukrainian defence firm, Militech Group, has developed an LTE modem as a backup for controlling drones when Starlink drops out. The partial restoration is good news for Ukraine's communications — but the gap over occupied territory remains a hole in its air defence.

articles.title: UPDATE: Ubisoft denies forcing developers to use generative AI — but its statement dodges the key claim
articles.description: Ubisoft has responded to reports that it requires developers to use generative AI, saying it only encourages teams to explore the technology and that projects are not required to use it. But the statement does not directly address the original claim: that developers pitching new games must explain how they will use AI or justify leaving it out. Other reporting says developers are still being heavily pushed toward AI, with around $1.2 million a month spent on generative-AI tokens.
articles.body: Ubisoft has denied reports that the company requires its developers to use generative AI in game development, following a November 25 investigation by Vertical Slice citing employees who said teams pitching new games had to explain how AI would speed up development — or justify not using it. In its statement, Ubisoft said: 'We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work. This doesn't mean that projects are required to use generative AI. Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make.' What the company did not do is deny the pitch rule itself — that proposals without an AI answer are not approved — and sources say staff felt 'cornered', with management treating AI use as unavoidable and pushing it especially hard for early game demos. Insider Gaming's own Ubisoft sources say that while AI use is not formally mandatory, developers are being pushed to adopt it in various ways, causing friction inside studios; one developer said 'it's not forced, but it feels like we are heavily encouraged to use it.' One tool being pushed is Imaginarium, an internal fork of an existing generative AI model, and internal data reportedly shows Ubisoft spending about $1.2 million a month on generative-AI tokens, rising by a couple of hundred thousand each month. The response comes a week after Ubisoft spun off its AI-focused team into a subsidiary called Motherbrain, and CEO Yves Guillemot has called generative AI a revolution comparable to games moving to 3D. Staff told Vertical Slice morale is 'abysmal' amid a strict five-day return-to-office mandate and ongoing cost-cutting. The episode captures the industry's central AI argument: a tool pitched as optional, in a workplace where saying no carries a cost.

articles.title: Remedy: Quantum Break 2's fate rests entirely with Microsoft
articles.description: Ten years after Quantum Break, Remedy Entertainment says a sequel is not in development — and the decision is not theirs to make. The rights to the sci-fi action game belong to Microsoft, unlike Alan Wake, whose rights Remedy regained. Fans keep asking, but Remedy says it can neither greenlight a sequel nor a remaster on its own.
articles.body: Ten years after the release of Quantum Break, fans of the sci-fi action game keep asking about a sequel — and Remedy Entertainment has now answered again, reminding players that the decision rests entirely with Microsoft. Asked on social media whether Quantum Break 2 is in development, the Finnish studio replied: 'As far as we know, no. The rights to Quantum Break belong to Microsoft, and the decision on a sequel is also theirs. But we are very pleased to see how much love players continue to show our game even after so many years!' Unlike Alan Wake, whose rights Remedy eventually brought back under its own control, Quantum Break remains Microsoft intellectual property, so the studio cannot independently decide to make a second part or even a remaster. Windows Central journalist Jez Corden argues a Quantum Break return could fit well into Xbox's brand-strengthening strategy under Asha Sharma, noting that Remedy makes high-quality games without astronomical budgets — Control Resonant cost only around 50 million euros and paid for itself. Microsoft is also interested in developing its game franchises for film and TV, and Quantum Break was ahead of its time there, combining a traditional story-driven shooter with a full live-action series starring Hollywood actors. For now, though, Remedy is busy with the Max Payne 1 and 2 remakes in partnership with Rockstar Games, and Quantum Break 2 remains a fan wish rather than a plan.

articles.title: Disney confirms Avatar 4 release date — December 21, 2029
articles.description: Disney has officially put Avatar 4 on its theatrical release schedule, alongside the third Black Panther and Incredibles films, confirming the sequel is still coming despite director James Cameron's earlier doubts. Avatar 4 is set for December 21, 2029, with Avatar 5 following on December 19, 2031. Part of the fourth film was already shot years ago, and its story jumps about six years forward.
articles.body: Disney has officially included the fourth part of the Avatar science-fiction franchise in its schedule of upcoming theatrical releases, alongside the third films in the Black Panther and Incredibles series — a clear signal that Avatar 4 is definitely happening. That is especially notable given that director James Cameron had previously expressed uncertainty about returning to the franchise. The previous film, Avatar: Fire and Ash, grossed about $1.48 billion worldwide — far less than Avatar: The Way of Water's $2.32 billion — and the drop had fans nervous about the series' future. Cameron himself had admitted he might postpone his return to Pandora and make another film first, naming an adaptation of Joe Abercrombie's novel 'The Devils' and a film about the atomic bombing of Hiroshima among his options, and saying he wanted to find a way to cut the cost and time of making the sequels. But part of the material for the fourth film was shot long ago, during work on The Way of Water and Fire and Ash. The story of Avatar 4 jumps roughly six years forward, and Cameron filmed the pre-jump episodes early, while the actors playing Jake Sully and Neytiri's children were still the right age — Trinity Jo-Li Bliss, who plays Tuk, was only nine at the time. The premiere of Avatar 4 remains scheduled for December 21, 2029, with Avatar 5 set for December 19, 2031 — meaning fans still face a long wait on Pandora.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus Essential December 2026 games revealed: Tony Hawk's 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, Amnesia: The Bunker
articles.description: Sony has revealed December's PlayStation Plus Essential lineup: the skateboarding collection Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4, fighting game Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 and horror title Amnesia: The Bunker. All three will be available to download from December 1 to January 4. Sony warns some games may be unavailable in certain regions.
articles.body: Sony has announced the December lineup for subscribers of the basic PlayStation Plus Essential plan, and it mixes genres: a skateboarding compilation, a long-running anime fighter and a tense horror game. Next month subscribers will receive Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 (PS4, PS5), the Dragon Ball fighting game Xenoverse 2 (PS4, PS5) and the horror title Amnesia: The Bunker (PS4). All three projects will be available for download from December 1 to January 4, giving subscribers more than a month to claim them. The Tony Hawk collection is the headline act — a remake package of two of the most beloved skateboarding games ever made — while Xenoverse 2 keeps one of the longest-supported Dragon Ball games in circulation and Amnesia: The Bunker offers a darker, more claustrophobic counterpoint for the holidays. Sony cautions that some games may be unavailable in a number of regions. Until the switch, Essential subscribers can still add November's games to their library: the cooperative zombie action game Dead Island 2, the Tomb Raider IV–VI Remastered trilogy and the roguelike deck-builder Monster Train 2.

articles.title: Devil May Cry creator Hideki Kamiya wants to make a new Castlevania
articles.description: Hideki Kamiya, creator of Devil May Cry, Bayonetta and Okami, has publicly asked Konami to entrust his studio Clovers with a new Castlevania. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he said a Kamiya-led Castlevania could be 'something amazing' — though he admitted he is 'a bit busy' right now. He also pitched a new Star Fox for Nintendo and a King's Knight sequel for Square Enix.
articles.body: The creator of Devil May Cry, Bayonetta and Okami, Hideki Kamiya, has asked Konami to entrust his studio Clovers with the development of a new Castlevania. The game designer made the pitch in a video on his own YouTube channel, saying: 'Maybe we'll make a new GetsuFumaDen with Konami… And Castlevania! I would really love to take on Castlevania. We could make something amazing, so please entrust it to us. Although, I'm a bit busy right now.' Kamiya raised Castlevania while explaining how his work on the Okami sequel is organized: after that game's announcement, some players assumed he had returned to Capcom's staff, but in fact he is working on the sequel at the independent studio Clovers, which cooperates with Capcom and is open to offers from other publishers. In the same video he named other series he would like to work on, including a new Star Fox for Nintendo, a sequel to King's Knight for Square Enix and another Kinnikuman Muscle Tag Match for Bandai Namco. Given Kamiya's huge experience making fast-paced action games, his Castlevania could resemble the Castlevania: Lords of Shadow duology from MercurySteam — a big-budget, combat-driven take on the series. The latest entry in the series to date is Castlevania: Belmont's Curse. Whether Konami, which has revived several of its classic series in recent years, takes him up on the offer remains to be seen — but a public pitch from one of action gaming's most celebrated directors is hard to ignore.

articles.title: GTA VI tops Japan's physical chart as PS5 outsells Switch 2 for the week
articles.description: Grand Theft Auto VI has debuted at number one in Japan's physical sales chart, selling 200,000 boxed PS5 copies in its first four days, according to Famitsu. PlayStation 5 also outsold the Nintendo Switch 2 in weekly hardware sales. It is the latest record for a launch already crowned the biggest of the generation in the UK.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI has confidently taken first place in Japan's physical sales chart, adding another market to its record-breaking launch. According to Famitsu, Japanese players bought 200,000 boxed copies of Rockstar's new game for PlayStation 5 in its first four days — a strong result for a market where physical sales still matter and where Western open-world games have traditionally faced a tougher climb. The launch also lifted hardware: PlayStation 5 outsold the Nintendo Switch 2 in weekly console sales, a notable reversal given the Switch 2's dominance since its release. The Japanese figures follow the game's performance in the UK, where it posted the biggest launch of the generation in the physical retail chart despite its boxed edition being essentially a download code in a case. Together, the numbers underline the scale of a release that is dominating games, music and culture at once — its soundtrack alone has sent older songs surging on streaming. For Sony, the Japanese result is doubly welcome: its console is riding the GTA VI wave even in Nintendo's home market. The question now is how long the momentum lasts, with the holiday season and the game's online mode — not expected until next year — still to come.

articles.title: UPDATE: Thanksgiving nor'easter leaves nearly 1 million without power; Macy's parade moves to Saturday
articles.description: The Thanksgiving nor'easter peaked with nearly 1 million customers without power across the eastern US on Thursday evening, with gusts up to 70 mph toppling trees and power lines and more than 2,300 flights delayed. The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET — the first postponement in its history. The National Weather Service says the storm departs overnight into Friday, though some restorations could stretch into the weekend.
articles.body: The powerful coastal storm that raked the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day left more than 960,000 households and businesses without electricity at its peak on Thursday evening, according to PowerOutage.us, up from the 800,000 reported earlier in the day. Pennsylvania was worst hit with more than 224,000 outages, followed by Virginia with around 200,000, New Jersey with about 191,000 and Maryland with roughly 177,000, as gusts of up to 70 mph and saturated ground brought down trees and power lines. Air travel was heavily disrupted too, with FlightAware counting more than 2,300 flights delayed and 451 cancelled within, into or out of the US as of 8:30 p.m. Thursday, during one of the busiest travel periods of the year. Strong onshore winds combined with king tides caused significant coastal flooding, with near-record levels at Ocean City, Maryland. The most visible casualty of the storm was the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, postponed from Thursday to Saturday at 8:30 a.m. — the first time in the parade's century-long history that the whole event has been moved to another day, after forecasters warned sustained winds of 30–40 mph with gusts to 65 mph would make flying the giant balloons unsafe. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who will miss Saturday's parade for scheduled foot surgery, said Saturday should bring partly sunny skies and highs in the low 50s. Utilities warned some customers, especially in flooded coastal communities, may wait until Friday or later for power to return.

articles.title: US authorizes SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites for AI data centers in space
articles.description: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites in space for the creation of data centers critical to powering artificial intelligence. The authorization is on a scale far beyond anything in orbit today and would move a large part of the AI computing boom off the planet. It raises major questions about orbital congestion, astronomy and who governs the new space economy.
articles.body: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized Elon Musk's SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites in space for the creation of data centers critical to powering artificial intelligence, CNN reports. The scale of the authorization is extraordinary: it would dwarf the thousands of Starlink satellites already in orbit and effectively turn low Earth orbit into an industrial zone for AI computation. The logic behind putting data centers in space is that solar power is abundant and uninterrupted there, and that the heat and energy demands of AI — which are straining power grids on Earth — could be handled off-planet. But the plan also raises serious concerns: a million satellites would transform the night sky, complicate astronomy, multiply the risk of collisions and space debris, and test a regulatory system that was never designed for constellations of this size. The authorization is a landmark for Musk, whose SpaceX already dominates launches and satellite internet, and it signals that Washington is willing to let American companies industrialize orbit in the race for AI supremacy. What remains unclear is the timeline, the cost, and whether the technical and environmental challenges of running data centers in space can be solved at anything like this scale — and how other nations, astronomers and rival operators will respond.

articles.title: Could you send me some nude photos?': Soccer players accuse coach of abuse, urge FIFA to act
articles.description: Five Argentinian footballers have filed a complaint with FIFA against Diego Guacci, a former River Plate and Argentina women's national youth team coach, accusing him of sexual harassment, threats and psychological abuse. Florencia Mercau, 32, told CNN in her first public interview that Guacci texted her asking for nude photos less than a day after they met. The players are urging FIFA to act in what CNN calls a lightning-rod case for women's football.
articles.body: Five Argentinian footballers have filed a complaint with FIFA, soccer's international governing body, against Diego Guacci, the former River Plate and Argentinian women's national youth team coach, accusing him of inappropriate conduct including sexual harassment, threats and psychological abuse. Florencia Mercau, now 32, spoke to CNN in an exclusive interview — the first time she has publicly discussed the abuse she says she endured. She said that not even a day had gone by after meeting Guacci before he sent her a text addressing her as 'Flor' and saying, 'Could you send me some nude photos?' Mercau also survived a suicide attempt, and her decision to speak out is part of a collective complaint by the five players, who are calling on FIFA to take action against a coach who held power over young women's careers. The case is a lightning rod because it goes to the heart of safeguarding in women's football: a national youth-team coach accused of exploiting his authority over teenage and young players, in a system where speaking out can end a career. FIFA has faced repeated criticism over how it handles abuse complaints, and the players' decision to go to world football's governing body — rather than only to domestic authorities — is a demand that it use its power to ban abusers from the sport entirely. The complaint adds to a growing list of abuse scandals that have shaken women's football in recent years, from Spain to the United States to Argentina.

articles.title: Spain's Sánchez stood up against Trump. His own voters may be about to bring him down
articles.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez built an international reputation standing up to Donald Trump, but after eight years in power his own voters may be about to end his government. Corruption scandals around him, the migrant disaster in Ceuta, two catastrophic train crashes and a housing affordability crisis have left Spaniards exhausted. As voters prepare to cast ballots on Sunday, most polls have his center-left Socialists trailing the center-right People's Party.
articles.body: For much of the past few years, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has enjoyed the kind of international reputation that few politicians do — including for standing up to Donald Trump. But after eight years in power, the fatigue among Spaniards is palpable, and as voters prepare to cast their ballots on Sunday, most opinion polls have Sánchez and his center-left Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) trailing behind the center-right People's Party (PP). The problems piling up around him are formidable: corruption scandals embroiling those around him, the migrant disaster in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, two catastrophic train crashes, a housing affordability crisis, and an economy that, though booming on paper, continues not to deliver for ordinary people. The cost-of-living pressures are central to the discontent — growth figures that look strong in Madrid have not translated into affordable homes or easier household budgets. Sánchez's defiance of Trump won him admirers abroad, but at home it is domestic failures that voters will judge. A defeat on Sunday would end one of Europe's longest-serving center-left governments and hand power to the PP, reshaping Spain's politics and its relationship with Washington and Brussels. For Sánchez, the irony is sharp: the international standing that defined his recent years may not be enough to save him from the verdict of his own electorate.

articles.title: The case that illustrates how Trump's retribution campaign is falling short
articles.description: Few cases better exemplify the failure of President Trump's campaign to prosecute his perceived enemies than one against two former FBI officials, which a federal judge threw out within two weeks. An FBI agent testified the case was built at the president's behest, with FBI leadership listing potential charges and demanding constant updates. In his written order this week dismissing the case, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui ridiculed prosecutors for 'rampant errors and misstatements stemming from the slapdash nature of this investigation.'
articles.body: Few cases better exemplify the continued failure in prosecuting Trump's perceived enemies than one brought against former FBI officials in October. In two weeks, a federal judge tossed the charges after an FBI agent testified the case was built at the behest of the president, with FBI leadership listing potential charges and demanding constant updates from agents. In mid-October, two former FBI officials whose previous work focused on nefarious foreign influence were charged with making false statements to lawmakers in 2023, allegedly misleading members of Congress as to the extent of their knowledge of the FBI's investigation into Hunter Biden's laptop years earlier. The now-dismissed charges focused on statements the officials made about their knowledge of that investigation. In his written order released this week dismissing the case, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui ridiculed prosecutors for bringing a politically charged case with 'rampant errors and misstatements stemming from the slapdash nature of this investigation and prosecution.' The case matters because it is the clearest test yet of the administration's retribution agenda: prosecutions aimed at officials associated with investigations Trump regards as hostile to him. That a judge dismissed it so quickly — and on the basis of an FBI agent's own testimony about political direction — undercuts the claim that these are ordinary law-enforcement matters. For the White House, the defeat is both legal and political: the courts are proving a stubborn obstacle to using criminal prosecution as a weapon against perceived enemies.

articles.title: ElevenLabs in early talks to raise at $33B valuation — more than six times AI music rival Suno
articles.description: ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise new funding at a $33 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on November 25, citing people familiar with the matter. The round is planned for the first quarter of 2027, though some investors are pushing for it to start sooner. The figure would be 50% above the $22 billion valuation set by a $300 million employee tender in September — and more than six times the $5.4 billion valuation Suno reached in June.
articles.body: ElevenLabs, the London- and New York-headquartered AI audio company behind the ElevenMusic song generator, is in early talks to raise new funding at a $33 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, November 25, citing people familiar with the matter. The company plans to start the round in the first quarter of 2027, although some investors are pushing for it to begin sooner, and ElevenLabs has declined to comment. A $33 billion valuation would be 50% higher than the $22 billion mark set by a $300 million employee tender offer in September, and roughly triple the $11 billion valuation from its $500 million Series D in February, led by Sequoia Capital. The climb has been steep: ElevenLabs was valued at $1.1 billion at its Series B in January 2024, $3.3 billion at its Series C in January 2025, and $6.6 billion in a September 2025 employee share sale. Annual recurring revenue has reportedly reached $700 million, up from $600 million in September, with enterprise customers accounting for 55% of revenue. The comparison with Suno matters for music: Suno competes directly with ElevenMusic, but ElevenLabs' valuation would be more than six times Suno's $5.4 billion post-money valuation from its June Series D. Unlike Suno, which faces copyright lawsuits from labels and artists, ElevenLabs has built its music offering on licences — deals with Merlin and Kobalt were in place when ElevenMusic launched in August 2025, Believe has since signed on, and a multi-year agreement with Universal Music Group followed in September. CEO Mati Staniszewski has spoken of building toward an IPO, and a $33 billion raise would be the latest step on that path.

articles.title: Matador secures worldwide rights to Belle and Sebastian's complete catalog
articles.description: Matador Records has secured worldwide rights to the complete catalog of Glasgow indie band Belle and Sebastian, the Beggars Group label announced on Wednesday, November 25. Every title is held under licence, with rights split between Bella Figura Music and the band itself, and financial terms were not disclosed. The deal extends a relationship that began in 1998, when Matador first released the band's music in the US.
articles.body: Matador Records has secured worldwide rights to the complete catalog of Belle and Sebastian, the Beggars Group label announced on Wednesday, November 25. Every title covered by the deal is held under licence, with the rights split between Bella Figura Music and the band itself. The early Jeepster-era albums 'If You're Feeling Sinister' (1996) and 'The Boy With The Arab Strap' (1998), along with the four EPs collected on 'Push Barman To Open Old Wounds, Volume 1' (2005), are licensed from Bella Figura and will carry both the Bella Figura and Matador imprints. Four albums originally released under Rough Trade in specific territories — 'Dear Catastrophe Waitress' (2003), 'The Life Pursuit' (2006), 'Write About Love' (2010) and 'The Third Eye Centre' (2013) — are licensed directly from the band and will be branded Matador/Rough Trade worldwide. The remaining seven albums, from 1996's 'Tigermilk' through 2023's 'Late Developers', are licensed from the band under the Matador name alone. Financial terms were not disclosed. The deal extends a relationship that began in 1998, when Matador released 'The Boy With The Arab Strap' in North America, and Matador has handled the band's output globally since 2015. The first release under the new arrangement is a 30th anniversary edition of 'If You're Feeling Sinister', featuring unreleased songs and unheard demos from the era, out digitally on January 20, 2027, with a white-vinyl LP following on February 26. The band are currently on a world tour marking the 30th anniversaries of 'Tigermilk' and 'If You're Feeling Sinister', concluding at Glasgow Royal Concert Hall on December 21. Matador has been expanding its catalog representation in recent years, adding Pavement, Spoon, Alice Coltrane's 'Ashram Tapes', the pre-Capitol Butthole Surfers releases and pre-2026 Interpol albums, with further reissues and expanded editions to follow in 2027.

articles.title: Believe acquires catalog of Beijing indie Tianyue Huayin — its first catalog acquisition in Greater China
articles.description: Believe has acquired the catalog of China-based independent label Tianyue Huayin, marking the Paris-headquartered company's first catalog acquisition in Greater China, where it has operated since 2016. The deal covers the catalog only — Tianyue Huayin will remain an independent label — and its value was not disclosed. The Beijing indie claims a catalog of more than 20,000 tracks, including releases by Xiao Mi and Huang Wenwen.
articles.body: Believe has acquired the catalog of China-based independent label Tianyue Huayin, the Paris-headquartered company announced, in its first catalog acquisition in Greater China, where it has operated since 2016. A Believe representative confirmed to MBW that the deal covers Tianyue Huayin's catalog, not the company itself, and the label will remain independent. The value of the deal was not disclosed, nor were the precise rights involved. Tianyue Huayin claims to have released more than 20,000 tracks to date, including music by artists Xiao Mi and Huang Wenwen. Believe disclosed the deal as it marked 10 years in Greater China, framing it as a catalog acquisition partnership to begin its second decade in the region, and celebrated its 20th anniversary at an event in Xiamen on November 19. Believe Asia-Pacific president Sylvain Delange used a keynote at the event to discuss technology's role in the creative process. The company says other Greater China signings include Karen Mok, A Si, Dream Music Group, INDEcompany and Chizhao. The Tianyue Huayin deal is Believe's second ownership move in two days: on November 25 it completed its full acquisition of Lili Louise Musique, parent of French indie tôt Ou tard, eight years after buying its first 49% stake in 2018. Together the two deals show Believe buying catalogs on two fronts at once — consolidating at home in France while planting its first catalog flag in China.

articles.title: Universal, Warner and the BPI back charter to tackle barriers keeping people with dementia from accessing music
articles.description: Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group and UK record industry body the BPI have backed the Music Made Easy Charter, launched at the House of Lords in London on Tuesday, November 24, by the charity Music for Dementia and the University of Sheffield. The charter calls on the music and technology industries to remove the barriers that stop people living with dementia from enjoying personalised music. Signatories commit to taking at least one concrete action within 12 months.
articles.body: Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group and UK record industry body the BPI have backed a charter targeting the barriers that stop people living with dementia from accessing music. The Music Made Easy Charter was launched at the House of Lords in London on Tuesday, November 24, by the charity Music for Dementia and the University of Sheffield, with other backers including children's audio platform Yoto, music technology company MediMusic and UK trade body ERA. Signatories have committed to supporting the charter's principles and taking steps within their areas of influence, each invited to share at least one action taken within 12 months. Suggested actions include working with rights holders and streaming platforms to simplify licensing and account arrangements in care settings, developing simpler music-playing technology, involving people living with dementia in designing products and services, and raising awareness of the access problem. The need is stark: a Music for Dementia survey of 1,000 family caregivers, conducted in August 2024, found that only 3 in 10 older family caregivers are able to stream music with the person they care for, and Age UK research found around 6 in 10 internet users aged 65 and over never use the internet to stream music or video. Music for Dementia puts the number of people living with dementia in the UK at 940,000, projected to rise to 1.5 million by 2040. The charter draws on research by the University of Sheffield's Muses, Mind, Machine research centre and the BRIDGES for Dementia Network, and follows a year of work by the Music Made Easy Taskforce, which grew out of a roundtable at Yoto's London headquarters in November 2025 attended by around 20 senior representatives. The charity has also developed m4dRADIO, a free online radio station for people living with dementia. BPI diversity, equity and inclusion head Hailey Willington said music should be accessible to all and that working together could redefine what accessible music technology looks like, ensuring it serves everyone, not just digital natives.

articles.title: UPDATE: YouTube paid Warner Music Group over $1B last year, annual report shows — and WMG sold catalog rights to its Bain venture for $233M
articles.description: Warner Music Group's annual report, filed with the SEC on November 19, shows YouTube paid the company more than $1 billion in fiscal 2026 — the first time the platform's annual contribution has crossed that threshold. The filing also reveals WMG sold recorded music catalog rights to Beethoven, its 50/50 joint venture with Bain Capital, for $233 million in the January-to-March quarter. It is a follow-up to WMG's record quarterly results covered earlier this week, with new detail from the 10-K.
articles.body: Warner Music Group's annual report, filed with the SEC on November 19 and analysed by MBW founder Tim Ingham on November 23, adds fresh detail to the record fiscal 2026 results the company reported last week. By MBW's estimate, YouTube paid Warner more than $1 billion in the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 — the first time the platform's annual contribution to WMG has crossed that threshold. The 10-K names any customer accounting for 10% or more of total revenues: Spotify represented 21%, YouTube 14% and Apple 10%, meaning the three platforms jointly supplied approximately 45% of Warner's $7.437 billion in fiscal 2026 revenues. The filing also shows that in the January-to-March quarter, Warner sold recorded music catalog rights to Beethoven, its 50/50 venture with Bain Capital, for $233 million. Warner's headcount fell to approximately 4,700 worldwide as of September 30, 2026 — around 1,500 below the roughly 6,200 it employed at the end of September 2022, shortly before CEO Robert Kyncl took over. At the same time, the company is spending more on A&R, with artist and repertoire costs up 11% year-on-year. Recorded music subscription streaming revenues rose 12.4% at constant currency to $3.017 billion for the year, and Kyncl told investors on the earnings call that money from Warner's AI licensing deals is on its way, with a material revenue contribution expected in fiscal 2027. The picture is of a company more concentrated than ever on three giant platform customers, leaner on staff, and monetising both its catalog and its AI licences.

articles.title: Vevo spotlights four more 2027 Artists to Watch: AZ Chike, 54 Ultra, Barry B and FreshMula
articles.description: MBW is showcasing four more artists from Vevo's DSCVR Artists to Watch 2027 roster: AZ Chike, 54 Ultra, Barry B and FreshMula. The 2027 class is made up of 18 artists chosen from more than 600 submissions, each filming two exclusive live performances for Vevo. The spotlight continues MBW's partnership with Vevo around the annual list, which also named Sienna Spiro DSCVR Artist of the Year.
articles.body: MBW is showcasing four more artists from Vevo's DSCVR Artists to Watch 2027 roster — AZ Chike, 54 Ultra, Barry B and FreshMula — as part of its continuing partnership with Vevo around the annual list. AZ Chike, signed to Warner Records, made national noise on Kendrick Lamar's 'GNX' and spent the year linking with production heavyweights including Hit-Boy and Tyler, the Creator; Vevo's Mika Sunga praised his LA roots, massive co-signs and unmistakable delivery. 54 Ultra, on Interscope, draws from the past without being bound by it, pairing retro influences with textured production, and said growing up watching Vevo videos made the honour especially meaningful. Barry B, on Universal Music Spain, moves between genres while staying connected to his musical identity, turning music videos into story-led short films, and called his Vevo session in Brooklyn incredible. FreshMula, on Dischi Numero Uno/Sony Music Italy, fuses rap, jazz and soul with distinct African vibes, in a sound Vevo's Chiara Bonarrigo said crosses borders naturally. The full 2027 class is made up of 18 artists, each delivering two live performance videos shot exclusively for Vevo, with the campaign running across Vevo's network since Tuesday, November 10. Vevo also named UK singer-songwriter Sienna Spiro, a member of its 2026 class, as its DSCVR Artist of the Year. Major labels hold 16 of the 18 places on the list, with the remaining spots going to EMPIRE and Symphonic-backed acts. For the four spotlighted artists, the Vevo platform is a launchpad into 2027 — and for the industry, the list is an early map of who the majors are betting on next.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo drops official version of melancholy 'Miss This Christmas' on Amazon Music
articles.description: Olivia Rodrigo has released the official version of 'Miss This Christmas', a melancholy piano ballad, on Amazon Music. She debuted the song live at a Nashville concert earlier this week, and the studio version arrived on Thursday, November 27. It is a holiday heartbreak song rather than a festive singalong, in keeping with the mood of her recent album.
articles.body: Olivia Rodrigo has released the official version of 'Miss This Christmas' on Amazon Music, Rolling Stone reports. The singer debuted the melancholy piano ballad live at a Nashville concert earlier this week, and the studio version arrived on Thursday, November 27, as the holiday season gets under way. The song is a heartbreak ballad for the holidays rather than a cheerful Christmas standard — a lonely, reflective take on missing someone at the time of year when that absence is felt most. Its release caps a huge year for Rodrigo, whose album 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love' has spent weeks at or near the top of the Billboard 200, most recently slipping to No. 2 on the chart dated November 28. The Amazon Music release puts the song on a major streaming platform just as holiday music takes over the charts, with Mariah Carey, Wham! and Bobby Helms already surging into the Hot 100 top 10. Rodrigo has made a habit of dropping new versions and live recordings around her releases, and a stripped-back piano track suits both her voice and the song's mood. Whether 'Miss This Christmas' becomes a seasonal staple or a one-off curio, it gives her fans a new original for the holidays — and it arrives at the exact moment the charts turn festive.

articles.title: Watch Wu-Tang Clan perform 'Triumph' and 'Bring Da Ruckus' at NFL Thanksgiving halftime show
articles.description: Wu-Tang Clan performed 'Triumph' and 'Bring Da Ruckus' at the NFL's Thanksgiving halftime show on Thursday, November 26, joined on drums by Red Hot Chili Peppers' Chad Smith. The performance brought the Staten Island hip-hop legends to one of the biggest television audiences of the year. It comes weeks after the group were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class.
articles.body: Wu-Tang Clan performed 'Triumph' and 'Bring Da Ruckus' at the NFL's Thanksgiving halftime show on Thursday, November 26, Rolling Stone reports. The New York hip-hop group were joined on drums by Red Hot Chili Peppers' Chad Smith, adding a rock edge to the two classic tracks. The Thanksgiving halftime slot is one of the biggest television stages in American music, reaching a family audience that stretches far beyond hip-hop fans, and the choice of Wu-Tang for the performance underlined how fully the group has moved from street legend to national institution. It also capped a remarkable autumn for the Clan: they were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as part of the 2026 class, in a ceremony in Los Angeles that celebrated their influence across generations of hip-hop. 'Triumph', from 1997's 'Wu-Tang Forever', is one of the group's most celebrated posse cuts, while 'Bring Da Ruckus' opened their 1993 debut 'Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)' and remains a setlist staple more than three decades later. Smith's presence behind the kit was a cross-genre flourish in keeping with the night, which also saw U2 play Dolly Parton's final recording at the Thanksgiving Eve halftime show the night before. For Wu-Tang, the halftime show was another reminder that their catalog still commands the biggest stages in the country.

articles.title: Snoop Dogg teams up with Feid for Thanksgiving single 'Gracias x Todo'
articles.description: Snoop Dogg has teamed up with Colombian star Feid for a Thanksgiving single, 'Gracias x Todo', released on Thursday, November 26. The two musicians recently previewed the track during a performance at the Latin Grammy Awards. The title translates as 'thanks for everything', a fitting sentiment for a Thanksgiving release.
articles.body: Snoop Dogg has teamed up with Feid for a Thanksgiving single, 'Gracias x Todo', Rolling Stone reports. The track arrived on Thursday, November 26, with the two musicians having recently previewed it during a performance at the Latin Grammy Awards. The title translates from Spanish as 'thanks for everything', a deliberately seasonal sentiment for a song released on Thanksgiving Day. The collaboration pairs one of hip-hop's most enduring figures with one of Latin music's biggest current stars: Feid, the Colombian singer and rapper, has spent the past few years building a global audience, while Snoop continues to release music at a relentless pace across genres and generations. Previewing the song at the Latin Grammys gave it a high-profile launch in front of the Latin music world before its official release, and the Thanksgiving timing turns it into a holiday record as well as a collaboration. It is the kind of cross-genre, cross-language pairing that has become routine at the top of the charts, where Latin artists regularly feature on mainstream American releases and vice versa. For Feid, sharing a track with Snoop is another marker of his arrival as a global star; for Snoop, it is the latest in a long line of collaborations that keep him current with younger audiences. The song's gratitude theme makes it an easy fit for Thanksgiving playlists, and its Latin Grammy preview suggests both artists see it as more than a throwaway holiday one-off.

articles.title: Watch Miranda Lambert perform a medley of her hits at the Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving halftime show
articles.description: Miranda Lambert performed a medley of her hits at the Dallas Cowboys' Thanksgiving halftime show on Thursday, November 27, Rolling Stone reports. The Cowboys' annual Thanksgiving game is one of the NFL's biggest television events, and the halftime show is a showcase slot for a major country star. Lambert, a Texas native, was a natural fit for the Dallas stage.
articles.body: Miranda Lambert performed a medley of her hits at the Dallas Cowboys' Thanksgiving halftime show, Rolling Stone reports. The performance came during the Cowboys' annual Thanksgiving Day game on Thursday, November 27, one of the NFL's biggest television events of the regular season. The halftime show at the Cowboys' Thanksgiving game is a showcase slot, and Lambert — a Texas native and one of country music's biggest stars — was a natural fit for the Dallas stage. A medley format let her run through the highlights of a catalog that stretches back two decades, from her early breakout hits to her more recent work, in the short window a halftime show allows. The performance continued a Thanksgiving week full of music on NFL stages: U2 played Dolly Parton's final recording at the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday night, and Wu-Tang Clan performed at another Thanksgiving halftime show on Thursday with Red Hot Chili Peppers' Chad Smith on drums. For Lambert, the Cowboys stage is also a homecoming of sorts — she has long been associated with Texas country, and the Thanksgiving game is a Texas institution. The NFL has increasingly used its holiday games to stage music moments that reach well beyond sports fans, and Lambert's medley gave country music its turn in the spotlight on one of the year's most-watched broadcasts.

articles.title: Hejira' at 50: Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo and more honour Joni Mitchell's 1976 masterpiece
articles.description: Rolling Stone has marked the 50th anniversary of Joni Mitchell's 'Hejira' with a tribute featuring Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo and more, published on November 26. The 1976 album, a road-trip classic built around Mitchell's restless travel songs, is discussed by admirers including Jamie Lee Curtis, producer Nigel Godrich and Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold. Half a century on, the album's influence on songwriters remains undiminished.
articles.body: Rolling Stone has marked the 50th anniversary of Joni Mitchell's 'Hejira' with a tribute in which Beck, Cameron Crowe, Clairo and more honour the 1976 masterpiece, published on November 26. Jamie Lee Curtis, producer Nigel Godrich, Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold and others discuss the road-trip classic, an album built around Mitchell's restless travel songs and her collaboration with fretless bassist Jaco Pastorius. Released in 1976, 'Hejira' followed the commercial peak of 'Court and Spark' and the confessional intensity of 'Blue', and it found Mitchell writing long, wandering songs about highways, hotels and leaving — a record that was initially a modest seller but has grown in stature ever since. Its influence runs through generations of songwriters, from the artists in Rolling Stone's tribute to the indie and folk musicians who still cite it as a touchstone for ambitious, literary songwriting. The 50th anniversary is a reminder of how Mitchell's catalog keeps being rediscovered: 'Blue' and 'Court and Spark' get most of the attention, but 'Hejira' is the album her fellow musicians tend to name first. Beck, Crowe, Clairo, Curtis, Godrich and Pecknold each approach it from a different angle — as fans, collaborators and students of the record — and together they make the case for 'Hejira' as one of the great American road albums. For a record about never staying in one place, its fiftieth birthday finds it more settled in the canon than ever.

articles.title: Mary J. Blige's 'Real Love' did not infringe 'Impeach the President', appeals court rules
articles.description: An appeals court has ruled that Mary J. Blige's 'Real Love' did not infringe the copyright of 'Impeach the President', the 1973 Honey Drippers track whose drum break is one of the most sampled in hip-hop history, Rolling Stone reports. The ruling, reported on November 26, is a win for Blige and a significant decision in the long-running legal arguments over sampling and interpolation. 'Real Love' was Blige's breakout hit in 1992.
articles.body: An appeals court has ruled that Mary J. Blige's 'Real Love' did not infringe on 'Impeach the President', Rolling Stone reports. The decision, reported on November 26, concerns the 1973 Honey Drippers funk track, whose opening drum break is one of the most sampled pieces of music in history and a foundational sound of hip-hop. Blige's 'Real Love', released in 1992 as the second single from her debut album 'What's the 411?', was her breakout hit and helped define the hip-hop soul sound she became known for. The case turned on whether Blige's song unlawfully copied protected elements of the earlier track, and the appeals court's ruling in her favour closes off a claim that had hung over one of the most famous songs of the 1990s. The decision matters beyond Blige: disputes over sampling and interpolation have shaped how producers work for decades, and court rulings on where influence ends and infringement begins set the boundaries for everyone making sample-based music. 'Impeach the President' has been at the centre of that argument since the earliest days of hip-hop, sampled by countless artists, and a ruling that Blige's use did not cross the line is a notable data point for artists and labels. For Blige, whose career has spanned more than three decades since 'Real Love', the ruling removes a legal cloud from the song that made her a star.

articles.title: Anuel AA releases 23-track 'RHLM2' album on his 34th birthday
articles.description: Puerto Rican rapper Anuel AA has released his long-awaited album 'RHLM2', a 23-track follow-up to his 2018 debut 'Real Hasta La Muerte', Billboard reports. The album arrived on Thursday, November 26, coinciding with the artist's 34th birthday and the US Thanksgiving holiday. It blends Latin trap and reggaeton and represents his first full-length album in four years.
articles.body: Puerto Rican rapper Anuel AA has released his long-awaited album 'RHLM2', a 23-track follow-up to his 2018 debut 'Real Hasta La Muerte', Billboard reports. The album arrived on Thursday, November 26, coinciding with the artist's 34th birthday and the US Thanksgiving holiday, and he described the project as a deeply personal return to the music that established his career. Billboard describes it as his first full-length album in four years, following a period in which the artist focused on family life and other projects. The project blends Latin trap and reggaeton across its 23 tracks and features collaborations with De La Rose, ROA and Fuerza Regida, as well as Blessd and Wisin. Billboard highlighted the track 'Instagram', which pairs Anuel AA with Blessd and Wisin and incorporates a sample of Don Omar's 2006 song 'Myspace'. The release also includes several previously issued songs, including 'Amanece', 'Más Rica Que Ayer', '¿Qué Nos Pasó?', 'La Llevo al Cielo' and 'Deportivo'. 'RHLM2' is a sequel to 'Real Hasta La Muerte', which debuted at No. 1 on Billboard's Top Latin Albums chart in July 2018. The release was first discussed during Billboard Latin Music Week in October, when he also teased a separate corridos project planned for later in the year. Anuel AA dedicated the project to his family and supporters who remained with him through difficult and successful periods, framing the album as a homecoming to the sound that made him a star.

articles.title: GTA VI: The Album' deluxe adds 23 new songs as the soundtrack chases the Billboard 200
articles.description: Atlantic Records and Rockstar Games have added a deluxe edition of 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album', with 23 new original songs taking the project to 57 tracks in total. The deluxe edition arrived on Monday, November 23, three days after the original 34-track album debuted alongside the game. Billboard reports the project is aiming to become the first video game soundtrack to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
articles.body: Atlantic Records and Rockstar Games added a deluxe edition of 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' on Monday, November 23, 2026, pushing the project to 57 tracks in total. The deluxe edition adds 23 original songs to the 34-track original, which reached listeners on November 20 alongside the game itself, and together the two editions form a 57-song collection. Billboard reports the project is aiming to become the first video game soundtrack to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200 chart. Travis Scott opens the added disc with 'Burn This Sh*t Down', a track that plays over the climactic final mission of the game's cinematic first chapter, and he had already contributed the pre-release single 'RHYNO'. Slayyyter follows with 'internet $tar', while The Dare, Anitta, Offset, 21 Savage, Pooh Shiesty, Young Nudy and SoFaygo all contribute solo cuts; Latto appears with Flo Milli on '50 Bands', Kodak Black teams with Michaël Brun on 'Tèt Kale Bobis', and Denzel Curry brings 454 on 'FLA Flow'. The original album already featured Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, JENNIE, Playboi Carti, Morgan Wallen, Keith Richards, Tove Lo, Kali Uchis and Young Thug, and the game itself carries more than 800 songs across 23 radio stations, several hosted by artists including Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, Trina, Trick Daddy, PinkPantheress, Burna Boy and Robyn. Three songs from the album have already reached the Hot 100: Morgan Wallen's 'Last Thing You Need' peaked at No. 9, Travis Scott's 'RHYNO' reached No. 84, and Justice's 'Flower in a Hurricane' — featuring King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, Tame Impala and SZA — debuted at No. 62, giving King Gizzard their first Hot 100 entry. Rockstar also announced a standalone score album, 'Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score', collecting 30 Justice tracks for release on December 11. Whether the album tops the Billboard 200 will show how much of the game's record launch came with a genuine music hit attached.

articles.title: DJ Goja takes 'Mi Chico' to No. 1 on Billboard's U.S. Afrobeats Songs chart
articles.description: DJ Goja has taken 'Mi Chico' to No. 1 on Billboard's U.S. Afrobeats Songs chart for the week of November 28, 2026. The chart credits DJ Goja, Jason Derulo and Melody as the artists on the track, with DJ Goja, Jason Derulo and E.Siakas listed as producers. It is the latest sign of Afrobeats' continued crossover into the American mainstream.
articles.body: DJ Goja has taken 'Mi Chico' to No. 1 on Billboard's U.S. Afrobeats Songs chart for the week of November 28, 2026. Billboard's chart page places the song at No. 1 with a peak position of No. 1, crediting DJ Goja, Jason Derulo and Melody as the artists on the track. The same page identifies DJ Goja, Jason Derulo and E.Siakas as producers, while O.M. Goja, J.J. Desrouleaux and S. Charles receive songwriting credits. The chart-topper pairs DJ Goja, a Romanian producer and DJ who has built a global following with Afrobeats-inflected dance records, with Jason Derulo, the American pop star, and Melody, the Spanish singer. 'Mi Chico' has been climbing the Afrobeats chart in recent weeks as the sound continues its crossover into the American mainstream, with Afrobeats acts and collaborations regularly appearing on Billboard's US charts. The No. 1 follows a run of Afrobeats hits that have moved from clubs and streaming playlists into the upper reaches of Billboard's genre rankings. For DJ Goja, the chart-topper is a career milestone, putting a Romanian DJ at the top of an American Afrobeats chart alongside two established pop names. For the genre, it is another marker of how thoroughly Afrobeats has become part of the global pop landscape rather than a niche sound.

articles.title: Karol G's 'BbY WOW' extends its Hot Latin Songs reign to a 14th week at No. 1
articles.description: Karol G's 'BbY WOW' extends its reign at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart for a 14th week, on the chart dated November 28, 2026. Behind it, Bad Bunny's 'DTMF' holds at No. 2 and Fuerza Regida's 'Suzuki' races to No. 3. The countdown also sees 'Te Estoy Correteando' lift to No. 5 and Bulin 47 and Kevin Wai launch at No. 10.
articles.body: Karol G's 'BbY WOW' extends its reign at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs chart for a 14th week, on the chart dated November 28, 2026. The Colombian star's hit continues to dominate the Latin songs ranking, having already topped Billboard's Global 200 for seven weeks earlier in the autumn. Behind it, Bad Bunny's 'DTMF' is parked at No. 2, and Fuerza Regida's 'Suzuki' continues to climb, racing to No. 3. 'Te Estoy Correteando' lifts to No. 5, while 'Ayúdame' slips to No. 4 and a Karol G and Drake collaboration drifts to No. 6. Omar Courtz commands No. 7, Carín León's 'Olimpo' is strong at No. 8, and Carín León also holds the line at No. 9, with Bulin 47 and Kevin Wai launching the countdown at No. 10. The top 10 shows the breadth of Latin music's current moment: established superstars in Karol G and Bad Bunny, the música mexicana wave led by Fuerza Regida, and newer names breaking into the countdown. 'BbY WOW' has now spent more than three months at the top of the Hot Latin Songs chart, a run that puts it among the longest-leading Latin hits of the year. With the holiday season under way and new releases still landing, the question is how much longer Karol G can hold off 'Suzuki' and 'DTMF' — but for now, the chart belongs to her.

articles.title: Billboard 200 top 10: Olivia Rodrigo slips to No. 2 as Noah Kahan climbs and Lil Baby tumbles
articles.description: Olivia Rodrigo's 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love' falls to No. 2 on the Billboard 200 dated November 28, earning 62,000 equivalent album units, after ATEEZ's 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' took the top spot. Noah Kahan's 'The Great Divide' rises a spot to No. 5 on 47,000 units, up 8%, while Lil Baby's 'FRESH' falls from No. 2 to No. 10 on 31,000 units, down 47%. Morgan Wallen's 'I'm the Problem' holds at No. 3.
articles.body: Olivia Rodrigo's 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love' falls to No. 2 on the Billboard 200 dated November 28, earning 62,000 equivalent album units in the week ending November 19, down 1%, after ATEEZ's 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' debuted at No. 1. Rodrigo's album had held the top spot for a fifth nonconsecutive week on the chart dated November 21, the longest run at No. 1 in 2026 among 2026 releases, passing Drake's four weeks with 'ICEMAN'. Morgan Wallen's 'I'm the Problem' is a non-mover at No. 3 with a little more than 49,000 units, up less than 1%, while U2's 'Carnaval de Luz' debuts at No. 4 with 49,000 units. Noah Kahan's 'The Great Divide' rises a spot to No. 5 on 47,000 equivalent album units, up 8%, and his 'Stick Season' is steady at No. 7 on 36,000 units, up 2%. Ella Langley's 'Dandelion' is pushed down to No. 6 on 45,000 units, up 2%, even as her single 'Choosin' Texas' extends its record 29-week run atop the Hot 100. SZA's 'SOS' steps up to No. 8 on 32,000 units, up 6%, while Olivia Dean's 'The Art of Loving' slips a spot to No. 9 on 32,000 units, down less than 1%. Rounding out the top 10, Lil Baby's 'FRESH' falls from No. 2 to No. 10 on 31,000 units, down 47%, a week after debuting with 59,000 units despite out-streaming Rodrigo. The chart, compiled by Luminate, shows a top 10 in transition as holiday music climbs the Hot 100 and the year's biggest albums jostle for position heading into December.

articles.title: Meet Chuyín, Billboard's Latin Up-and-Comer of November — masked música mexicana star plots first headlining tour for 2027
articles.description: Billboard has named Chuyín its Latin Up-and-Comer Artist of the Month for November, profiling the masked música mexicana breakout star. His 16-track debut album 'Los Locos Nunca Mueren' arrived in May via Street Mob Records, and his single 'Pues Qué Le Hago?' gave him his first Billboard No. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay in September. He tells Billboard he is working on a sophomore album and will embark on his first headlining tour in 2027.
articles.body: Billboard has named Chuyín its Latin Up-and-Comer Artist of the Month for November, profiling the masked música mexicana breakout star in a feature published on November 26. Chuyín is three years old — or 21, if you count in dog years, as he does — and already making his mark on música mexicana. His 16-track debut album, 'Los Locos Nunca Mueren' (Crazy People Never Die), was released May 7 via Street Mob Records, debuting at No. 9 on the Top Regional Mexican Albums chart and No. 17 on Top Latin Albums, both dated May 23. In September, 'Pues Qué Le Hago?' gave him his first No. 1 on a Billboard chart, topping Regional Mexican Airplay. At the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards last month, a mob of Chuyíns in white straitjackets turned the stage into a psychiatric ward during a performance of 'Pues Ya Ni Pedo', with the closing gag revealing members of Fuerza Regida beneath the oversized masks. On the album, which features Fuerza Regida, Calle 24, Luis R Conriquez, Óscar Maydon and Jorsshh, Chuyín takes on the carnal pleasures and intoxicating excesses common to contemporary corridos — then gives them a comedic twist. 'Everyone sings about the neverending party. I sing about the hangover,' he tells Billboard. Born in Tepic, Nayarit, Mexico, and raised in Rancho Cucamonga, California, he insists that, asked about the person behind the mask, 'I'm Chuyín.' His recommended song is 'Olvídate de Mí', a candid account of romantic self-sabotage he says he penned entirely on his own. What is next: Chuyín is working on his sophomore album and exclusively reveals to Billboard that he will embark on his first headlining tour in 2027, with further details to be announced soon.

articles.title: The Mastermind
articles.author: May Jeong
articles.description: The most talked-about magazine profile of the week: a year of reporting and more than 100 interviews about the world's biggest pop star, written as a fairy tale that never once uses her name — and a case study in how celebrity power actually works.
articles.body:
Vanity Fair's profile of Taylor Swift — published November 23, 2026 and written by May Jeong after more than 100 interviews — never names its subject. Instead it calls her "The Star" and tells her story twice, as the two sides of a record. The A side is the familiar legend: a child born in 1989 grows up on a Christmas tree farm south of Reading, Pennsylvania, plays Sandy in Grease and Maria in The Sound of Music, learns guitar from a computer repairman until her 12-year-old fingers bleed, and signs with a newly opened Nashville label at 15. She becomes a generational talent, survives a bad breakup over a 27-second phone call, and when the Nashville label sells her life's work to her archnemesis's manager, she appeals to her fans, wins her music back, and meets her shining knight.

The B side retells the same life with the gloss stripped off. The Christmas tree farm is 11 acres bought by a third-generation banker father who managed a portfolio of around $270 million at Merrill Lynch. At 10 the family moves into a 3,560-square-foot Georgian Colonial in Wyomissing that a visitor calls a "six-star hotel." Her mother, described by one neighbor as "definitely a theater mom, very aggressive," pushes the guitar lessons — when the teacher reports the girl complains the chords hurt her hands, the parents reply, "Just keep working her. She needs this to get better." Her father films her early performances, drives her to gigs, and hands out tickets to business associates, asking them to cheer loudly so she always seems to play to a full house.

What emerges from interviews with neighbors, classmates, teachers, lovers, scholars, critics and music executives, Jeong writes, is that the Star's most enduring identity is "not musician, not artist, not celebrity, but a combination of victim and victimizer." Former classmates push back on her famous story of being bullied at school: Chanice Skinner, who sat beside her in music class, recalls her as "always part of the popular crowd" and says, "If you weren't part of her friend group, you didn't exist to her." Arielle Peppers remembers the Star arriving at school in Ugg boots — brown, black and blue — while her own single mother, working at a bakery, a dairy mill and as a caretaker, told her one pair cost half a paycheck. The piece revisits the 2019 sale of her masters — her father had invested a reported $500,000 in the Nashville label and made $15 million when it sold — her Tumblr post accusing the new owner of "incessant, manipulative bullying," the death threats her fans sent him, and her unprecedented feat of re-recording her albums to buy the originals back.

The profile works through her feuds in code: "The Brat" is Charli XCX, who sang about her insecurities next to the world's biggest pop star and was then, the piece argues, quietly frozen out; "The Protégé" is Olivia Rodrigo, whose falling-out followed a delayed songwriting credit; "The California Girl" is Katy Perry. One unnamed music executive calls her "truly Regina George," and another source, "The Person Familiar," says, "If you don't see it her way, she comes after you." A music critic who panned her found her friends — professional musicians who had credited the critic for their early success — shunning her, and her roommate asking her to move out.

The piece closes with her wedding to Travis Kelce — "Redwood" — at Madison Square Garden in the summer of 2026, during a heat wave, with 1,000 guests, a $26 million charitable donation beforehand, and a raffle in which one guest reportedly won a Chanel bag and another a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle. Jeong sets the $26 million against her fortune — $1.6 billion in fall 2025, over $2 billion by the time the issue goes to press, "or the GDP of Eritrea" — and notes it works out to roughly what a New Yorker on the median household income of $81,228 would give if they donated $1,055. Hidden in the text, 19 bolded capital letters spell out "Look What You Made Me Do." The final turn is philosophical: stars function as mirrors, cultural theorist Stuart Hall observed, and in a secular age we turn to singers for the community and meaning churches once provided. "The Star's version was used in the making of this article."

articles.title: My Apology to American Democracy
articles.author: George Packer
articles.description: A striking piece of public self-correction from a writer who warned America was becoming an authoritarian state: after the November 3 midterms, Packer explains what he got wrong — and why the threat still isn't over.
articles.body:
After any election, George Packer writes, it is natural to hunt for results that prove you were right all along — and after the Democrats' remarkable new majority in the November 3, 2026 midterms, every faction is doing exactly that. Supporters of Medicare for All point to Abdul El-Sayed's win in Michigan; skeptics point to Roy Cooper's blowout in North Carolina; those who want to retire the culture war point to Gina Hinojosa and James Talarico in Texas. But Packer argues it is more useful to search for what you got wrong, because views exploded by events have a way of disappearing from the mind, leaving the illusion that your wishes always matched reality.

A year earlier, Packer had written that America was becoming an authoritarian state, in a piece titled "America's Zombie Democracy." There were grounds for it: President Trump ruled with almost no checks, the Supreme Court offered little resistance and Congress none, the civil service had been gutted, independent agencies neutered, and the Justice Department warped into a tool for rewarding friends and punishing enemies.
