articles.description: Carly Rae Jepsen's 'Run Away With Me' has seen a 288 percent streaming bump thanks to 'GTA VI', as the game's soundtrack rollout sends listeners back to the 2015 pop classic. It is the latest sign of the game's enormous cultural reach before its release.
articles.body: Carly Rae Jepsen's 'Run Away With Me' has seen a 288 percent jump in streams thanks to 'GTA VI', as the game's soundtrack rollout sends a new generation of listeners back to the 2015 pop classic. The song, from Jepsen's beloved album Emotion, has become a fan favourite over the years, but the GTA VI connection has given it a second life — the kind of sync effect that can turn a decade-old track into a chart story overnight. It is the latest evidence of the game's cultural gravity: with its release set for November 19 and a Miami music event featuring Travis Scott and Cardi B, GTA VI is dominating not just gaming but music, film and fashion. The soundtrack is even getting a big physical media rollout, a rarity in the streaming era. For Jepsen, the bump is a reminder that a great pop song never really dies — it just waits for the right moment to come back.

articles.title: Jimmy Kimmel criticizes Trump's 'fishy' support of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.description: Jimmy Kimmel has criticised Donald Trump's 'fishy' support of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after the president reinstated the chip boss following a spy-sex scandal. The late-night host's jabs land as tech stocks seesaw on AI fears.
articles.body: Jimmy Kimmel has criticised Donald Trump's 'fishy' support of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after the president reinstated the chip boss following what Rolling Stone calls a spy-sex scandal. The late-night host's monologue lands in a week when Nvidia and the wider AI trade have been whipsawing, with tech stocks seesawing as AI fears overshadow Huang's return. Kimmel has made Trump a nightly target for years, and the Huang story gives him rich material: a president publicly backing a CEO whose company sits at the centre of the AI boom, in circumstances Kimmel finds suspicious. The joke also touches a real question — how close the White House is to the chip industry that powers the AI race, and what that closeness is worth. For viewers, it is Kimmel doing what he does best: turning a business story into a punchline that sticks.

articles.title: Hollywood heavyweights urge Dems to dump Schumer
articles.description: Hollywood heavyweights are urging Democrats to dump Chuck Schumer as Senate leader, in the latest sign of the party's internal tensions. The push from entertainment industry figures adds celebrity weight to a leadership fight that has been simmering for months.
articles.body: Hollywood heavyweights are urging Democrats to dump Chuck Schumer, adding celebrity firepower to the party's internal fight over its Senate leadership. The push from entertainment industry figures — donors, producers and stars who have long bankrolled the party — is a sign of how deep the frustration runs with Schumer's leadership, and how willing the party's cultural wing has become to say so in public. The Democratic Party has been arguing with itself for months over strategy, messaging and leadership, and Hollywood's intervention turns an inside-Washington debate into a public one. For Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for years, the pressure from donors who fund the party's campaigns is hard to ignore, even if the decision ultimately rests with his colleagues. For the party, the episode is another reminder that its coalition — from Hollywood to the Rust Belt — is pulling in different directions, and that the leadership question is not going away.

articles.title: Mariah Carey and Wham! holiday classics storm back into the Hot 100 top five
articles.description: Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' has jumped back into the Hot 100's top five, with Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' right behind it, as holiday streaming takes over in late November. The seasonal surge is arriving earlier and stronger than ever.
articles.body: Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' has jingled back into the Hot 100's top five, jumping from No. 18 to No. 4, while Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' leapt from No. 14 to No. 5 — and both are driven almost entirely by streaming. It is the first time Carey's song has ranked in the Hot 100's top bracket on a chart dated in November, a sign of how early the holiday season now starts on streaming. The surge is not limited to the two giants: Bobby Helms' 'Jingle Bell Rock' jumped up the chart on streaming, and a string of other Christmas songs entered the Hot 100 in the same week. The pattern is familiar — every year the holiday catalogue swallows the chart — but it keeps arriving earlier, fuelled by playlists and by listeners who treat November as the start of Christmas. For the artists chasing a No. 1 in the final weeks of the year, the message is clear: the holidays are coming, and they will own the chart until January.

articles.title: UPDATE: ATEEZ debut on the Hot 100 with 'UP' alongside fourth Billboard 200 No. 1
articles.description: UPDATE: ATEEZ have debuted on the Hot 100 with their title track 'UP' at No. 90, alongside topping the Billboard 200 with 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' — their fourth No. 1 album. The K-pop group are now charting on both of Billboard's main charts at once.
articles.body: UPDATE: ATEEZ have added a Hot 100 debut to their Billboard 200 triumph, with the title track 'UP' entering the main singles chart at No. 90 as 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' tops the albums chart — the group's fourth career No. 1 on the Billboard 200. The simultaneous entries on Billboard's two main charts are a measure of how far the group has come: a K-pop act that once seemed like a niche concern is now a regular at the top of the American charts. The group said they were 'sincerely happy and honored' to have entered the Hot 100 as well as earning their fourth Billboard 200 No. 1. The feat also reflects the wider strength of K-pop on this week's charts, with KATSEYE, BTS, Stray Kids and rookie LNGSHOT all placing on the Billboard 200, and JENNIE's 'Dracula' holding at No. 3 on the Hot 100. For ATEEZ, the double is the latest step in a rise that has been built on relentless touring and a fiercely loyal fanbase.

articles.title: JENNIE's 'Dracula' with Tame Impala holds at No. 3 on the Hot 100
articles.description: JENNIE's 'Dracula', her collaboration with Tame Impala, has held at No. 3 on the Hot 100, matching its career high for a second consecutive week. The BLACKPINK star's solo run continues to defy expectations.
articles.body: JENNIE's 'Dracula', her collaboration with Australian rock band Tame Impala, has held at No. 3 on the Hot 100, matching its career high for a second consecutive week. The track's staying power is a testament to JENNIE's strength as a solo artist: the BLACKPINK member has firmly established herself as a global solo star, and 'Dracula' has the radio stability to hold its position even as holiday songs flood the chart. The Tame Impala connection adds a rock dimension to the song that has helped it cross over, and it keeps Kevin Parker in the charts conversation in a week when Seal covered Tame Impala's 'New Person, Same Old Mistakes'. For JENNIE, the second week at No. 3 confirms that her solo career is not a side project but a major chart force in its own right — and with the Hot 100's top 10 in flux, a push higher is not out of the question.

articles.title: KATSEYE's 'WILD' surges 14 spots to No. 39 on the Billboard 200
articles.description: KATSEYE's 'WILD' has surged 14 spots to No. 39 on the Billboard 200, in a strong week for the HYBE-Geffen global girl group. Their single 'Animal' sits at No. 38 on the Hot 100.
articles.body: KATSEYE's 'WILD' has surged 14 spots from the previous week to rank at No. 39 on the Billboard 200, in a strong week for the global girl group formed through the partnership between HYBE and Geffen Records. The jump is one of the biggest moves on this week's albums chart, and it comes as the group's single 'Animal' holds at No. 38 on the Hot 100. KATSEYE's rise reflects the HYBE-Geffen experiment working: a group built for a global audience, with members from around the world, finding traction in the American market. The surge also underlines how broad K-pop's footprint on the Billboard 200 has become this week, with ATEEZ at No. 1, the K-pop Demon Hunters soundtrack at No. 44, BTS's 'ARIRANG' at No. 73, Stray Kids at No. 105 and rookie LNGSHOT debuting at No. 118. For KATSEYE, the momentum suggests the group is moving from promising newcomer to established chart act.

articles.title: Rookie LNGSHOT debuts on the Billboard 200 at No. 118
articles.description: Rookie boy group LNGSHOT, produced by singer-producer Jay Park, have made their first entry on the Billboard 200, with their mini album 'S.W.I.S.H.' ranking at No. 118. It is the group's first appearance on Billboard's main album chart since debuting.
articles.body: Rookie boy group LNGSHOT, produced by singer and producer Jay Park, have made their first entry on the Billboard 200, with their mini album 'S.W.I.S.H.' ranking at No. 118. The debut is a milestone for a group that only recently launched: cracking the Billboard 200 at all is a rare achievement for a new act, and it puts LNGSHOT on the map in the American market. The group are part of a wider wave of K-pop acts charting this week, from ATEEZ's No. 1 to KATSEYE's surge and BTS's 'ARIRANG' at No. 73. For Jay Park, the producer behind the group, the debut is vindication of a bet on a new generation of K-pop idols. For LNGSHOT, the challenge now is to turn a first chart entry into a career — and the Billboard 200 is a strong place to start.

articles.title: K-pop Demon Hunters soundtrack holds at No. 44 as BTS and Stray Kids chart
articles.description: The soundtrack to the hit animated film 'K-pop Demon Hunters' has landed at No. 44 on the Billboard 200, while BTS's 'ARIRANG' sits at No. 73 and Stray Kids' 'This & That' at No. 105. The animated film's music keeps finding new listeners months after release.
articles.body: The soundtrack album for the hit animated film 'K-pop Demon Hunters' has landed at No. 44 on the Billboard 200, holding its place in a week dominated by K-pop acts. BTS's 'ARIRANG' sits at No. 73 and Stray Kids' 'This & That' at No. 105, in a chart where K-pop's presence stretches from ATEEZ at No. 1 through KATSEYE, P1Harmony and rookie LNGSHOT. The 'K-pop Demon Hunters' soundtrack has been one of the year's surprise music stories: a film soundtrack that became a streaming phenomenon in its own right, introducing a new audience to K-pop sounds. Its staying power on the Billboard 200, months after the film's release, shows that the audience has not moved on. For the industry, the film is a case study in how animation, streaming and K-pop can combine into a chart force that outlasts a normal album cycle.

articles.title: Kremlin dismisses estimate of 720,000 Russian war dead, tells public to trust Defense Ministry figures
articles.description: The Kremlin has dismissed a Meduza and Mediazona estimate that more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war in Ukraine, telling the public to trust only Defense Ministry numbers. The estimate, based on leaked Rosstat data analyzed over two weeks, put the real death toll above 720,000 once delayed registrations and soldiers listed as missing are counted. It matters because it is the first official reaction to the most detailed independent Russian death toll yet — a figure larger than the number of U.S. soldiers lost in World War II.
articles.body: Journalists from Meduza and Mediazona spent more than two weeks studying data from Russia's Rosstat statistics agency, obtained after the system was hacked by the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and the Ukrainian group SilentCrow. The leaked records show more than 490,000 deaths registered since the full-scale invasion began, but many losses are recorded with long delays and some missing soldiers are only later declared dead; adjusting for those factors, the journalists estimate the true toll is above 700,000 and possibly already past 720,000. That is more than the United States lost in World War II, and more than the number of boys born in Russia in a single year. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded by urging the public to rely solely on the Defense Ministry, which has never published an overall death toll. The estimate, if accurate, would underline the scale of Russia's manpower losses nearly five years into the full-scale war, and the political sensitivity of acknowledging them at home.

articles.title: Poland proposes NATO consider shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine headed toward alliance territory
articles.description: Poland has proposed that NATO consider shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine when they are headed toward alliance territory, Bloomberg reported. The idea follows three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles falling in Poland during Russia's mass attack on November 20. It matters because it would mark a major expansion of NATO's role in the war — but Poland's own deputy defense minister has since signaled the alliance does not back the idea.
articles.body: The proposal comes after Russia's large-scale attack on Ukraine on November 20, during which three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles crossed into Polish airspace and fell on Polish territory, prompting Warsaw to summon the Russian ambassador and consult with NATO allies. Poland is now floating the idea that allied air defenses could intercept Russian missiles while they are still over Ukraine, if their trajectory threatens NATO territory. Such a step would go well beyond NATO's current posture of defending only its own airspace and would risk direct engagement between alliance and Russian forces. The reaction has been cool: Poland's deputy defense minister Cezary Tomczyk indicated NATO does not support the proposal. The debate nonetheless shows how the war's spillover into NATO territory is pushing allies to reconsider where the line is drawn, even as they stop short of direct involvement.

articles.title: Trump administration abandons business deals as incentive for Russia, shifts back to 'land for peace' approach
articles.description: The Trump administration has abandoned using business deals as an incentive for Russia to end the war in Ukraine and shifted back to a 'land for peace' approach, the Financial Times reported. Earlier the White House had dangled economic cooperation and sanctions relief in exchange for a settlement. The shift matters as negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. prepare to meet in Abu Dhabi — and President Zelensky says Washington wants a deal by January.
articles.body: According to the Financial Times, the White House has dropped the idea of offering Moscow trade, energy deals and sanctions relief as a sweetener for ending the war, and is now focused on a territorial settlement — land in exchange for peace. The business-incentive approach had been a signature of the administration's early diplomacy, promising Russia reintegration into global markets if it agreed to stop fighting. Its abandonment suggests Washington has concluded that economic carrots will not move the Kremlin, and that the deal now turns on the hardest question of all: territory. The timing is significant: trilateral talks are due in Abu Dhabi, and Zelensky has said the U.S. wants an agreement by January, a tight deadline while Russia intensifies its strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. For Kyiv, a 'land for peace' framing raises the stakes of the talks, since any territorial concession would be politically explosive at home.

articles.title: Zelensky says U.S. wants peace deal by January
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky says the United States wants a peace deal by January. He spoke as negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. prepared to meet in Abu Dhabi for talks aimed at ending the war. The timeline matters because it sets a tight deadline while Russia is intensifying its strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure ahead of the negotiations.
articles.body: Zelensky said Washington is pushing for an agreement by January, as the three sides prepare to meet in Abu Dhabi — the next round of the U.S.-brokered talks. The deadline lands as Russia steps up its attacks: Zelensky has accused Moscow of intensifying strikes on Ukraine and its infrastructure before the negotiations, saying Russia has 'a rather unusual view of diplomacy — as a subtype of expansion.' In one recent overnight attack, Russia fired 36 missiles and 172 drones at Kyiv and 12 other regions, damaging homes, energy networks and a kindergarten, and forcing the closure of a major Kyiv bridge. The January target gives the talks a concrete horizon, but it also raises questions about what kind of deal could be reached that fast — and at what price for Ukraine, given the administration's reported shift toward a 'land for peace' formula.

articles.title: Russian governor arrested on charges of embezzling a billion rubles and accepting an airboat as a bribe
articles.description: Murmansk region governor Andrey Chibis has been arrested on charges of embezzling a billion rubles and accepting an airboat as a bribe, and a court has ordered him detained. Chibis had led the Arctic region for seven years. It is the latest in a series of corruption cases against senior Russian regional officials during the war.
articles.body: Andrey Chibis, who spent seven years as governor of the Murmansk region in Russia's far northwest, was arrested and a court ordered him held in custody. Investigators accuse him of embezzling around a billion rubles and of taking an airboat — a flat-bottomed vessel used on Arctic waterways — as a bribe. The case is the latest in a run of high-profile corruption prosecutions against regional leaders and defense officials since the full-scale invasion began, a campaign the Kremlin presents as a wartime cleanup but which analysts also read as a tool for reshuffling elites and enforcing loyalty. Chibis's arrest is striking because Murmansk is a strategically important Arctic region, home to Russia's Northern Fleet, and because governors are usually removed quietly rather than arrested in public corruption cases.

articles.title: At least 11 Russian regions move to reduce C-sections; women say doctors refuse the procedure even when medically necessary
articles.description: At least 11 regions in Russia have introduced programs to reduce the number of cesarean sections, the independent outlet Novaya Gazeta Europe reported — and women say doctors are refusing the procedure even when it is medically necessary. The push is part of the state's pro-natalist demographic policy. It matters because it shows official birth-rate targets overriding medical judgment in Russian maternity care.
articles.body: At least 11 Russian regions have adopted programs aimed at cutting the number of cesarean sections, according to Novaya Gazeta Europe, whose reporting Meduza cited. Women in those regions say doctors are now refusing C-sections even in cases where the operation is medically indicated, leaving them to go through risky vaginal births. The campaign fits into the Kremlin's broader demographic drive: with birth rates falling and war losses mounting, the state has been tightening abortion access and promoting childbirth, and now appears to be treating the C-section rate itself as a target to be lowered. Medical experts note that cesareans are often life-saving, and that pressuring doctors to avoid them can endanger both mothers and babies. The story is a window into how Russia's demographic anxieties are reaching into the delivery room.

articles.title: Russia's Finance Ministry proposes 15% tariff on delicacies from 'unfriendly countries'
articles.description: Russia's Finance Ministry has proposed a 15% tariff on delicacies imported from countries Russia has declared 'unfriendly.' The measure would raise prices on imported luxury foods. It is part of Moscow's countersanctions toolkit as the war economy strains and the government looks for new revenue.
articles.body: Russia's Finance Ministry has proposed introducing a 15% tariff on delicacy food imports from 'unfriendly countries' — the official Russian list that includes the EU, the United States, the United Kingdom and other states that imposed sanctions over the invasion of Ukraine. The proposal would hit imported luxury foods, a category that has already shrunk sharply since 2022 as sanctions, countersanctions and import substitution reshaped Russian supermarket shelves. The move serves two purposes: raising revenue for a budget under heavy war spending, and further squeezing Western goods out of the Russian market. It also reflects the growing strain on Russia's wartime economy, where the government is hunting for new income as military expenditure stays high and growth slows.

articles.title: Ukraine's presidential chief of staff Budanov fined for speaking Russian
articles.description: Kyrylo Budanov, Ukraine's presidential chief of staff, will be fined 3,400 hryvnias (68 euros) for speaking Russian during events in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka on November 2. The fine follows a complaint under Ukraine's language law, which requires officials to use Ukrainian in their duties. It is a small penalty, but a symbolic one — language rules being enforced at the very top of the wartime government.
articles.body: Ukraine's presidential chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, is to be fined 3,400 hryvnias — about 68 euros — for speaking Russian during public events in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka, a town near Kyiv, on November 2. The fine was imposed after a complaint under Ukraine's language legislation, which obliges state officials to carry out their duties in Ukrainian. Budanov, the former military intelligence chief, only recently moved into the president's office, making him one of the most senior officials to be penalized under the law. The amount is trivial, but the case is symbolically charged: language has been a sensitive political issue throughout the war, with the state promoting Ukrainian in public life while millions of Ukrainians still speak Russian at home. That the rule is applied even to the president's right-hand man is the point the enforcement is making.

articles.title: Russia hits Kyiv and Kharkiv overnight with ballistic missiles and 113 drones; two killed in Kharkiv apartment strike
articles.description: Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with ballistic missiles and 113 drones, Ukraine's Air Force said, with air defenses shooting down or suppressing 87 of them. In Kyiv, ballistic strikes injured at least seven people and set a shopping center ablaze in the Desnianskyi district. In Kharkiv, a drone hit the 15th floor of an apartment block in the Novobavarskyi district, killing two people and injuring at least three, with people reported trapped under rubble.
articles.body: In the night of November 25–26, Russian forces launched a combined attack on Ukraine, firing Iskander-M, Tsirkon and S-400 ballistic missiles from the Bryansk and Kursk regions, along with 113 drones launched from six directions — including 76 jet-powered Shaheds plus Gerbera decoys and Parodiya imitators. By 8 a.m., Ukraine's military said it had neutralized 87 targets, 52 of them jet-powered Shaheds, using aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare units and mobile fire groups. In Kyiv, missiles struck in several waves, injuring at least seven people and starting a large fire at a shopping center in the Desnianskyi district. In Kharkiv, a drone slammed into the 15th floor of a residential high-rise in the Novobavarskyi district, killing two people and injuring at least three, and a second strike hit the Kholodnohirskyi district. The attack came as Dnipro and its region entered a fourth day of power interruptions after earlier strikes, and days before trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi — part of a pattern of Russia intensifying attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure ahead of negotiations.

articles.title: Ukraine downs jet-powered Shahed with Blysk laser air defense — a world first, presidential adviser says
articles.description: Ukraine's Blysk laser air defense system has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone, presidential adviser Serhii 'Flash' Beskrestnov said — the first time a jet-powered drone has ever been downed by a laser in combat. The system, built by the private company Carmine Sky, was placed on combat duty in Kyiv in early November. It matters because jet-powered drones are fast and hard to intercept, and a laser shot costs only electricity, versus $10,000–$100,000 for an interceptor missile.
articles.body: A combat laser guarding a critical infrastructure facility shot down a jet-powered Russian Geran drone, Beskrestnov, an adviser to President Zelensky on defense technology, wrote on Telegram — calling it a first in the world. The Blysk system, developed by the private Kyiv company Carmine Sky under the state's 'Private Air Defense' program with support from the Brave1 defense tech cluster, fires a 4-kilowatt beam with a range of up to one kilometer, burning through a Shahed's hull in several seconds. The jet-powered Geran-5 cruises at more than 450 kilometers per hour and flies as high as about six kilometers, according to Ukrainian military intelligence, making it far harder for traditional mobile air-defense teams to hit than the slower propeller-driven Shaheds. Blysk was placed on combat duty in Kyiv in early November but recorded no kills in its first days, as cloud and fog over the capital degraded the laser; it is not connected to Tryzub, the laser project announced in December 2024. Beskrestnov gave no date or location for the shootdown, and the claim has not been independently confirmed. He also cautioned that it is too early to talk about serial production — tests continue while the lasers protect critical infrastructure.

articles.title: North Korea pauses military aid to Russia after diplomatic spat, Ukrainian intelligence says
articles.description: North Korea has temporarily suspended military support for Russia, including deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery ammunition, Ukraine's military intelligence (GUR) said on November 26. Kim Jong Un reportedly ordered the pause personally after a dispute over remarks by Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed the claim, and it could not be independently verified — but if true, it would disrupt a key supply line for Russia's war.
articles.body: Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate said Kim Jong Un personally ordered a temporary halt to some military support for Russia, including KN-23 ballistic missiles and an upcoming batch of artillery ammunition. The restrictions reportedly also bar Russian military transport aircraft from North Korean airspace, and Pyongyang is holding back a Russian request to expand its troop contingent in Russia from 8,500 to 50,000 soldiers. According to GUR, the dispute began in October, when Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko said Moscow would help ease tensions between North and South Korea; North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui reportedly called that inconsistent with the alliance. GUR described the move as a slowdown, not a break, in cooperation. The claim fits other signs of friction: Zelensky said on November 17 that Russia receives dozens of North Korean ballistic missiles a month, while Deutsche Welle reported on November 24 that the large new North Korean deployment Zelensky predicted over the summer has yet to materialize. Moscow and Pyongyang have not commented, and the claim has not been independently verified.

articles.title: U.S. approves $621.9 million F-16 maintenance and equipment sale to Ukraine
articles.description: The U.S. State Department has approved the sale to Ukraine of F-16 maintenance and equipment worth $621.9 million under the Foreign Military Sales program. The package supports Ukraine's fleet of Western-donated F-16 fighter jets. It comes as Kyiv pushes to keep its air force flying through a winter of intense Russian missile and drone attacks.
articles.body: The U.S. State Department has authorized the sale to Ukraine of maintenance and equipment for F-16 fighter jets valued at $621.9 million, under the Foreign Military Sales program. The package is aimed at sustaining the F-16s donated to Ukraine by European allies, which have become a core part of Kyiv's air defense as Russia escalates its nightly missile and drone barrages. Keeping the jets mission-ready requires a steady flow of spare parts, servicing and support equipment, and the approval signals continued U.S. backing for Ukraine's air force even as the politics of further aid are debated in Washington. The announcement came alongside other military-support news, including the Pentagon saying it is ramping up production of Patriot interceptor missiles — a separate effort from the 48 interceptors Kyiv has been seeking under a contract that, Zelensky has said, the Pentagon chief has not yet signed.

articles.title: Budanov: first stage of large POW exchange may happen in late November or early December
articles.description: The first stage of a large-scale prisoner-of-war exchange between Ukraine and Russia may take place in late November or early December, presidential chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov said. The exchange is planned to run in several stages. It would be a rare humanitarian breakthrough at a moment when peace talks are stalled and fighting is intensifying.
articles.body: Kyrylo Budanov, the head of the President's Office, said the first stage of a major prisoner-of-war exchange between Ukraine and Russia could happen in late November or early December, with the swap carried out in several stages. No numbers have been announced publicly. Prisoner exchanges have continued sporadically throughout the war, often after long negotiations and mediation, and they remain one of the few channels where Kyiv and Moscow still deal with each other directly. The timing is notable: it would come just as trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi get underway and as Zelensky says the U.S. wants a peace deal by January. For the families of captured soldiers, who have waited months or years for news, even a staged exchange would be a significant moment — and a signal that, despite the escalation on the battlefield, some diplomacy still functions.

articles.title: Trump and NATO chief Rutte urge Russia not to expand war beyond Ukraine after Mar-a-Lago meeting
articles.description: Donald Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met at Mar-a-Lago on the evening of November 25 and urged Russia not to expand the war in Ukraine to other countries. The meeting came days after Russian cruise missiles fell on Polish territory. It signals allied unity ahead of the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi — and reports alongside it suggest the U.S. may delay planned cuts to its military presence in Europe.
articles.body: President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte met on the evening of November 25 at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, and afterward urged Russia not to expand the war in Ukraine to other countries. The warning follows the November 20 incident in which three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles crossed into Polish airspace and fell on Polish territory, an event that rattled NATO's eastern flank and revived debate about how the alliance should respond to spillover from the war. The meeting also came amid reports that the United States may postpone planned reductions of its military presence in Europe. For Kyiv, the message matters because it frames any Russian escalation beyond Ukraine as a red line for the alliance, even as Washington pushes for a negotiated settlement — and as Poland floats the idea of NATO shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine that are headed toward alliance territory.

articles.title: UK invests £9.5 million in 200-megawatt wind farm in Ukraine
articles.description: The United Kingdom will invest £9.5 million — about €11.3 million — in building a 200-megawatt wind farm in Ukraine. The project supports Ukraine's energy resilience at a moment when Russia is systematically targeting its power grid. It is a concrete British bet on Ukraine's postwar energy future, made in the middle of the war.
articles.body: Britain has allocated £9.5 million, roughly €11.3 million, to build a wind farm with a capacity of 200 megawatts in Ukraine. The investment lands as Russia keeps hammering Ukraine's energy infrastructure: on November 26, planned power outages were in force across parts of several regions, and Dnipro and its region were entering a fourth day of power interruptions after earlier strikes. Wind power is particularly valuable in this context because it is decentralized — harder to knock out with a single strike than a big thermal plant — and because it fits Ukraine's longer-term push to rebuild its energy system around renewables. The project also carries a political message: London is investing in Ukraine's reconstruction now, not waiting for the war to end, and is tying its support to the energy sector that Russia is trying hardest to destroy.

articles.title: Government simplifies approval of new Ukrainian defense tech for military use
articles.description: Ukraine's government has simplified the official approval process for new domestically developed defense items — including drones — to enter military service, Prime Minister Serhii Koretsky said. The change cuts red tape for Ukrainian weapons makers. It matters as Ukraine races to scale up its own arms production and reduce dependence on foreign supplies.
articles.body: The government has eased the formal admission of new Ukrainian defense developments into service with the armed forces, Prime Minister Serhii Koretsky announced. The simplified procedure covers items such as drones and other defense equipment developed by Ukrainian companies, which previously faced a lengthy official approval process before they could be used by the military. The reform is part of Kyiv's broader wartime push to build up domestic arms production — a strategy that has already produced systems like the Blysk laser air defense and a growing fleet of Ukrainian-made drones. With Western aid uncertain and Russian attacks intensifying, getting homegrown weapons to the front faster is a priority, and the government is betting that cutting bureaucracy will let small and mid-sized Ukrainian defense firms scale up more quickly.

articles.title: Capcom is shutting down Exoprimal — dinosaur shooter support ends in 2027
articles.description: Capcom has announced it will end support for its sci-fi PvPvE shooter Exoprimal on September 29, 2027, when the game's servers will be switched off. After that date the game will be unplayable even for existing owners. The season pass has already been pulled from sale, and the game itself will be delisted on March 30, 2027.
articles.body: Capcom has confirmed the end of the road for Exoprimal, its dinosaur-filled cooperative shooter that launched to a mixed reception. Support for the game will officially cease on September 29, 2027, at which point the servers will be shut down and competitive matches will no longer be possible — effectively making the always-online title unplayable. The publisher has already removed the season pass, which included premium content and in-game currency, from sale, while the base game and its expansions will remain available in digital stores until March 30, 2027. The closure gives the game's remaining community roughly a year of notice, but it is another reminder of how fragile live-service games are once publisher support ends. Exoprimal never found a large sustained audience despite its distinctive premise of exosuit soldiers fighting dinosaur hordes, and Capcom is now winding it down rather than investing further. For players, the key dates are clear: buy any remaining content before the end of March 2027, and expect the servers to go dark the following September. The announcement follows a wider industry pattern of publishers sunsetting underperforming live-service titles.

articles.title: Samsung unveils the world's first 1100Hz gaming monitor
articles.description: Samsung Electronics has presented the Odyssey G6 (G60H), a 27-inch gaming monitor capable of a refresh rate of up to 1100Hz — a world first. The display is aimed at competitive gamers where every millisecond counts. It carries one DisplayPort 2.1 connector and two HDMI 2.1 ports.
articles.body: Samsung Electronics has unveiled what it claims is the world's first gaming monitor with a refresh rate of 1100Hz: the 27-inch Odyssey G6 (G60H). The headline figure is aimed squarely at competitive and esports players, for whom ultra-high refresh rates can mean smoother motion and a marginal edge in reaction-based games. The monitor is equipped with a single DisplayPort 2.1 input alongside two HDMI 2.1 ports, giving it modern connectivity for high-end PCs and consoles. While few current games and graphics cards can actually push frame rates anywhere near 1100 frames per second, the panel is a statement of where display technology is heading, following the rapid climb from 144Hz to 240Hz, 360Hz and beyond in recent years. Samsung has not yet detailed pricing or a release date in the report, but the Odyssey line is its flagship gaming brand, so a premium price is likely. For most players the practical benefit over existing 240Hz or 360Hz screens will be small, yet the announcement sets a new benchmark that rival manufacturers will now chase. It also underscores how the monitor market continues to compete on raw speed even as resolution and HDR improvements slow.

articles.title: Insider: Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet coming to PS5 in late 2027
articles.description: Naughty Dog's sci-fi action game Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is set to launch on PlayStation 5 in late 2027, according to insider NateTheHate. The leaker had previously named 2027 as the studio's internal target and has now narrowed it to the end of the year. Studio head Neil Druckmann confirmed in September that a full presentation of the game will take place in 2027.
articles.body: The next game from Naughty Dog, the studio behind The Last of Us and Uncharted, may be closer than many expected. According to well-known insider NateTheHate, the science-fiction action game Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is scheduled to release on PlayStation 5 in late 2027. The insider had already pointed to 2027 as Naughty Dog's internal target over the summer, and has now refined that window to the final months of the year, expressing hope that the studio will impress players both when the game is shown and when it launches. The timing lines up with comments from studio head Neil Druckmann, who confirmed in September that a full presentation of Intergalactic will happen in 2027. The game was first announced at The Game Awards in December 2024, where its retro-futuristic style and bounty-hunter protagonist drew wide attention. Very little gameplay has been shown publicly since, so the planned 2027 reveal should finally clarify what the game actually plays like. If the late-2027 window holds, Intergalactic would become one of the biggest PlayStation exclusives of that year, and a major test of whether Naughty Dog can launch a successful new franchise after years focused on The Last of Us.

articles.title: Fan-saved Gothic 3 Classic launches on consoles
articles.description: THQ Nordic has released Gothic 3 Classic, a remaster of the cult RPG, on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5. The project was overseen by Alkimia Interactive, the Spanish studio behind this year's Gothic 1 Remake. Crucially, the remaster builds on the fan community's own work, incorporating mods based on the Community Patch 1.75 that fix graphics, balance and combat.
articles.body: THQ Nordic has announced the console release of Gothic 3 Classic, a remaster of the 2006 cult role-playing game, now available on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5. The project was handled by Alkimia Interactive, the Spanish studio that also delivered the Gothic 1 Remake earlier this year. What makes this release unusual is how much of it comes from the fans: the developers built on the community's own long-running work, folding in modifications related to graphics, balance, combat and gameplay, with the famous Community Patch 1.75 serving as the foundation. Gothic 3 was notoriously buggy at launch, and it was the fan community that spent years patching and improving it — so this official console version is, in a real sense, a game saved by its players. The remaster brings the open-world fantasy RPG to modern consoles for the first time, giving a new audience access to a series that helped define European RPG design. For longtime fans it is a chance to replay a classic in its most polished form, and for THQ Nordic it keeps the Gothic brand alive while the full remake of the first game continues to find its audience. The release is also a rare case of a publisher formally crediting and building on community modding work.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2 team has grown to nearly 200 people, CD Projekt RED pleased with progress
articles.description: CD Projekt RED has significantly expanded the team working on Cyberpunk 2 during 2026, with 199 developers now on the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 and plans to reach around 320 by the end of 2027. Management told investors it is happy with progress but is not yet ready to say when the project will enter full production. The Witcher IV remains the studio's priority, with 513 people on it and a release planned for 2028.
articles.body: CD Projekt RED is steadily ramping up work on Cyberpunk 2, the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077. According to the studio's latest financial report, 199 people are now working on the project, up sharply over the course of 2026, and the team is expected to grow to roughly 320 developers by the end of 2027. During an investor call, Karolina Gnas, the company's vice president for strategy and investor relations, said development is progressing well and leadership is pleased with where the sequel stands — but it is still too early to announce a date for moving into full production. Cyberpunk 2 will arrive only after The Witcher IV, which remains CD Projekt's top priority with 513 developers and a release planned for 2028. The studio's total developer headcount rose slightly from 1,045 to 1,051 since July, showing resources are being shifted rather than simply added. The growth of the Cyberpunk 2 team is a concrete sign that the sequel is moving from early concept work toward something more substantial, even if a release date is still years away. Earlier reports suggested the studio may add cooperative multiplayer to Cyberpunk 2, though nothing has been confirmed. For fans, the message is patience: the sequel is real, staffed and progressing, but The Witcher IV comes first.

articles.title: Remedy thrilled with Rockstar partnership as Max Payne remakes progress well
articles.description: Remedy Entertainment CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon has called working with Rockstar Games on the Max Payne 1 and 2 remakes a 'terrific' experience, praising the publisher's attitude toward the Finnish studio that created the series. The combined remake is in full production on Remedy's Northlight engine, with Rockstar funding and publishing. Remedy also noted Control Resonant had its strongest launch ever, selling a million copies in three weeks and returning the studio to profitability.
articles.body: Remedy Entertainment is happy with how its collaboration with Rockstar Games is going. In an interview with Game File's Stephen Totilo, Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon described the experience of working with Rockstar on the remakes of the first two Max Payne games as 'terrific', singling out the publisher's respectful attitude toward the Finnish studio that originally created the series. Rockstar is financing the project and will publish it, while Remedy rebuilds both Max Payne and Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne as a single combined remake on its Northlight engine. According to Remedy's November report, the project is now in full production. The comments come at a good moment for Remedy: its recent release Control Resonant had the strongest launch in the studio's history, reaching one million copies sold in three weeks and helping return the company to profitability. That success gives Remedy breathing room as it works on the Max Payne remakes alongside its other projects. For fans of the bullet-time noir shooters, the update is encouraging — the remake is not a side project but a fully staffed production backed by Rockstar itself. No release date has been announced yet, but full production status suggests the wait is now measured in years rather than an indefinite horizon.

articles.title: Marvel drops final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday ahead of December 18 premiere
articles.description: Marvel has released the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, with the film set to premiere in the US on December 18. The trailer leans on the X-Men, with the rallying line 'To me, my X-Men!' Marvel also published a composite poster of the main characters, which was widely criticised on social media for its low quality and poor character design.
articles.body: Marvel Studios has published the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, the next big crossover film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, ahead of its US premiere on December 18. The trailer puts the X-Men front and centre, including the rallying cry 'To me, my X-Men!', signalling how heavily the film leans on the mutant heroes as they are folded into the MCU. The release is one of the most anticipated films of the year, with Doomsday positioned as the next Avengers-scale event after years of build-up. Alongside the trailer, Marvel released a composite poster featuring the film's main characters — and that poster drew a very different reaction, with social media users criticising it for low quality and awkward character design. The contrast between the polished trailer and the poorly received poster has become a talking point of its own. With less than a month to go until release, the final trailer is Marvel's last big marketing push before opening weekend, and expectations are high: the film needs to deliver both as a spectacle and as a payoff for the multiverse storyline. Whether it can live up to the Avengers name — and the X-Men's long-awaited full MCU debut — will be decided at the box office in December.

articles.title: Russian government plans distribution certificates for video games, following the film model
articles.description: The Russian government is planning to introduce distribution certificates for video games, modelled on the existing system for films, according to sources cited by Kommersant. The idea was first proposed in 2024 but may now be backed as part of a draft law 'On activities for the development and distribution of video games in the Russian Federation.' The move would add a new layer of state approval to game releases in Russia.
articles.body: The Russian government is considering a new system of state control over video games. According to sources cited by the newspaper Kommersant, the cabinet plans to introduce distribution certificates for games, similar to the прокатные удостоверения already required for films shown in Russia. The idea was first floated in 2024, but it may now gain official backing as part of a draft law titled 'On activities for the development and distribution of video games in the territory of the Russian Federation.' If adopted, the system would mean games need a state-issued certificate before they can be distributed — a significant new regulatory step for the Russian games market, which has operated without such a permit regime until now. The proposal comes as Russian authorities continue to tighten oversight of digital media and entertainment, and it raises questions about how certification would work in practice: who applies, what criteria are used, and whether games could be refused a certificate. For Russian developers and distributors, the change could add bureaucracy and delays to releases, while for international publishers it would be another factor in an already complicated market. The draft law is still under discussion, so the final form of the rules — and whether the certificate idea survives — remains to be seen.

articles.title: UPDATE: Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday as storm hits New York
articles.description: UPDATE: For the first time in its history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed — moved to Saturday, starting at 8:30 a.m. ET — because of forecast heavy rain and strong winds from the nor'easter raking the East Coast. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will not attend Saturday's parade due to scheduled foot surgery. In Philadelphia, organisers cancelled the Thanksgiving Day parade, billed as the oldest in the nation, after first announcing they would ground the balloons.
articles.body: UPDATE: The storm story has a major new development: the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, an American institution, has been postponed for the first time in its history. Forecast heavy rain and strong winds from the nor'easter moving up the East Coast forced organisers to move the parade to Saturday, when it will now begin at 8:30 a.m. ET. The decision follows days of warnings that gusts of 25 to 35 mph across the New York area could endanger the parade's giant balloons, and the storm is now delivering exactly the wet and windy conditions forecasters feared. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will not attend Saturday's parade because of a scheduled foot surgery, he said during a news conference on Wednesday. The disruption extends beyond New York: in Philadelphia, organisers decided to cancel the Thanksgiving Day parade — billed as the oldest in the nation — after first announcing they would ground the balloons. The parade postponement caps a Thanksgiving week already upended by the storm, with thousands of flight delays, a state of emergency in New Jersey, and travel chaos across the Northeast. For millions of Americans the parade is a fixed point of the holiday, and moving a centennial edition to Saturday is a measure of just how severe this storm is. The new Saturday timing also sets up an unusual weekend, with the parade now competing for attention with the start of the holiday shopping season.

articles.title: UPDATE: Iowa residents get all-clear after Army detonation of five tons of explosives — testing continues
articles.description: UPDATE: The Army's controversial detonation of nearly five tons of deteriorating lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant went ahead on Wednesday, and residents were given the all-clear just after 6:30 p.m. ET, with officials saying monitoring detected zero airborne lead. But returning home is only the first step: extensive soil and air testing is still ahead, and officials have offered few details on how far oversight will go. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Iowa families deserve clear answers about what the monitoring shows.
articles.body: UPDATE: The story has moved on significantly — the detonation itself has now happened. Two hazy plumes rose over the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday morning as the Army carried out its plan to detonate nearly five tons of deteriorating lead azide, despite days of legal battles and public outcry from nearby residents in Middletown. Hours later, the Army announced an all-clear just after 6:30 p.m. ET, saying government mapping had detected zero airborne lead, and FEMA said the shelter-in-place order had been lifted so residents in the affected area could safely resume normal activities. The agency had offered lodging to those who chose to leave through Friday. But the all-clear is not the end of the story: post-detonation surface sampling is underway, results will be released once complete, and the EPA says it will continue air monitoring and sampling in the field, offering those services to people in the area. Experts caution that real-time monitoring, while encouraging — airborne lead levels held steady at 0.0 — does not have the same resolution as laboratory analysis, so there is still a need to wait and see. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. wrote on X that Iowa families deserve clear answers about what the monitoring shows, what remains under investigation and what they should do to protect their health. Incoming Iowa leaders are also calling for transparency about the longer-term oversight plan, which federal officials have so far described only in general terms.

articles.title: UPDATE: Tech stocks seesaw as AI fears overshadow Jensen Huang's Nvidia return
articles.description: UPDATE: Tech stocks clawed back some losses on Wednesday after a steep morning drop, but the AI sell-off continued despite Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO. The Nasdaq closed down 0.62% after falling as much as 4.6% at the open, and briefly fell 20% from its early-October peak — bear-market territory. Nvidia shares slid 3.9%, while hot October inflation data — core PCE up 3.3% year-on-year — fuelled expectations of a December Fed rate hike.
articles.body: UPDATE: The Jensen Huang story has developed dramatically — he is back as Nvidia CEO, but the market turmoil around AI has only deepened. On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO and president, sending the company's shares soaring more than 30% in their third-best day on record. But by Wednesday the mood had flipped: tech stocks plunged at the open as investors questioned AI valuations and braced for higher interest rates. The Nasdaq Composite fell as much as 4.6% shortly after the opening bell before paring losses to close down 0.62%, while the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% from its early-October peak — into bear-market territory — before recovering. The Dow erased an early 1,100-point drop to gain 165 points, and the S&P 500 closed down just 0.25%, buoyed by gains in non-tech sectors. Nvidia shares slid 3.9% on Wednesday, memory-chip makers SanDisk and Micron fell 5.6% and 4.6% respectively, and Anthropic dropped almost 10% intraday before ending the day up just over 1%. Inflation data released on Wednesday added to the pressure: core PCE, which excludes food and energy, rose 3.3% year-on-year in October, well above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, reinforcing bets on a December rate hike. Treasury yields fell sharply as nervous investors rushed into bonds, with the 10-year yield declining to around 4.84%. The whiplash — a 30% surge on Huang's return followed by a near-bear-market scare two days later — captures how unsettled the AI trade has become.

articles.title: US economy grew 4.3% in the third quarter — fastest in three years — but inflation stayed hot
articles.description: The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, revised sharply up from the earlier 3.4% estimate — the fastest pace in three years, powered by consumer spending and business investment in AI. But inflation remained a problem: core PCE rose 3.3% year-on-year in October, well above the Fed's 2% target. Consumer confidence also jumped to 103.3 in November, up 11.4 points from October.
articles.body: The US economy expanded considerably faster in the third quarter than the government initially reported, according to new numbers released on Wednesday by the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis. GDP grew at an annualised rate of 4.3% from July through September, revised up from the earlier estimate of 3.4% — the fastest pace in three years — powered by robust consumer spending and business investment in artificial intelligence. The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index also surged, reaching 103.3 in November, up 11.4 points from October's reading of 91.9. But inflation remained the stubborn problem hanging over the otherwise upbeat reports: the headline PCE price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, accelerated to 3.8% year-on-year in October, while core PCE, which excludes food and energy, came in at 3.3% — well above the central bank's 2% target. That combination of hot growth and sticky inflation is reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December and again in early 2027, a prospect that rattled markets on Wednesday. The data landed on the eve of Thanksgiving, adding an economic subplot to the holiday: Americans are spending and confident, but still paying more, and the Fed's next move is now the central question for investors heading into the end of the year.

articles.title: Americans to spend nearly $1 billion more on gas this Thanksgiving
articles.description: Drivers hitting the road this Thanksgiving weekend will spend about $980 million more on gas than last year, according to GasBuddy estimates shared with CNN, making this potentially the most expensive Thanksgiving ever for gasoline. The AAA national average for regular gas dipped to $3.62 a gallon on Tuesday, but prices remain elevated by the Iran war: Americans have paid an extra $165 billion for gas and diesel since it began in late February. AAA expects 72.9 million people to travel by car this weekend.
articles.body: Thanksgiving travel comes with a painful reminder of the Iran war at the pump. Americans hitting the road this holiday weekend will spend about $980 million more on gasoline over the five-day travel period starting Wednesday than they did last Thanksgiving, according to GasBuddy estimates shared with CNN — a figure that could make this the most expensive Thanksgiving ever for fuel, challenging the Biden-era record. The AAA national average for regular gas dipped to $3.62 a gallon on Tuesday, and prices have actually plunged by 56 cents through the first 24 days of November, the most on record, according to a CNN review of AAA data. GasBuddy estimates Americans are saving $1.3 billion on fuel compared with a month ago. But the longer view is bleaker: Americans have paid an extra $165 billion for gas and diesel since the Iran war started in late February — almost $1,300 per household — and that elevated baseline is what drives the year-on-year increase. AAA expects 72.9 million people to travel by car this holiday weekend, down slightly from 73.1 million last year, and overall AAA projects 81.5 million travellers in total. For families driving to Thanksgiving dinner, the cost of the trip itself has become part of the holiday's expense — and a visible, everyday consequence of a war now in its ninth month.

articles.title: FAA tightens 'Line Up and Wait' runway rules ahead of Thanksgiving travel rush
articles.description: As millions of Americans prepare to fly for Thanksgiving, the FAA is tightening the rules for 'Line Up and Wait', the air traffic control practice of holding an aircraft on the runway before takeoff clearance. From Tuesday, controllers may only permit it when their tower has a supervisor on duty who is not simultaneously working another control position. The change comes as the FAA forecasts 417,000 flights over the holiday period.
articles.body: With one of the busiest travel weeks of the year under way, the Federal Aviation Administration has tightened the rules governing a common air traffic control practice used to keep flights moving. Beginning Tuesday, controllers can only permit an aircraft to 'Line Up and Wait' — positioning a plane on the runway while it awaits takeoff clearance — when their tower has a supervisor on duty who is not simultaneously working another control position. The change is a safety measure aimed at reducing runway risks during a period of intense traffic: the FAA is forecasting 417,000 flights over the Thanksgiving travel period, and AAA projects 81.5 million travellers overall. The rule change lands in the wake of heightened scrutiny of the FAA and US aviation safety, including the recent nationwide ground stop that prompted a federal probe. 'Line Up and Wait' is a routine procedure, but it puts an aircraft in a vulnerable position on an active runway, and the new supervisor requirement adds a layer of oversight at exactly the moment when towers are at their busiest. For passengers, the practical effect should be minimal — a slightly more cautious flow of departures — but it is a visible sign of the FAA moving to tighten safety margins before the holiday rush peaks. The timing, days before Thanksgiving, underscores how seriously the agency is taking runway safety this season.

articles.title: Artists are quitting Instagram and Facebook over fears AI will steal their work
articles.description: Independent artists are leaving Instagram and Facebook in growing numbers, fearing Meta's proposed terms-of-service updates would let their images and styles be scraped to train generative AI models. CNN spoke with more than a dozen artists navigating the shift. Meta's updated terms were due to take effect October 30, then November 20, before being delayed indefinitely on November 5 — but the delay has not stopped the exodus.
articles.body: A wave of independent artists is walking away from Instagram and Facebook, and the reason is artificial intelligence. CNN spoke with more than a dozen artists who say they fear Meta's proposed updates to its terms of service would allow their images, styles and creative work to be scraped without their knowledge to train generative AI models. The problem is already visible: watercolour artist Matty Burnham from the UK told CNN he discovered a Pinterest account impersonating his illustration in 2024, with AI versions of his watercolours listed on fake profiles via Shopify, Facebook and Instagram. AI-generated art profiles are 'monetising Facebook', he said, taking business away from the creators themselves. The proposed terms were originally due to take effect on October 30, then pushed back to November 20, before Meta announced on November 5 that the updates were delayed indefinitely — with existing terms remaining in effect. But the delay has not reassured artists. Samantha Waldron, co-owner of Dutcher Photography in Madison, Wisconsin, told CNN she deleted all her business and personal Facebook pages earlier this month, moved her Instagram business accounts to personal ones, deleted most posts and removed external website links from her Meta bios. Megan Wimberley, founder of Cowgirl Artists of America in Tulsa, is deleting all her Meta accounts, calling the proposed terms a major breach of trust. Google released its SynthID Detector tool to the public this month to help identify AI-generated images, but for many artists the damage to trust is already done — and the platforms they built their livelihoods on now feel like a risk rather than a home.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' strange NFL trip may be over after incendiary attack on his head coach
articles.description: Aaron Rodgers' NFL career may be ending in fittingly baffling fashion after the four-time MVP tore into Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy on live television. Rodgers, benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, accused McCarthy of missing meetings and losing the team during Sunday's loss to the Eagles. With the season nearly over, his final image as a player may be a webcam rant rather than a touchdown.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers' strange NFL journey appears to be reaching its end, and the final act is as incendiary as anything in his career. The four-time MVP and Super Bowl champion, once the golden boy in Green Bay, tore into his head coach on live television, his headphone mic brushing against his sweatshirt, looking like a man at peace with ending a glittering career. The outburst came after the Pittsburgh Steelers revealed Rodgers would be benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, prompting his appearance on 'The Pat McAfee Show' — the same platform where he became known for Covid-19 scepticism, anti-vaccination takes and political rants. Rodgers said head coach Mike McCarthy was absent from an offensive meeting on Thursday, failed to show at a walkthrough on Friday and missed a morning meeting on Saturday before the Steelers' game in Philadelphia, and claimed McCarthy lost the team during Sunday's loss to the Eagles. McCarthy made clear on Wednesday that the benching decision was his, and he is about to lead his 11th game in charge of his hometown team. Rodgers has said his career will be over after this season, and there are few obvious landing spots left — the New England Patriots are in the hunt with Drake Maye out for the season with a broken ankle, while the Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts also face quarterback troubles. It is now possible that the final image of Rodgers as an active NFL player will not be in uniform, throwing a late-game touchdown, but on a webcam, unburdening himself to a baffled Pat McAfee. It seems, sadly, a fitting ending for one of the most baffling personalities in recent NFL history.

articles.title: UPDATE: The Chicks join Jason Isbell's class action against Suno as amended complaint adds 16 plaintiffs and targets v6
articles.description: An amended complaint filed November 24 in Boston federal court adds 16 new plaintiffs to Jason Isbell's proposed class action against AI music company Suno, including The Chicks, Dirty Projectors' David Longstreth, Carl Craig, Phil Elverum and Ezra Furman, plus the heirs of Willie Colon and Sam Moore. The filing also targets Suno's v6 models, launched in September, with new demonstrations showing the models still responding to artists' names. The case brings no copyright claims; instead it accuses Suno of encoding musicians' identities into its models without consent, under right-of-publicity laws in 14 states and Puerto Rico plus Illinois' biometric privacy law.
articles.body: The amended complaint was filed on Tuesday, November 24, in Boston federal court, 21 days after Suno asked the court to dismiss the case, the last day the plaintiffs could amend without Suno's consent or the court's permission. Isbell filed the original suit on August 31 alongside David Lowery, Guy Forsyth and Eduardo Calle. The 16 new plaintiffs also include Dirty Projectors founder David Longstreth, Detroit techno producer Carl Craig, Mount Eerie's Phil Elverum and singer-songwriter Ezra Furman, plus the surviving spouses of salsa bandleader Willie Colon and Sam & Dave singer Sam Moore. The new plaintiffs are residents of Illinois, California, New York, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Washington, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Hawaii, which matters because Suno's dismissal motion argued the original four lacked standing under the laws of states where none of them lived. Puerto Rico is now the only jurisdiction named in the complaint without a plaintiff based there. The filing adds demonstrations using Suno's v6 models, which launched in September, after the original suit was filed: the prompt 'Franz Nicolay' alone produced accordion-led songs described as theatrical folk-punk cabaret, even though Suno claims v6 was trained only on licensed music via BMG, Warner, Believe and TuneCore. Other examples include 'Emily Strayer' producing songs with a rolling banjo, 'Martie Maguire' returning a Texas country track, and a prompt of 'The Chicks' generating 'Feather Count', whose vocals saved as a reusable voice produced tracks with layered female harmonies singing Ford's jingle. The complaint keeps the original 17 counts and seeks an injunction, statutory and liquidated damages, restitution, disgorgement of profits and punitive damages. Suno also faces a second UMG/Sony suit filed in September asserting 60,202 further recordings, a $202 million Elvis Presley estate suit and a $47.7 million Eight Mile Style suit, both filed November 6.

articles.title: PRS for Music signs Roblox licensing deal, with royalty payments for songwriters from 2027
articles.description: PRS for Music has signed a licensing agreement with Roblox covering music use across the gaming platform, announcing the deal on November 25. Royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers will begin in 2027; financial terms were not disclosed. PRS calls it an important principle: when music creates value in online worlds, its writers should share in it.
articles.body: The UK collection society announced the deal on Wednesday, November 25, and says it will start distributing royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers in 2027. Financial terms were not disclosed. PRS says the agreement 'establishes an important principle: when music helps create value within online worlds, the people who write and compose it should share in that value.' Roblox hosts millions of user-built games and virtual worlds and reported an average of 138 million daily active users in Q3 2026, up 12% quarter-over-quarter but down 9% year-over-year. PRS chief commercial officer Dan Gopal said games are now among the world's most consumed entertainment media, and partnerships like this set foundations for how the industry moves forward. Roblox head of music partnerships Jessica Meehan said the platform is 'thrilled to welcome PRS as a partner as we build the future of the music economy on Roblox'. The deal is part of a wider PRS push to license music in games: in March it launched legal action against Steam operator Valve, alleging Valve has never obtained a licence for PRS members' music since the store launched in 2003. In a May 2025 op-ed, PRS executives called for a shift away from buyouts towards a consistent royalty model for music in games. Roblox has also struck music deals with Symphonic earlier this month, Too Lost in July, and DistroKid in 2024, when independent artists could opt in on a gratis basis. In June 2021 music publishers sued Roblox via the NMPA for more than $200 million, settling that September. PRS paid out GBP 1.07 billion (USD 1.41 billion) in 2025, up 4.9%, and represents more than 190,000 songwriters, composers and publishers.

articles.title: Musixmatch relaunches Pro for Artists with lyric merch, fan analytics and optional AI licensing coming soon
articles.description: Musixmatch launched a rebuilt Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform on November 25, adding lyric-merch sales, a Wallet for earnings, and an analytics dashboard tracking how fans engage with lyrics. The platform, used by more than 1.5 million artists, will also offer optional AI licensing 'coming soon', letting artists earn from authorised use of their lyrics by AI platforms. The company did not name the AI platforms or give a launch date.
articles.body: The new version of the platform went live on November 25, and Musixmatch says it is now used by more than 1.5 million artists. Artists and managers use the platform to transcribe and time-sync lyrics and distribute them to Spotify, Instagram, Apple Music, Amazon Music and Google. The update adds lyric merchandise that artists can sell to fans via the Musixmatch app and website, a Wallet tracking earnings, merchandise sales and referrals in a single view, and an Insights & Analytics dashboard combining streaming activity, follower data and lyric views across a catalog. Co-president Marco Paglia said lyrics are one of the most powerful ways people connect with music, and the new tools let artists see how and where fans engage with their lyrics and earn from that engagement directly. The platform's AI Enrichment tool transcribes lyrics and synchronises them line by line and word by word, and produces AI-generated meanings and themes for songs. Artists also get access to Music Lens, an AI agent unveiled in November 2025 that helps them explore their catalogs and uncover insights. The planned AI licensing option follows deals Musixmatch signed in October 2025 with the publishing arms of all three majors, Sony Music Publishing, Universal Music Publishing Group and Warner Chappell Music, giving it access to catalogs of more than 15 million works to develop non-generative AI services. Musixmatch did not name the AI platforms that would license lyrics through the Wallet or give a launch date. In October Musixmatch acquired Music Reports, the company behind the Songdex copyright registry, describing the deal as making it a full-stack rights and royalties platform.

articles.title: Believe fully acquires Lili Louise Musique, parent of French indie tot Ou tard
articles.description: Believe has fully acquired Lili Louise Musique, parent of French indie label tot Ou tard, becoming sole shareholder, announced November 25. Founder Vincent Frerebeau stays at the helm and keeps full control of artistic direction; terms were not disclosed. The deal completes a partnership begun in 2018, when Believe bought a 49% stake from Wagram Music for EUR 12.3 million.
articles.body: The Paris-headquartered company announced the deal on Wednesday, November 25, calling it 'a natural continuation' of a partnership that began in 2018, when Believe acquired a 49% stake in Lili Louise Musique from Wagram Music. Believe did not disclose the financial terms of the transaction, and founder Vincent Frerebeau will continue to lead the group with full control over its directions and artistic choices. The deal covers all of Lili Louise Musique's activities, including tot Ou tard, live performance company Zouave, publishing arm LLM, the innovative-projects company Guess What, and stakes in live music company Uni-t. Each brand will keep its identity, organisation, teams, premises and corporate culture, along with artistic, editorial and strategic autonomy, Believe said. Frerebeau said that in a market moving faster and faster, the ability to think long-term becomes even more valuable, and the new chapter protects what makes the group unique. Tot Ou tard, described by MBW in 2018 as the second-biggest independent label in France behind Because Music, celebrated its 30th anniversary this year, with best-known signings including Vianney, Vincent Delerm and Shaka Ponk. Believe's pre-IPO filings showed the company paid EUR 12.3 million for its original 49% stake. The deal follows Believe's October move to expand Romain Vivien's role, putting the Global Head of Music in direct charge of its EMEA, Americas and APAC regions. Believe itself was taken private by the Upbeat BidCo consortium of founder Denis Ladegaillerie, the EQT X fund and TCV funds, which acquired around 95% of its share capital in 2024 and completed a squeeze-out, with the company delisted from Euronext Paris in August 2025. Believe operates in more than 50 countries and employs more than 2,000 people.

articles.title: Beatles attraction at 3 Savile Row, site of the band's final public concert, approved by London council
articles.description: Westminster City Council approved plans on November 24 for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former Apple Corps HQ where the band played its final public concert on the rooftop in January 1969. The attraction, 'The Beatles at 3 Savile Row', is expected to open in 2027, with archive exhibitions, a recreated basement studio and rooftop access. Apple Corps CEO Tom Greene said visitors will feel they are sitting behind the band as they played their final show.
articles.body: Westminster City Council's Planning Committee signed off on the plans on Tuesday, November 24, for the project Apple Corps first unveiled in May under the name 'The Beatles at 3 Savile Row'. The attraction is expected to open in 2027, with exhibitions drawn from the Apple Corps archives, a recreated version of the basement recording studio, and access to the rooftop. The Beatles worked on 'Let It Be' in the building's basement studio in 1969, and on January 30 that year John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr, joined by Billy Preston, played on the building's roof in the band's last public live performance. The rooftop set was later featured in Peter Jackson's 2021 documentary 'Get Back', which won five Emmy Awards. Apple Corps CEO Tom Greene said visitors will feel they are sitting behind the Beatles as they played their fabled final show, before stepping onto probably the most famous terrace in the world. The front of the building will be returned to how it looked and felt in 1969, right down to the Apple green carpet, supplemented with the latest AV technology, and the company wants to host bookable evening events plus a cafe and bar in the basement for ticket holders. Draft conditions in Westminster's planning papers, reported by the BBC ahead of the vote, included a ban on live music on the rooftop terrace. The BBC also reported Apple Corps expects as many as 900 visitors a day on weekdays and 1,140 on weekends, while the Savile Row Bespoke Association objected, warning the street's narrow sidewalks could become congested. Greene told the committee the building was sold in the mid-1970s after the breakup and Apple Corps was excited to buy back the headlease, noting fans still congregate outside every day, and pointed to a letter Paul McCartney sent the committee. In October Apple Corps announced plans to take over The Beatles Story in Liverpool and move it to a 100,000-square-foot city centre site in 2028, and in August Universal Music Group signed a global partnership with Apple Corps covering Beatles merchandise, licensing and e-commerce. Sam Mendes' four Beatles films are set for release in April 2028.

articles.title: Downtown Music Publishing hires ex-Luminate exec Helena Kosinski and Armada's Michel Peek for international expansion
articles.description: Downtown Music Publishing has appointed Helena Kosinski as SVP of International Strategy and Business Development and Michel Peek as General Manager of UK & Europe, both newly created roles announced November 25 as part of a new international expansion strategy. Kosinski, formerly of Luminate/MRC Data/Nielsen Music, will lead DMP's international growth from London; Peek, formerly of Armada Music, will run the UK and European push from Virgin Music Group's Amsterdam offices. Peek reports to Kosinski, who reports to DMP president Emily Stephenson.
articles.body: Downtown Music Publishing announced the two newly created roles on Wednesday, November 25, as part of a new international expansion strategy. London-based Kosinski will lead the growth and transformation of the international business, spotting growth opportunities globally, setting DMP's strategy for signing clients and songwriters, and developing partnerships and commercial opportunities. She will report directly to DMP president Emily Stephenson, while Peek will report directly to Kosinski. Kosinski joins from her own consulting company, where she advised data and technology companies on the music business, and previously held executive positions at Luminate and its predecessors MRC Data and Nielsen Music, where she led the international business. Luminate, which powers the Billboard charts, took its current name in 2022, and Kosinski is also chair of the advisory board at Music Technology UK. Peek, based in Virgin Music Group's Amsterdam offices, is tasked with growing DMP's presence in the UK and Europe, building relationships with independent publishers, labels, managers and collecting societies. He joins from Armada Music, where he set up the company's publishing arm in 2018 and served as general manager of Armada Music Publishing; the Amsterdam label, co-founded by Armin van Buuren, formed its publishing arm in 2024 as part of its acquisition of Cloud 9 Music.
