Its sudden surge is the latest sign of how 'GTA VI' is rewriting chart fortunes: the game's soundtrack has already delivered a posthumous D'Angelo song, 'Kamikaze', and pushed Morgan Wallen's 'Last Thing You Need' up the Hot 100, while the 'GTA VI: The Album' deluxe edition runs to 57 tracks. The game's cultural footprint is enormous — it sold an estimated 44.9 million copies in its first four days — and its music choices are now moving streaming numbers at a scale few films or TV shows can match. Whether 'Run Away With Me' actually cracks the Hot 100 will depend on whether the streaming spike holds through the tracking week, but the fact that a decade-old album track is even in the conversation shows how a single placement in the biggest entertainment launch of the year can change a song's life. For Jepsen, whose career has been defined by critical adoration rather than chart dominance, a first Hot 100 entry for one of her signature songs would be a late and richly deserved milestone.

articles.title: Inside Harry Styles' MSG residency and why fans want experiential concerts
articles.description: Harry Styles' 30-night 'Together, Together' residency at Madison Square Garden — which ran from August 26 to October 31, 2026 — has become a case study in the new economics of live music, and in why fans now want experiences, not just concerts. Josephine Vaccarello, president of MSG Entertainment and Billboard's touring executive of the year, broke down the strategy on Billboard's 'On the Record' podcast, recorded live at Billboard's Live Music Summit on November 10. The residency model is one she believes will only keep growing.
articles.body: Harry Styles' 30-night 'Together, Together' residency at Madison Square Garden — which ran from August 26 to October 31, 2026, as part of a 67-date tour in just seven cities around the world — has become a case study in the new economics of live music, and in why fans now want experiences rather than just concerts. Josephine Vaccarello, president of MSG Entertainment, broke down the strategy on a special live edition of Billboard's 'On the Record' podcast at Billboard's Live Music Summit on November 10 in Los Angeles; she was selected as Billboard's touring executive of the year. According to Vaccarello, the summer of 2026 was the busiest the Garden has ever seen, and Styles' run — projected to generate $200 million at the box office alone — turned New York into a fan destination, with pop-up shops in NoHo and the East Village, exclusive merch, a karaoke station, photo booths and a 'Coming Up Roses' flower shop selling $5 roses for charity. The first 16 of the 30 shows helped drive a $30.1 million increase in concert revenue for MSG Entertainment and a 37 percent rise in total quarterly revenue. 'I do feel like people want to be a participant rather than a spectator,' Vaccarello said. 'We want to make sure that we're creating special moments throughout the entire journey for the customer, even from the initial outreach or announcement of a show up until them coming to the venue.' The residency model benefits artists, who stay put instead of living on a tour bus, and lets productions reach a scale that is not practical when a show moves every night — and fans have shown they will travel and pay premium prices for it, with presale prices for Styles' dates cresting $1,000 and resale listings at multiples of face value. Live Nation is putting on more than 470 residency shows this year, most of them in Las Vegas, and the model has been embraced by Beyoncé, Bad Bunny and Billy Joel, while Sphere has set a new standard for immersive live experiences. Styles' choice sums up the shift: big enough to play stadiums, he instead chose 30 nights at the Garden over four nights at MetLife Stadium, betting that intimacy, spectacle and a whole world built around the shows would matter more to fans than sheer capacity.

articles.title: Ariana Grande says 'insane' backlash to 'Petal' music video felt like 'Black Mirror'
articles.description: Ariana Grande has addressed the online backlash to the music video for 'Petal', describing the reaction as 'insane' and comparing the experience to an episode of 'Black Mirror'. 'Petal' is the follow-up project to her 'Eternal Sunshine' era, and a tour documentary is in the works showing the process behind both. Grande's comment underlines how quickly a video's imagery now gets dissected — and attacked — online.
articles.body: Ariana Grande has addressed the online backlash to the music video for 'Petal', describing the reaction as 'insane' and comparing the experience to an episode of 'Black Mirror'. 'Petal' is the follow-up project to her 'Eternal Sunshine' era, and a tour documentary is also in the works showing the process behind 'Eternal Sunshine' and 'Petal'. The video's imagery divided fans and commentators online, with the debate escalating quickly across social media — the kind of pile-on Grande likened to the dystopian anthology series, in which technology turns everyday life into a nightmare. Grande has been unusually candid in recent years about the toll of online scrutiny, and her 'Black Mirror' comparison captures how surreal it feels when a piece of art is instantly fed through the internet's judgement machine. The 'Petal' era comes as Grande balances music with film work and a major tour, and the documentary in progress suggests she wants fans to see the craft behind the spectacle rather than just the finished product. The episode is also a reminder of how the music-video cycle now works: a video is no longer just a visual for a song, but a cultural event in its own right, judged within hours by millions of people who have never heard the track in isolation.

articles.title: U.K. hard techno brand Teletech is on track to sell 500,000 tickets this year. Here's how it broke into America
articles.description: U.K. hard techno brand Teletech is on track to sell 500,000 tickets this year, and has broken into America — a striking rise for a sound that began in underground warehouses. The brand has ridden hard techno's surge from a niche European scene into festival main stages and US clubs. Its expansion shows how fast electronic music's hardest, fastest corner has gone mainstream.
articles.body: U.K. hard techno brand Teletech is on track to sell 500,000 tickets this year, and has broken into America — a striking rise for a sound that began in underground warehouses. Hard techno, with its pounding 140-plus BPM kicks and industrial edge, has surged from a niche European scene into festival main stages and US clubs over the past few years, and Teletech has been one of the brands leading the charge. The half-a-million-ticket figure puts the promoter in the same league as many mid-sized festival operators, and its US breakthrough marks a new phase: American audiences, long slower to embrace techno's harder end, are now turning up in large numbers for the sound. Teletech's growth mirrors a wider shift in electronic music, where the hardest and fastest styles — once confined to Berlin basements and Rotterdam raves — are now filling arenas and topping streaming playlists. For the live industry, it is another sign that the post-pandemic appetite for intense, communal, high-energy nights out has not faded, and that a brand built on underground credibility can scale without losing the crowd that made it.

articles.title: Director Peter Berg isn't giving up on the unreleased Rihanna documentary: 'Keep hope alive'
articles.description: Director Peter Berg says he has not given up on the unreleased Rihanna documentary he shot years ago, telling fans to 'keep hope alive' for the long-delayed film. The documentary, filmed over a number of years, has never been released despite longstanding interest from Rihanna's fans. Berg's comments suggest the project may yet see the light of day.
articles.body: Director Peter Berg says he has not given up on the unreleased Rihanna documentary he shot years ago, telling fans to 'keep hope alive' for the long-delayed film. The documentary was filmed over a number of years and has been the subject of speculation ever since, with Rihanna's fans — who have waited years for new music as well as new film — regularly asking when, or whether, it will ever appear. Berg's refusal to declare the project dead is the most encouraging sign in a long time that the footage may yet be finished and released. Rihanna remains one of pop's biggest stars despite not releasing an album in a decade, and a documentary offering an intimate look at her life and work would be a major event for her fanbase and for the music-film market, which has boomed in recent years with hit concert films and artist documentaries. Berg, best known for films such as 'Friday Night Lights', 'Lone Survivor' and 'Deepwater Horizon', has a long relationship with Rihanna, and his comments suggest the documentary is a passion project he is still determined to complete. For now, though, there is no release date — only Berg's message to fans to keep hoping.

articles.title: Dolly Parton to receive CNN Heroes Legacy Award, with Miley Cyrus accepting on her behalf
articles.description: Dolly Parton is to receive the CNN Heroes Legacy Award, and Miley Cyrus will accept the honour on her behalf. The award recognises Parton's decades of humanitarian work, from her Imagination Library — which has given away more than 200 million free books to children — to disaster relief and funding for vaccine research. Cyrus, Parton's goddaughter, is a fitting choice to collect the award.
articles.body: Dolly Parton is to receive the CNN Heroes Legacy Award, and Miley Cyrus will accept the honour on her behalf. The award recognises Parton's decades of humanitarian work alongside her music career, and the CNN Heroes ceremony is a fitting stage: it honours ordinary people doing extraordinary things, and Parton has spent a lifetime doing exactly that. Her Imagination Library, founded in 1995, has given away more than 200 million free books to children around the world, while her Dollywood Foundation has supported education and disaster relief in her native Tennessee, including major donations after the 2016 wildfires in the Smoky Mountains. She also helped fund the research behind the Moderna Covid-19 vaccine with a $1 million donation to Vanderbilt University. That Cyrus will accept the award on her behalf is a neat touch: Cyrus is Parton's goddaughter, and the two have performed together many times, including a memorable duet of 'Jolene'. Parton, who turned 80 this year, remains one of music's most beloved figures, and the Legacy Award is the latest in a long line of honours recognising that her impact goes far beyond her songs. Her philanthropy has become as much a part of her legacy as 'Jolene' and '9 to 5', and the CNN Heroes stage will put that work in front of a national television audience.

articles.title: Drake shot Future's 'Ya Hit' video scenes at Moody Center without permission, Rice University says
articles.description: Drake filmed scenes for Future's 'Ya Hit' music video at Austin's Moody Center without permission, according to Rice University. The arena, home to the University of Texas at Austin's basketball teams and a major concert venue, was used as a location for the video without authorisation. It is the latest in a string of unauthorised-filming rows involving big-name artists.
articles.body: Drake filmed scenes for Future's 'Ya Hit' music video at Austin's Moody Center without permission, according to Rice University. The arena — the 15,000-plus-capacity home of the University of Texas at Austin's basketball teams and one of the city's biggest concert venues — was used as a location for the video without authorisation from the venue. The revelation adds to a growing list of unauthorised-filming rows involving major artists, in which music videos and promotional shoots have used stadiums, arenas and other landmarks as backdrops without clearing the location first. For venues, the issue is not just the shoot itself but the precedent: a major arena appearing in a high-profile video without permission raises questions about control over the venue's image, insurance and liability, and about who profits from its use. Drake and Future are longtime collaborators — their joint mixtape 'What a Time to Be Alive' (2015) and the 'Life Is Good' video are landmarks of their partnership — and 'Ya Hit' is the latest in that run. Neither artist nor the venue has yet commented publicly on the claim, and it is not clear whether Moody Center will pursue the matter. The story is a reminder that even the biggest stars in the world still need a location permit.

articles.title: Lukashenko offers to fly Zelensky to Moscow for talks; Zelensky replies: 'What am I, his suitcase?'
articles.description: Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko has offered to fly to Moscow together with Volodymyr Zelensky for peace talks with Vladimir Putin, promising to personally guarantee the Ukrainian president's safety. Zelensky dismissed the idea as 'not a serious conversation', joking: 'What am I, his suitcase?' The exchange underlines how far apart the sides remain on where any talks could even take place.
articles.body: Alexander Lukashenko made the offer in an interview with the French magazine Le Point, saying: 'I could get on a plane with Volodya Zelensky and fly to Moscow. Just the two of us. As the guarantor of his security, I could get on a plane with him and fly to Moscow.' He argued that Russia, Ukraine and Belarus could reach a deal to end the war among themselves faster than with the Europeans, and added that if Zelensky refused, he should 'go to the front himself with a rifle and fight'. Zelensky responded on Tuesday that the proposal was 'not a serious conversation' and 'simply clogging up the information space with unconstructive proposals'. 'We are at war. We can't meet in Moscow, we can't meet in Kyiv. We all understand this perfectly,' he said, adding: 'Let him come to Kyiv together with Putin. And we will likewise guarantee them a safe reception.' Putin has repeatedly said he is willing to meet Zelensky, but only in Moscow — an offer Zelensky has rejected every time. Ukraine has accused Belarus of providing its territory to Russian troops since the start of the full-scale invasion, and Zelensky has also said Belarus installed relay transmitters along the border to help direct Russian drone strikes. The episode matters because it shows the peace-talk debate is still stuck on the most basic question — the venue — even as the US pushes for a final deal.

articles.title: Ukrainian drones strike two Rosneft refineries in Russia's Samara region overnight, one person killed
articles.description: Ukrainian drones attacked Russia's Samara region overnight, killing one person and setting two Rosneft oil refineries on fire, Meduza reported. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the strikes targeted the Kuibyshev and Syzran refineries. It is the latest in Ukraine's sustained campaign against Russian oil infrastructure.
articles.body: Ukrainian drones struck the Samara region overnight on November 24–25, and regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said one person was killed. Ukrainian Telegram channels reported that the Kuibyshev and Syzran refineries were hit, and Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the strikes, saying a fire broke out at the Kuibyshev plant, with primary oil-processing units and two storage tanks damaged. In Novokuybyshevsk, 70 apartment buildings, four schools, two kindergartens and one medical facility were left without electricity, according to the city's head. The attack came the same day Vladimir Putin said at a Kremlin meeting that Ukraine keeps striking Russian refineries despite Donald Trump's requests, and promised an 'inevitable' response. Ukraine's refinery campaign has been one of its most persistent strategies of the war, aiming to cut the fuel and revenue that sustain Russia's war machine. The overnight strike shows Kyiv is pressing on with that campaign even as US-led peace talks continue in Abu Dhabi, where delegations from the US, Russia and Ukraine are all reported to be present.

articles.title: Two Ukrainians accused of railway sabotage in Poland on behalf of Russian intelligence
articles.description: Poland has seen two acts of sabotage on its railways, and two Ukrainians working for Russian intelligence services are accused of carrying them out, Meduza reported. On November 15, an explosive device went off near the village of Mika as a freight train was passing. The incidents come amid a string of suspected Russian hybrid attacks across Europe.
articles.body: Two sabotage incidents have hit Poland's railways, and the suspects are two Ukrainians accused of working for Russian intelligence, according to Meduza's main-stories roundup. On November 15, an explosive device detonated near the village of Mika while a freight train was passing through. Polish authorities have treated the incidents as part of a pattern of Russian-linked sabotage across Europe, which has included arson, infrastructure attacks and other covert operations in NATO countries over the past two years. The case is sensitive because it involves Ukrainian citizens allegedly recruited by Moscow, a tactic Kyiv has warned about repeatedly. It also lands in the same week that Russia's ambassador to Warsaw, Georgy Mikhno, was summoned to the Polish Foreign Ministry and handed a 'very sharp diplomatic note' after Russian missiles were reported to have violated Polish airspace. For Poland, a key hub for military aid to Ukraine, railway security is directly tied to the war effort, and the sabotage raises questions about how Russia is trying to disrupt supply lines without an open confrontation with NATO.

articles.title: Moscow warns Russian military pensions in Latvia could stop if embassy staff are fired
articles.description: Russia says it will have to suspend pension payments to nearly 6,000 former Soviet military personnel living in Latvia if staff at the Russian Embassy's social security office are dismissed. Moscow says Latvia demanded that all of them be fired. The dispute is the latest friction between Russia and the Baltic states.
articles.body: Russia's Foreign Ministry has warned that it will be unable to keep paying pensions to military retirees living in Latvia if the staff of the social security unit in the Russian Embassy's consular section are dismissed. Nearly 6,000 people in Latvia receive Russian military pensions, and Moscow says Latvia demanded that all of the embassy's social security staff be fired. The pensions go to former Soviet military personnel and their families who remained in Latvia after independence, a group that has long been a point of tension between Riga and Moscow. Latvia, like Estonia and Lithuania, has taken a hard line against Russian influence since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, including restricting Russian-language education and moving to close border crossings with Russia — Estonia announced its land border crossings with Russia will close from December 1. The pension warning is a reminder that the Baltic states' break with Moscow reaches into the everyday lives of thousands of residents, and that Russia is using administrative levers to put pressure on its neighbours.

articles.title: Kazakhstan tried to secretly hand Chechen activist to Russia; he twice attempted suicide, fearing extradition
articles.description: Kazakh authorities tried to transfer Chechen activist Mansur Movlaev to a city where detainees are handed over to Russia, without telling his lawyers. A lawyer on the case says officials meant to extradite him in secret. Movlaev twice attempted suicide, fearing he would be sent back to Russia.
articles.body: On November 24, Kazakh authorities tried to transfer Chechen activist Mansur Movlaev from a pretrial detention centre in Almaty to Petropavl without notifying his lawyers, Meduza reported. A lawyer on the case said officials intended to extradite him to Russia in secret, using Petropavl as a transit point where detainees are handed over to Russian authorities. Movlaev twice attempted suicide, fearing extradition to Russia, where Chechen activists and critics of the Kadyrov regime face imprisonment, torture or worse. The case highlights the precarious position of Russian and Chechen exiles in Central Asia, where governments balance relations with Moscow against asylum obligations. Kazakhstan has previously handed detainees to Russia, and human rights groups have warned that extradition requests from Moscow are often politically motivated. Movlaev's case matters because it tests whether Kazakhstan will protect a critic of the Chechen authorities or quietly comply with a Russian request.

articles.title: Ukrainian psyop radio mixes Russian rock with instructions on how to surrender, NYT reports
articles.description: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces run a network of radio transmitters that wage psychological warfare on Russian troops, The New York Times reported, as covered by Meduza. The stations sound like local broadcasters, play Russian rock music, and slip in instructions on how to surrender. It is a glimpse into the information war running alongside the fighting.
articles.body: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces operate a network of radio transmitters designed to persuade Russian soldiers to lay down their arms, The New York Times reported, in a story picked up by Meduza. The stations are built to sound like ordinary local broadcasters: they play Russian rock music and mix in news and talk, before slipping in instructions on how soldiers can surrender safely. The idea is to reach Russian troops in the field and in occupied areas, where Ukrainian broadcasts would otherwise never be heard. Psychological operations have been a constant, quieter front of the war, from leaflets and phone calls to soldiers' families to Telegram channels aimed at Russian units. What makes this operation notable is its craft — using familiar music and formats to slip past listeners' defences rather than sounding like an enemy broadcast. It also reflects Kyiv's broader approach of targeting the morale and cohesion of Russian forces, not just their equipment, as the war grinds into its fifth year.

articles.title: Yandex removes all references to anonymity from its browser's user agreement
articles.description: Russian tech giant Yandex has removed all references to anonymity from its browser's user agreement. The company says the scope and purpose of data processing are unchanged. The change comes as Russia tightens control over the internet and digital privacy.
articles.body: Yandex, Russia's biggest tech company, has removed all references to anonymity from the user agreement for its browser, Meduza reported. The company says the scope and purpose of its data processing have not changed, presenting the edit as a technical update rather than a policy shift. But the removal of the word 'anonymity' from the agreement is symbolically significant in a country where the state has steadily expanded surveillance of online activity, from mandatory data retention to laws requiring companies to hand user data to security services. Yandex has been under growing pressure since the full-scale invasion, when it sold its news and media assets to state-controlled VK and its founder Arkady Volozh left Russia. The browser change matters for ordinary Russians because Yandex Browser remains one of the country's most popular browsers, and its privacy promises were one of the few things users could point to. In practice, the edit confirms what privacy advocates have long argued: anonymity was never truly on offer in the Russian internet.

articles.title: UPDATE: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia kill two and injure 50, including a baby and four children
articles.description: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia and nearby settlements on November 24 killed two people and injured 50, including a baby and four children, according to Ukraїnska Pravda. A separate morning strike on November 25 hit the Shevchenkivskyi district, injuring six more people, including two children. Much of the city was left without power after an energy facility was hit.
articles.body: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia and surrounding settlements on November 24 killed two people, and the number of injured in the city rose to 50 — among them one baby and four children, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. On the morning of November 25, a separate strike on the Shevchenkivskyi district damaged homes and cars, and the number of injured there rose from one to three and then to six, including two children, according to the State Emergency Service. After the overnight attacks, a large part of Zaporizhzhia and the region were left without electricity, with officials reporting a strike on an energy facility; electric transport stopped in the regional centre and residents reported interruptions to the water supply. Traffic across the Dnipro hydroelectric dam in Zaporizhzhia was also closed. The attacks fit the pattern of Russia's autumn campaign against Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, which has repeatedly hit civilian areas alongside power facilities. Zaporizhzhia, a frontline city, has been struck almost daily, and the rising toll among children underscores the human cost of a campaign that shows no sign of easing as winter sets in.

articles.title: Parliament passes law legalising cryptocurrency, with 18% tax and 5% military levy on profits
articles.description: Ukraine's parliament has passed a law legalising the cryptocurrency market and setting tax rules for it, with 271 MPs voting in favour. Profits from crypto transactions will be taxed at 18% personal income tax plus a 5% military levy. The law takes effect on July 1, 2027, and aligns Ukraine with the EU's MiCA crypto regulation.
articles.body: On November 25, the Verkhovna Rada passed Bill No. 10225-d, 'On Virtual Assets', by 271 votes to 8, legalising Ukraine's cryptocurrency market and setting out how profits from it will be taxed, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. The law is scheduled to take effect on July 1, 2027. It splits oversight between two institutions: the National Securities and Stock Market Commission will license and supervise service providers, while the National Bank of Ukraine will handle electronic money, stablecoins and currency controls. Individuals will pay 18% personal income tax plus a 5% military levy on profits from crypto transactions, calculated on net annual profit, while a preferential 5% rate will apply to qualifying pre-existing holdings through the end of 2028. The bill also extends the deadline for businesses to restore documents destroyed in the fighting from 90 to 180 days. The legislation fulfils commitments Ukraine made to the IMF and the European Union under the Ukraine Facility programme and is designed to align with MiCA, the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy must still sign the law before it takes effect. For Ukraine, the move brings a large, previously grey market into the open — and, with the military levy, turns crypto profits into a small but direct contribution to the war effort.

articles.title: UPDATE: Zelenskyy says Pentagon chief Hegseth has not signed contract for 48 Patriot interceptors
articles.description: President Zelenskyy has confirmed that the contract for 48 Patriot missiles has not been signed by US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying 'it depends exclusively on him'. The statement follows reports that the Pentagon had not approved the transfer of around 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine. Air defence remains Ukraine's most urgent need as Russia pounds its energy grid.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that the contract for 48 Patriot missiles has not been signed by US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, saying the decision 'depends exclusively on him', Ukraїnska Pravda reported. The statement follows a Financial Times report that the Pentagon had not approved the transfer of around 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, despite earlier expectations. The Patriot systems are the backbone of Ukraine's defence against Russian ballistic missiles, which have been used heavily in the autumn campaign against the country's energy infrastructure. With hourly power outages already in force in parts of Ukraine on November 25 and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant losing external power for the 17th time, every interceptor matters. Zelenskyy's public naming of Hegseth puts direct pressure on the Pentagon chief and signals Kyiv's frustration with delays in US military support. It also comes as Zelenskyy said he would ask the incoming Democratic-controlled US Congress for tougher sanctions on Russia if Donald Trump fails to secure a peace deal by the end of the year. The episode shows that even as peace talks continue in Abu Dhabi, Ukraine's immediate survival still depends on weapons decisions being made in Washington.

articles.title: Merz urges Europe to set clear limits for Russia
articles.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has called on Europe to set clear boundaries for Russia, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. The appeal comes as European leaders debate how to deter Moscow and support Ukraine while US-led peace talks continue. Germany is Europe's largest economy and a central voice in that debate.
articles.body: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has called on Europe to establish clear limits for Russia, Ukraїnska Pravda reported, in one of the day's top stories. Merz's appeal comes at a moment when European leaders are wrestling with two questions at once: how to deter further Russian aggression, and how to keep supporting Ukraine if US backing wavers. Germany, as Europe's largest economy and biggest military donor to Kyiv after the United States, carries particular weight in that debate. The call for clear boundaries also echoes the broader European discussion about red lines — from sanctions and frozen Russian assets to security guarantees for Ukraine — as the Trump administration pushes for a negotiated settlement. Merz has positioned himself as a more hawkish voice than his predecessor on Russia, and his statement signals that Berlin wants Europe to speak with one voice rather than letting individual capitals set their own terms. For Ukraine, a firm European line matters because any peace deal will need European money, weapons and political backing to hold.

articles.title: European Commission changes EU accession negotiating position on Ukraine after Polish demands
articles.description: The European Commission has partly accommodated Polish demands on protecting farmers and hauliers, changing the EU's negotiating position on Ukraine's accession, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. The shift shows how domestic politics in member states can reshape Kyiv's path to membership. Accession talks remain one of Ukraine's key strategic goals.
articles.body: The European Commission has changed the EU's negotiating position on Ukraine's accession after partly taking into account Polish demands on protecting farmers and transport operators, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. Warsaw has pushed for safeguards for its agricultural sector and road hauliers, worried that Ukrainian competition could undercut Polish producers once Ukraine joins the single market. The Commission's adjustment shows how Ukraine's membership bid is shaped not only by Kyiv's reforms but by the domestic politics of individual member states. Poland is one of Ukraine's most important allies — a key transit route for military aid and host to large numbers of Ukrainian refugees — but it has also been one of the most vocal about protecting its own farmers, with border blockades by Polish truckers and farmers a recurring feature of the war years. For Kyiv, the change is a reminder that the road to EU membership runs through 27 national capitals, each with its own interests. The accession process is also tied to the broader war effort: membership is seen in Kyiv as a long-term security guarantee in itself, anchoring Ukraine in Western institutions regardless of what any peace deal says.

articles.title: NABU and SAP uncover new criminal organisation in 'Carthage' case; anti-corruption chief warns of pressure campaign
articles.description: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office have uncovered a new criminal organisation in the 'Carthage' case, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. SAP chief Oleksandr Klymenko said the anti-corruption bodies know about a group behind a campaign against them, calling it a continuation of pressure on NABU and SAP.
articles.body: NABU and SAP have uncovered a new criminal organisation in the 'Carthage' case, Ukraїnska Pravda reported, in the latest development in one of Ukraine's biggest anti-corruption investigations. SAP chief Oleksandr Klymenko said the anti-corruption agencies are aware of a group behind what he described as a campaign against them, and called the campaign a continuation of pressure on NABU and SAP. The statement comes amid a tense period for Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions, which have faced political attacks and attempts to curb their independence since the summer, when controversial legislation briefly threatened their autonomy before mass protests forced a reversal. The 'Carthage' case adds to a string of high-profile investigations into corruption in wartime procurement and the energy sector. For Ukraine's Western partners, the independence of NABU and SAP is a key condition for continued financial support and for EU accession, so any pressure on them is watched closely in Brussels and Washington. Klymenko's public warning suggests the agencies believe the pressure is coordinated rather than incidental — and that they intend to fight it in the open.

articles.title: Norway to provide Ukraine at least $7 billion in 2027, mainly for air defence and drones
articles.description: Norway will provide Ukraine with at least $7 billion in 2027, mainly for air defence and drones, according to Ukraine's Defence Ministry. The commitment followed a meeting of defence ministers in Oslo. It is one of the largest single-year pledges from a European ally.
articles.body: Norway will provide Ukraine with at least $7 billion in 2027, primarily for air defence and drones, according to Ukraine's Defence Ministry, as reported by Ukraїnska Pravda. The commitment followed a meeting of defence ministers in Oslo. The scale of the pledge is striking: $7 billion in a single year from a country of 5.5 million people, and it is earmarked for the two capabilities Ukraine needs most — interceptors and air-defence systems to protect its cities and energy grid, and drones, which have become the central weapon of the war. Norway, enriched by energy revenues, has been one of Ukraine's most generous supporters relative to its size, and the 2027 pledge extends that support into a fourth year of full-scale war. The announcement also comes as Kyiv waits on delayed US decisions, including the unsigned Patriot missile contract, making European pledges more important than ever. For Ukraine, the Norwegian money is not just about hardware: it is a signal that at least some European allies are planning for a long war even while peace talks continue.

articles.title: Hourly power outages across parts of Ukraine as Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses external power for the 17th time
articles.description: Ukrenergo said hourly power outages will apply around the clock on November 25 in parts of Ukraine's regions, for all consumers, with limits for industry. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant lost external power for the 17th time due to shelling and is running on generators. A thermal power plant also stopped generating after heavy shelling.
articles.body: On November 25, hourly power outages will apply around the clock in parts of Ukraine's regions for all consumers, with 0.5 to 3 queues of outages, while industry faces power limits, Ukrenergo said, as reported by Ukraїnska Pravda. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant lost external power for the 17th time as a result of shelling and is operating on diesel generators, according to the Energy Ministry. In Dnipro and parts of the region, emergency power cuts were introduced after fresh Russian strikes on energy facilities. DTEK reported that one thermal power plant stopped generating electricity and suffered significant damage in a massive bombardment. The outages are the latest consequence of Russia's sustained campaign against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, which has already been attacked around 100 times in a single week earlier this month. With winter approaching, the grid is under its heaviest strain, and every new strike makes repairs harder. For millions of Ukrainians, the outages mean cold homes, dark streets and disrupted water supplies — the daily reality of a war now fought as much against the power grid as against the front line.

articles.title: Capcom to shut down Exoprimal in September 2027
articles.description: Capcom has announced it will end service for its dinosaur team shooter Exoprimal on September 29, 2027, after which the game will no longer be playable. In-game purchases were already switched off on November 24, and the game will be removed from digital stores on March 30, 2027. The closure ends the live-service experiment just over four years after the game's July 2023 launch.
articles.body: Capcom has announced that Exoprimal, its team-based dinosaur action game, will be shut down on September 29, 2027. After that date the game will no longer be playable at all, even for owners who bought it, because it is an online-only live-service title. The wind-down has already begun: the ability to buy items in the in-game store was disabled on November 24, 2026, and the game itself will be delisted from all digital storefronts on March 30, 2027, months before the servers go dark. Exoprimal launched in July 2023 for PlayStation, Xbox and PC, pitting squads of players in futuristic exosuits against waves of dinosaurs in fast-paced PvE missions. Despite a distinctive premise and a large launch roster of dinosaur types, the game never built a large lasting audience, and Capcom gradually scaled back its seasonal content. The shutdown follows a familiar pattern for live-service games that fail to hold players: a long sunset period, early removal from sale, and a final server switch-off. For Capcom, which has otherwise had a strong run of releases, Exoprimal stands out as a rare live-service misfire, and its closure frees the team and resources for the publisher's bigger franchises.

articles.title: Lords of the Fallen II delayed to April 2027
articles.description: CI Games has delayed its dark fantasy soulslike Lords of the Fallen II to April 2027, slipping out of the first-quarter window it promised earlier this year. Founder and CEO Marek Tyminski announced the new window on X on November 24, saying the exact release date will be revealed in December, possibly at The Game Awards. The game is coming to PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.
articles.body: CI Games has pushed Lords of the Fallen II back to April 2027, the company confirmed on November 24. Founder and CEO Marek Tyminski announced the new window in a brief post on X, writing simply: "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December." The exact date is expected to be revealed next month, with speculation that it could land during The Game Awards on December 10, though nothing has been confirmed. The delay is the latest slip for the sequel to the 2023 soulslike reboot: the game was once aimed at 2026 before being moved to the first quarter of 2027, and April now sits just past that window. CI Games did not give a new reason for the delay, though the project carries real financial pressure — the Warsaw-based publisher signed a 28.6 million euro syndicated bank loan in late October to fund the rest of production and marketing, and that facility matures in August 2027, leaving only a few months of sales to repay it. The sequel expands the series with new areas including Ysiguen, a region inspired by Asian mythology with twisted pagodas, demonic enemies and the dragon Lingao. A closed beta is planned for January 2027, ahead of the launch on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2 team to grow to around 320 developers by the end of 2027
articles.description: CD Projekt Red is steadily expanding the team building Cyberpunk 2, the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077. Around 199 developers are working on the game now, a figure expected to reach roughly 200 by the end of 2026 and about 320 by the end of 2027. The studio has also said it wants to develop games faster than it did with the original.
articles.body: CD Projekt Red has continued to grow the development team behind Cyberpunk 2, the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077. Around 199 developers are currently working on the project, according to the studio's latest update, and the team is expected to reach roughly 200 people by the end of 2026 before growing to about 320 by the end of 2027. The steady ramp-up reflects the game's scale: Cyberpunk 2 is still early in production, and CD Projekt Red is building out the team as pre-production gives way to full development. The studio has also spoken about its ambition to make games faster, having learned hard lessons from Cyberpunk 2077's long and troubled development cycle, which stretched across most of a decade and ended in a famously rocky launch before years of fixes and the Phantom Liberty expansion redeemed it. A team of 320 would still be smaller than the peak headcount on the original game, but it signals that the sequel is now one of the studio's main priorities alongside The Witcher 4. No release window has been announced, and with the team still growing, the game is likely years away. For fans, the numbers are the clearest public signal yet of how seriously CD Projekt Red is investing in returning to Night City.

articles.title: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis promises new content while faithfully recreating the 1996 original
articles.description: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, the upcoming reimagining of the original 1996 Tomb Raider, will offer plenty of new material while carefully recreating the best moments of the classic, according to its developers. The team has reworked location structure and aesthetics, story progression and gameplay mechanics rather than making a straight remake. The game is in development for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC.
articles.body: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is shaping up to be much more than a straight remake of the 1996 original, its developers have said. The game takes the first Tomb Raider as its foundation but will differ from it substantially, with the team reworking many elements including the structure and look of its locations, the way the story unfolds, and the underlying gameplay mechanics. At the same time, the developers say they are carefully preserving and recreating the best moments of the original — the tombs, traps and set pieces that made Lara Croft an icon — so returning players will recognise the adventure even as it plays differently. The balance is a familiar challenge for remakes of beloved classics: change too little and it feels like a museum piece, change too much and it loses what fans loved. Legacy of Atlantis is the latest attempt to modernise Lara Croft's debut for a new generation, following the well-received remastered collection of the original trilogy. It is in development for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC, though no release date has been announced yet. For a franchise approaching its 30th anniversary, the project is a test of whether the original's design can still work when rebuilt from the ground up.

articles.title: Activision wants to teach game bots to joke and gloat using voice-chat recordings
articles.description: Activision is exploring the idea of training AI bots in online games using recordings of real players' voice chats, so the bots can pick up how human players actually talk. A virtual teammate could celebrate a win with the squad, while a rival bot could taunt opponents after a kill. The idea raises obvious questions about how player voice data would be collected and used.
articles.body: Activision is considering using recordings of players' voice chats to train bots for its online games, teaching them to behave more like real people. The idea is that bots would learn from how human players actually communicate: a virtual teammate could celebrate a victory together with the squad, while a bot opponent could taunt or gloat after winning a firefight, mimicking the banter that is part of everyday multiplayer matches. The goal is to make AI-controlled players feel less robotic and more like genuine opponents and allies, particularly in modes where bots fill empty slots or serve as training partners. But the concept immediately raises questions about privacy and consent — voice chat is one of the most personal forms of player data, and using it as training material would require clear rules about what is recorded, how long it is kept, and whether players can opt out. It also touches on a sensitive area for Activision, whose Call of Duty games already use automated voice moderation to detect toxic behaviour in chats. Turning that same audio into a training resource would be a major step further. No specific game or launch has been attached to the idea, and it remains at the exploration stage rather than a confirmed feature. Even so, it points to where multiplayer AI is heading: bots that do not just shoot straight, but talk like the players they are replacing.

articles.title: Fan criticism did not change the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy's story
articles.description: The story of the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy was planned from the very beginning and has not changed in ten years, Square Enix says — not even after criticism from some fans. No corrections were made to the script in response to the backlash. The trilogy's final part, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, is dated April 8, 2027.
articles.body: Square Enix planned the full story of the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy from the start, and a decade later it has not changed a word of it — even after criticism from parts of the fanbase. According to the studio's leadership, the scenario was mapped out in full before the first game launched, and no corrections were made to the script in response to fan complaints about the direction of the story. That is a striking stance for a remake of one of the most beloved role-playing games ever made, where every plot twist is scrutinised by millions of players. The first two entries, Final Fantasy VII Remake and Rebirth, deliberately diverged from the 1997 original in places, introducing new characters and alternate-timeline elements that split the fanbase between those who welcomed the surprises and those who wanted a faithful retelling. Square Enix's message now is that those choices were always part of the plan, not reactions to feedback, and the ending was decided long ago. The trilogy concludes with Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which Square Enix has dated for April 8, 2027, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC. With the finale now less than five months away, the studio's insistence that the story never wavered sets up a final chapter that will be judged on a vision fixed a decade ago, for better or worse.

articles.title: Subnautica 2's first major update arrives December 2 with a new region and a giant leviathan
articles.description: Unknown Worlds has announced that Subnautica 2's first major update, called Tar Voyage, will launch on December 2. It adds a new region, vehicle upgrades and a huge predator called the Collector Leviathan, which hunts with four tentacles above deep-sea trenches. The update also advances the story, revealing what happened to the colonists who arrived before the player.
articles.body: Subnautica 2 will receive its first major content update on December 2, developer Unknown Worlds has announced. The update, titled Tar Voyage, is the biggest addition to the underwater survival game since it entered early access on May 14, and it brings a new region to explore, vehicle components and a giant new predator. The new area is home to the Collector Leviathan, an enormous creature that moves on four tentacles and hunts anything passing above the deep-sea trenches — a threat designed to make even veteran players think twice about where they swim. The small Tadpole submarine can also be fitted with a new Frog Chassis, giving it arms and legs so it can jump, sprint and climb walls, opening up new ways to move through the environment. Beyond the new creatures and gear, the update pushes the story forward, revealing the fate of the colonists who reached the planet before the player and shedding light on how their settlement fell apart. Subnautica 2 has been in early access for just over six months, and this update is an early test of the studio's post-launch plans for a game whose predecessor built its reputation on atmosphere, exploration and dread of the deep. The update arrives free for all early-access players on December 2.

articles.title: Steam Awards 2026 nominations open with a new Hall of Fame prize for past winners
articles.description: Valve has opened nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards, with players able to vote in each category until 10 a.m. Pacific time on November 30. This year marks the awards' tenth anniversary, and Valve has added a new Hall of Fame award, pitting every previous Game of the Year winner against each other for the title of best game of the past decade. Final voting starts December 18, with winners announced January 2, 2027.
articles.body: Valve has opened nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards, the community-voted prizes that have become a fixture of the platform's end-of-year calendar. Players can nominate games in more than a dozen categories — including Game of the Year, VR Game of the Year, Best Game on Steam Deck, Outstanding Visual Style and Outstanding Story-Rich Game — until 10 a.m. Pacific time on November 30. This year is the tenth anniversary of the awards, and Valve is marking it with a new category: the Hall of Fame award, which gathers every previous Game of the Year winner to compete for the title of best game of the past decade. It is a deliberately nostalgic addition, inviting players to weigh a decade of winners against each other rather than just the past twelve months. After nominations close, final voting will run from December 18, with the winners announced on January 2, 2027. The Steam Awards are unusual among industry prizes because they are decided entirely by players rather than critics or juries, which has produced some famously offbeat winners over the years. With GTA VI dominating the conversation this autumn, the Game of the Year race looks more predictable than usual — but the Hall of Fame vote, pitting ten years of champions against each other, may be the more interesting contest.

articles.title: FAA probe zeroes in on culprit of nationwide ground stop, but questions remain
articles.description: Investigators looking into the nationwide ground stop earlier this month have recreated the mysterious technical failure in a lab and believe they have found the culprit, a source familiar with the investigation told CNN. The focus is on a new router at a remote radio site in Arkansas that overwhelmed the air traffic control system with a massive amount of data, causing gaps in radar and radio communications. The findings come as the FAA chief and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy prepare to face tough questions at hearings next week.
articles.body: Investigators looking into what caused a nationwide ground stop earlier this month have been able to recreate the mysterious technical failure in a laboratory and believe they have found the culprit, according to a source familiar with the investigation. The probe has zeroed in on a new router installed at a remote radio site in Arkansas, which investigators believe overwhelmed the nation's air traffic control system with a massive amount of data, triggering gaps in radar and radio communications. The failure grounded flights across the country and exposed how fragile parts of the system can be. The findings are emerging just as the investigation itself faces scrutiny: FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy are set to appear at hearings on Capitol Hill next week, where they are expected to face tough questions about what went wrong and what happens next as the agency races to modernise the air traffic control system. CNN has reached out to the FAA and to L3Harris, the contractor that owns and operates the telecommunications system, for comment. The incident has renewed debate about the state of America's ageing aviation infrastructure, which relies on a patchwork of old and new equipment, and about whether modernisation is moving fast enough. With the Thanksgiving travel rush now under way, the timing of the hearings could hardly be more sensitive.

articles.title: Supreme Court, not Congress, will decide the future of Trump's immigration agenda
articles.description: The Supreme Court is set to decide the fate of President Donald Trump's immigration agenda, with blockbuster cases on his asylum ban, his expansion of mandatory detention of migrants, and his push to send some people in the US illegally to third countries with dubious human rights records. The first showdown comes December 9, when the justices hear arguments on third-country removals. Decisions are expected by late June.
articles.body: The future of President Donald Trump's immigration agenda will be decided by the Supreme Court, not by Congress, as the justices prepare to take up a series of blockbuster appeals. The court will soon consider challenges to the president's asylum ban, his vast expansion of mandatory detention of migrants, and his push to send certain people in the US illegally to countries other than their homeland — including some with dubious human rights records. The showdown begins on December 9, when the justices will hear arguments in a case challenging Trump's push to remove certain migrants to third countries. In the spring, the court will hear a challenge to the asylum ban. Decisions in these cases are expected by late June. The stakes are enormous: immigration enforcement has been the centrepiece of Trump's second term, and the rulings will determine how far a president can go in reshaping the system by executive action. Steve Vladeck, CNN Supreme Court analyst and professor at Georgetown University Law Center, said it stands to reason that hyper-aggressive immigration enforcement will continue to be one of the hallmarks of the Trump administration even as it faces Democratic majorities in both chambers of the legislature. With Congress divided, the court has effectively become the arena where the limits of presidential power on immigration will be drawn.

articles.title: Key Chinese Communist Party figure placed under corruption probe as Xi's purge escalates
articles.description: Chen Jining, the Communist Party chief of Shanghai and a man considered a potential heir to Chinese leader Xi Jinping, has been placed under investigation for suspected serious violations of discipline, state media Xinhua said on Tuesday evening. The move marks an escalation of an anti-corruption purge that has already ensnared a large swath of China's top officials. Chen, 62, has run China's largest city and financial centre since October 2022.
articles.body: The Communist Party chief of Shanghai, considered one of the potential heirs to Chinese leader Xi Jinping, has suddenly been placed under investigation, marking an escalation of an anti-corruption purge that has already ensnared a large swath of the country's top talent. Chen Jining, 62, who has run China's largest city and financial centre since October 2022, is facing a corruption charge and is suspected of "serious violations of discipline," state media Xinhua said on Tuesday evening. The announcement is striking because of Chen's stature: Shanghai is China's economic engine, and its party chief is one of the most powerful posts in the country, often seen as a stepping stone to the very top. That a figure once talked about as a possible successor to Xi could fall under investigation shows how far the purge has reached — and how few officials can now be considered untouchable. Xi's anti-corruption campaign has been running for more than a decade and has removed thousands of senior officials, but its recent escalation has swept up figures across the military, government and party apparatus. The probe of Chen raises fresh questions about stability at the top of the party and about who, if anyone, is being groomed to follow Xi. No further details of the allegations against Chen have been released.

articles.title: Miss Universe crowns winner after another turbulent year for the world's biggest pageant
articles.description: Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico was crowned Miss Universe 2026 on home soil, capping off another tumultuous 12 months for the scandal-plagued pageant. The win gives Puerto Rico a home-soil victory in a year when the competition has again been dogged by controversy offstage. Details of the final night's competition are still emerging.
articles.body: Jennifer Barreto of Puerto Rico was crowned Miss Universe 2026 on home soil, capping off another tumultuous 12 months for the scandal-plagued pageant. Winning in front of a home crowd, Barreto takes the crown in a year when the world's biggest beauty pageant has once again been dogged by controversy away from the stage, from questions about its ownership and finances to disputes over judging and transparency. The pageant, which draws tens of millions of viewers worldwide, has spent recent years trying to reinvent itself — admitting married women and mothers, raising age limits and presenting itself as a platform for advocacy rather than just appearance — while still wrestling with the scandals that have followed it. Barreto's victory is a major moment for Puerto Rico, which has a long and proud history in international pageantry and has produced several Miss Universe winners. The island's fans turned the final night into a homecoming celebration. For the Miss Universe organisation, the hope will be that a popular winner on home soil can shift attention back to the competition itself after a year in which the headlines were so often about everything except the contestants.

articles.title: Democrats cracked the GOP's southern red wall this year. Now they are plotting how to tear it down
articles.description: Following Democratic upsets across the South in the midterm elections, party donors and strategists are planning to target more seats in the region, starting with gubernatorial elections next year. Democrats flipped Senate seats in Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, powered in part by a surge in Black turnout, and came within two points in Louisiana. The biggest upset saw Democrat Scott Colom topple Mississippi Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith.
articles.body: Following Democratic upsets across the South in the midterm elections, invigorated party donors and strategists are planning to target more seats in the region, starting with gubernatorial elections next year. Democrats — powered in part by a surge in Black turnout — achieved broad gains this month, flipping Senate seats in Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, and coming within two points of doing so in Louisiana, a state President Donald Trump won by 22 points two years ago. In one of the biggest upsets of the midterms, Democrat Scott Colom toppled Mississippi Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith to become the first Black senator elected from the state since the Reconstruction era. In an interview with CNN, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear, the outgoing head of the Democratic Governors Association and a likely 2028 presidential candidate, exulted in his party's gains in the South — though he faced some criticism for not having the Democratic Governors Association invest more in the successful campaign of Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa. The results have shattered the long-standing assumption that the South is safely Republican territory, and Democratic strategists now see an opening to compete in states they had largely written off. The next test comes in next year's gubernatorial races, where the party will try to prove that the midterm gains were the start of a realignment rather than a one-off reaction to Trump. Republicans, meanwhile, will be working to win back voters who drifted away in a year when corruption ranked as a bigger concern than the cost of living for many voters.

articles.title: Federal grand jury indicts Thomas Markle on child sex abuse material charges
articles.description: A federal grand jury in Los Angeles on Tuesday indicted Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, on charges that he kept child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors say the material included photos in which Markle himself was pictured with prepubescent children. The indictment is a dramatic new turn for a man already estranged from his daughter and long a tabloid fixture.
articles.body: A federal grand jury in Los Angeles on Tuesday indicted Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, on charges that he kept child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors say the material included photos in which Markle himself was pictured with prepubescent children, according to the indictment. The charges mark a dramatic and dark new chapter for Markle, who has been estranged from his daughter for years and has become a regular fixture in the tabloid press, giving interviews about the royal family while his relationship with Meghan remained broken. He has never met his grandchildren and has spoken publicly and often bitterly about the rift. The indictment now puts him at the centre of a federal criminal case, with charges of the most serious kind, and the details alleged by prosecutors are stark. Federal cases involving child sexual abuse material typically carry severe penalties, and the grand jury's decision to indict means prosecutors presented enough evidence to establish probable cause. Further details of the case, including when Markle is expected to appear in court, have not yet been released. The news is likely to reverberate well beyond the courtroom, given Markle's connection to the Duchess of Sussex and the years of public attention on the family's estrangement.

articles.title: UPDATE: Jensen Huang apologizes to employees, says he's in therapy
articles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees in an hour-long company-wide meeting on Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the matter, and said he is in therapy. The apology follows his dramatic reinstatement as CEO on Monday after President Trump pressed Nvidia's board to restore him. Meanwhile, the longtime board members who backed his return saw the value of their combined holdings jump by nearly $2.5 billion as the stock surged more than 30 percent.
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees in an hour-long company-wide meeting on Tuesday, according to a source familiar with the matter, and told staff he is in therapy. The apology comes a day after Huang was dramatically reinstated as chief executive, following an unprecedented corporate saga in which the board first accepted his resignation and then, under pressure from President Donald Trump, restored him to the job on Monday morning. Huang's return sent Nvidia's shares soaring more than 30 percent, easing fears of a market crash that had alarmed the White House. The episode has also cast a harsh light on Nvidia's board: longtime directors Tench Coxe, Mark Stevens and Harvey Jones, who stood by Huang through the crisis, saw the value of their combined holdings jump by nearly $2.5 billion from Friday to Monday as the stock rebounded. Including Huang, nearly half of Nvidia's 11-person board has been with the company since its early days, and the three longest-serving members together own more than 62 million shares. Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, known as the "CEO Whisperer," called the board's decision to reinstate Huang a "complete failure of corporate governance" and urged the directors to resign. Questions also remain about prohibited Nvidia chips reaching China despite US export controls, and about Huang's affair with a woman US officials feared could be working with Chinese intelligence. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: UPDATE: Thanksgiving nor'easter could become a bomb cyclone as it rakes the East Coast
articles.description: The storm bearing down on the East Coast for Thanksgiving is strengthening into a nor'easter that could become a bomb cyclone if its central pressure falls fast enough, forecasters say. Heavy rain, gusts over 50 mph and moderate to major coastal flooding are expected from Georgia to Long Island, with rain reaching New York City around 10 a.m. on Thanksgiving morning. The FAA expects the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years, with more than 417,000 flights scheduled over nine days.
articles.body: The storm threatening Thanksgiving travel on the East Coast is intensifying into a nor'easter that could become a bomb cyclone if its central pressure drops rapidly enough, meteorologists say. The system will form off the Southeast on Wednesday and track up the coast through Thanksgiving Day, bringing soaking rain, strong winds and severe coastal flooding. Rainfall rates could reach an inch per hour at times, with wind gusts exceeding 50 mph along the coast, and onshore winds combined with king tides — the highest tides of the year — and this week's full moon could produce moderate to major coastal flooding from Georgia and the Carolinas to Long Island. Major flooding is possible in Charleston, South Carolina, during Wednesday morning's high tide, and moderate flooding is expected from Delaware to New Jersey, with the greatest threat at Thursday morning's high tide. In New York City, home to the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, conditions should stay dry for the 8:30 a.m. start, but rain is forecast to develop by late morning and intensify through the evening, with gusts over 40 mph from Washington to Boston posing problems for the parade balloons — city rules require balloons to fly lower or stay grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph. On the storm's western edge, up to six inches of wet snow could fall around St. Louis, where a winter storm watch is in effect. The travel stakes are enormous: the FAA expects the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years, with more than 417,000 flights scheduled over nine days, and Tuesday was forecast to be the busiest day with 52,000 flights. Rain could disrupt flights across the Southeast, including Atlanta, on Wednesday before moving into the Mid-Atlantic.

articles.title: FTC and seven states ask court to throw out 10 of Live Nation and Ticketmaster's defenses in BOTS Act lawsuit
articles.description: The US Federal Trade Commission and seven states have asked a federal judge in Los Angeles to strike 10 of the 12 defenses Live Nation and Ticketmaster raised against their ticket-resale lawsuit. The motion, filed November 19, argues the defenses are legally or factually deficient, including the claim that scalpers rather than Ticketmaster caused any harm to fans. A hearing is scheduled for January 7, 2027.
articles.body: The US Federal Trade Commission and seven states have asked a federal judge to throw out 10 of the 12 defenses Live Nation and Ticketmaster raised against their ticket-resale lawsuit, in a motion filed in federal court in Los Angeles on Thursday, November 19. The states are Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Nebraska, Tennessee, Utah and Virginia. The lawsuit, filed in September 2025, alleges Ticketmaster knowingly let brokers spread purchases across multiple accounts to get around artist-set ticket limits, then triple-dipped on fees: charging brokers when they bought, again when tickets were relisted on its own resale marketplace, and charging the fans who bought them there. The complaint says consumers paid more than $16.4 billion in mandatory fees on Ticketmaster purchases from 2019 through 2024, including $3.7 billion in fees on resale tickets. The FTC and states want civil penalties, other monetary relief and a court order stopping the practices. Among the targeted defenses are four blaming scalpers and bot operators for any harm, two arguing the BOTS Act is too vague to apply, and claims that the companies were singled out or sued too late. The motion notes the companies earlier called the BOTS Act's language clear in their motion to dismiss, and points out a judge already ruled on September 28, 2026 that the Act does not preclude platforms from facing liability. Live Nation and Ticketmaster deny the allegations and called the suit misguided. A hearing on the motion is set for January 7, 2027. The case is separate from the antitrust lawsuit in which a Manhattan jury found in April that the companies operated illegal monopolies.

articles.title: PRS for Music signs Roblox licensing deal
articles.description: UK collection society PRS for Music has signed a licensing agreement with Roblox covering the use of music across the gaming and creation platform, with royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers starting in 2027. The deal, announced Wednesday, November 25, comes as PRS pushes to license music use in games, including its March legal action against Steam operator Valve. Roblox reported an average of 138 million daily active users in Q3 2026.
articles.body: PRS for Music has signed a licensing agreement with Roblox covering the use of music across the gaming and creation platform, the UK collection society announced on Wednesday, November 25. PRS says it will start distributing royalty payments to songwriters, composers and publishers in 2027, and that the deal establishes the principle that when music helps create value within online worlds, the people who write and compose it should share in that value. Financial terms were not disclosed. Roblox hosts millions of user-built games and virtual worlds and reported an average of 138 million daily active users in Q3 2026, up 12% quarter-on-quarter but down 9% year-on-year. The agreement is part of a wider PRS effort to license music in video games: in March it launched legal action against Steam operator Valve, alleging Valve has never obtained a license for PRS members' music since the store launched in 2003, a case concerning the communication to the public right. PRS executives have called for a shift away from buyouts and towards a consistent royalty model for music in games, pointing to Roblox and Fortnite. Roblox has also signed a series of music deals, including with Symphonic and Too Lost this year, and a 2024 DistroKid beta that let independent artists opt in on a gratis basis. In 2021 a group of publishers sued Roblox via the NMPA for more than $200 million, settling that September. PRS paid out £1.07 billion ($1.41 billion) to songwriters, composers and publishers in 2025, up 4.9% year-on-year, and says it represents more than 190,000 writers and publishers.

articles.title: City of Baltimore sues Vivid Seats over alleged bait-and-switch ticket pricing
articles.description: The City of Baltimore sued Vivid Seats on Monday, November 23, alleging the resale platform advertises ticket prices fans can never actually pay. The suit cites a J. Cole ticket at CFG Bank Arena advertised at $156 that cost $238 at checkout, and a Trevor Noah ticket rising from $125 to $205. Vivid Seats denies the allegations and says it has shown all-in pricing nationwide since May 2025.
articles.body: The City of Baltimore is suing Vivid Seats, alleging the ticket resale platform advertises prices that Baltimore fans can never actually pay, in a lawsuit filed in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City on Monday, November 23, under the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance. The city wants a court order stopping four practices it says leave fans paying more than advertised, plus civil penalties for each violation and attorneys' fees. According to the city, a pre-suit investigation identified misleading Google search ads showing prices unavailable on the Vivid Seats site until at least July 2026, drip pricing that climbs screen by screen through checkout, per-ticket prices that applied only to buyers purchasing at least two tickets, and mandatory service and delivery fees shown only after the first page until at least April 2026. City Solicitor Ebony M. Thompson said a family seeing a $98 ticket advertised and paying $154 for it is bait-and-switch, a 57% markup. The complaint cites examples from shows by J. Cole, BTS, Megan Moroney and Trevor Noah: a J. Cole ticket at CFG Bank Arena advertised at $156 cost $238 by the final checkout screen, and a Trevor Noah ticket rose from $125 to $205. The city argues Vivid Seats exploits shoppers' tendency to stick with a purchase once they have invested time in it, using what the FTC calls digital dark patterns. Vivid Seats denies the allegations, saying it has presented all-in pricing nationwide since the FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect in May 2025. Baltimore is not the first public body to sue Vivid Seats over pricing: Pennsylvania prosecutors sued in May 2025, and in April rival StubHub agreed to refund $10 million in fees to settle FTC allegations. The UK's Competition and Markets Authority fined StubHub UK close to £900,000 in June over fees added only at checkout.

articles.title: Dutch collecting society BumaStemra threatens legal action against AI background music supplier YourNeuroTune, alleging it uses Suno
articles.description: Dutch collecting society BumaStemra has given AI background-music supplier YourNeuroTune until noon CET on Wednesday, November 25 to confirm it will stop supplying music made with Suno, or face court action. BumaStemra says Suno was trained on its members' music without permission, and that YourNeuroTune tells business customers they no longer need to pay the society. YourNeuroTune says it will only respond on the substance if the matter goes to court.
articles.body: Dutch collecting society BumaStemra is threatening legal action against AI background music supplier YourNeuroTune, giving the Netherlands-based company until noon CET on Wednesday, November 25 to confirm it will stop commercially supplying music made with an AI model it says was trained on creators' work without permission. If it does not, BumaStemra says it will go to court. YourNeuroTune supplies background music to gyms, hospitality venues and retailers, and tells customers they no longer need to pay anything to BumaStemra, according to the society's statement on Tuesday, November 24. BumaStemra says it has established that YourNeuroTune used Suno, and that the company's conduct is unlawful because creators are forced to compete with a product built on their own work while receiving nothing. YourNeuroTune told Dutch current affairs programme Nieuwsuur it was aware of the ultimatum but would only respond on the substance if the matter went to court. The company, based in Hilvarenbeek, says it serves more than 450 clients in four countries and charges UK customers £44.95 per location per month; its site advertises premium business music with no PPL or PRS fees and generates a pre-filled email for Dutch customers to cancel their BumaStemra license. Co-founder Sam Jansen told Dutch outlet IO+ in October that the company works only with models under commercial license, without naming them. BumaStemra opted out of text and data mining under Dutch copyright law in March 2024. The dispute joins a widening set of collecting-society cases against Suno: GEMA won its case in Munich on July 31, Koda sued in Copenhagen in November 2025, and SOCAN filed in Canada in September. Suno is also defending US lawsuits from Universal and Sony, while Warner settled in November 2025 and struck a licensing partnership, followed by deals with BMG and Believe.

articles.title: ATC Music Group to acquire the UK's One Media iP for $20M, secures facility of up to $133M to buy more music rights
articles.description: London-headquartered ATC Music Group has agreed to acquire UK music rights company One Media iP for £15 million (about $20 million), and secured a conditional facility of up to £100 million (about $133 million) from Corrum Capital for future catalog acquisitions. The acquired business, with a catalog of more than 400,000 assets, will be rebranded ATC Rights, led by former Round Hill Music global COO Steve Clark.
articles.body: London-headquartered ATC Music Group has agreed to acquire UK-based music rights company One Media iP for £15 million (approximately $20 million), the company announced on Monday, November 23. The majority of the price, £12 million, will be funded from a new acquisition facility from US-based Corrum Capital Management, which can be expanded with further uncommitted facilities up to a total of £100 million (about $133 million) for future acquisitions of music rights and catalogs. ATC also conditionally raised about £3.1 million (about $4.1 million) through an oversubscribed share placing, around £2 million of which will go toward the purchase price. The acquired business will be rebranded ATC Rights, with former Round Hill Music Global COO Steve Clark joining as Managing Director. The deal gives ATC a music rights and digital distribution operation at scale for the first time, completing a platform built over five years that now spans artist management, live work and rights ownership. One Media iP was established in 2005 and owns a catalog of more than 400,000 assets, including master recordings, composition rights and producer royalties; it generated revenues of £4.8 million and profit before tax of £0.9 million in the year to October 31, 2025. The sale needs approval from One Media iP Group shareholders at a general meeting on December 11, with holders of 32.2% of shares already backing it. ATC's management arm represents more than 100 artists, writers and producers, including Radiohead, Nick Cave and Robbie Williams, and its live booking business ATC Live joined forces with Arrival Artists in September 2025 to form ROAM. Corrum has been active in music rights financing, backing Atlantic Screen Group with $30 million in January and helping finance GoDigital Music's roughly $115 million purchase of Latin catalogs in December 2025.

articles.title: As The MLC hits $4.4B in royalties paid to songwriters and publishers, CEO Kris Ahrend sets out its priorities for the next five years
articles.description: The Mechanical Licensing Collective has now distributed more than $4.4 billion in royalties since launching in January 2021, with membership past 110,000. In an interview, CEO Kris Ahrend says the MLC will begin distributing its remaining unclaimed royalties on a market-share basis in April 2027, starting with January 2021 usage, and sets out plans to use AI to fix publishing data problems.
