articles.description: Russian forces struck the city of Zaporizhzhia overnight on November 24, killing two people and injuring dozens, according to the regional military administration. The strikes destroyed a private home, partially destroyed a five-storey apartment building and damaged other homes and transport infrastructure. The casualty count rose through the morning as rescue work continued.
articles.body: Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia overnight on November 24, killing two people and injuring dozens, said Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of the regional military administration. The strikes destroyed a private home, partially destroyed a five-storey apartment building in the city's Kosmichnyi district, and damaged other multi-storey and private homes as well as transport infrastructure. At least 22 people were reported injured in the first hours, including two children, and the number later rose to 44 as rescuers pulled more victims from the rubble and hospitals updated their counts. Zaporizhzhia, a frontline regional capital in south-eastern Ukraine, has been hit repeatedly in recent weeks as Russia intensifies its campaign against Ukrainian cities. The attack was part of a wider overnight barrage in which Russia launched 96 strike drones across Ukraine, with impacts recorded at 13 locations. Ukrainian air defences said they neutralised 73 of the drones, but the ones that got through hit residential areas and critical infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia, Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr regions. The strike is a reminder that, even as diplomacy over a possible peace deal continues, Russia's nightly attacks on Ukrainian cities have not let up — and civilian casualties keep mounting.

articles.title: UPDATE: At least 720,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine by fall 2026, Meduza and Mediazona estimate
articles.description: At least 720,000 Russian armed forces personnel had died in the war in Ukraine by late September 2026, according to a new analysis by Meduza and Mediazona based on leaked Russian mortality data. It is the first estimate to include troops listed as missing, and it is far higher than previous public counts. A parallel analysis by Novaya Gazeta Europe put confirmed, registered deaths at at least 490,000.
articles.body: At least 720,000 Russian armed forces personnel had died in the war in Ukraine by fall 2026, according to a new analysis by Meduza and Mediazona, published on November 23. The estimate is based on leaked data from Rosstat, Russia's federal statistics agency, obtained by the hacker groups Cyber Partisans of Belarus and SilentCrow, who breached Rosstat's systems earlier in the autumn. More than a dozen independent journalistic teams worked on the data, and the analysis is the first to include soldiers listed as missing in action — many of whom are almost certainly dead — which is why the figure jumps so sharply from earlier counts. A parallel investigation by Novaya Gazeta Europe and other outlets, using the same leaked records, found at least 490,000 Russian men aged 18 to 64 whose deaths have already been entered into official registries; the gap between that confirmed figure and the 720,000 estimate reflects paperwork delays and the missing. The data also reveals how Russians are dying: according to iStories, which examined the same leaked records, explosions and shrapnel account for 92 percent of recorded Russian military deaths, while gunshot wounds account for less than 2 percent — a sign of a war dominated by artillery, drones and mines rather than close combat. The figures dwarf Russia's official casualty statements, which Moscow has barely updated since 2022, and they raise hard questions about how long the Kremlin can sustain its manpower-intensive offensives. For Ukraine and its allies, the numbers are also a measure of the war's grinding human cost on both sides.

articles.title: South Korea scrambles fighter jets over Russian military aircraft, issues evacuation alert on island
articles.description: South Korea scrambled fighter jets on the morning of November 24 after several Russian military planes briefly entered the country's air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan. An evacuation alert was issued on an island in the area. The incident comes amid heightened tensions over Russian military activity near US allies in East Asia.
articles.body: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said several Russian military planes briefly entered the country's air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan on the morning of November 24. Seoul scrambled fighter jets in response, and an evacuation alert was issued on an island in the area as a precaution. The aircraft did not enter South Korean territorial airspace, and such incursions into the identification zone — a buffer area where foreign aircraft are expected to identify themselves — happen periodically, but they are treated seriously because they test response times and readiness. The incident comes as Russia has stepped up military signalling toward US allies in the Pacific, including joint patrols and bomber flights with China, and as Moscow's war in Ukraine continues to strain its relations with Seoul. South Korea has been a significant, if indirect, supporter of Ukraine, and the episode is a reminder that the war's reverberations extend well beyond Europe. No confrontation or shots were reported, and the Russian aircraft left the zone after the South Korean jets were launched. Seoul typically lodges a formal protest through military channels after such incidents.

articles.title: Russian lawmakers draft bill that would ban foreign films from cinemas for weeks at a time
articles.description: Russia's State Duma has drafted a bill introducing quotas for foreign films in cinemas, according to the state news agency TASS, which said it had obtained a copy of the document. The quotas would effectively ban foreign films from Russian screens for weeks at a time. The move is the latest step in the Kremlin's campaign to push Western culture out of Russian public life.
articles.body: Russia's State Duma has drafted a bill that would introduce quotas for foreign films in cinemas, according to the Russian state news agency TASS, which said it had obtained a copy of the document. Under the proposal, foreign films would be barred from Russian screens for weeks at a time, with domestic productions given priority in scheduling — a sharp escalation of the cultural protectionism that has grown since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Hollywood studios largely stopped releasing films in Russia in 2022, and the market has since been dominated by Russian productions and films from friendly countries, but foreign titles still reach cinemas through parallel imports and independent distributors. The bill would formalise that squeeze into law, giving the state a direct lever over what audiences can watch on the big screen. It fits a broader pattern: the authorities have already tightened control over books, music, theatre and streaming, and have repeatedly framed Western popular culture as a threat to Russian values. For Russian cinemas, which have struggled with falling attendance and a thin slate of domestic hits, the quotas could mean more empty screens — and more pressure to show state-approved fare. The draft has not yet been formally introduced, so its final form and timetable remain unclear.

articles.title: Why is Estonia closing its border with Russia?
articles.description: Estonian authorities have announced the closure of all land border crossings with Russia starting December 1, and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna explained the decision in a column for Politico. The move follows a string of sabotage and hybrid-warfare incidents blamed on Moscow. A petition by a Narva resident asking to keep the border open for family visits prompted Estonia's interior minister to suggest petitioning Putin to end the war instead.
articles.body: Estonian authorities have announced the closure of all land border crossings with Russia starting December 1, and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna explained the reasoning in a column for Politico. Estonia, a NATO and EU member sharing a 294-kilometre border with Russia, has accused Moscow of waging a hybrid campaign against it — including sabotage, GPS jamming, cyberattacks and the use of migrants as a pressure tool — and the border closure is presented as a security measure rather than a political gesture. The decision has divided opinion in the border city of Narva, where many residents have family on the Russian side: one resident, Ksenia Agar, launched a petition asking Estonia to keep the border open for family visits, and Estonia's interior minister responded by suggesting she petition Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine instead. Russia's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, summoned Estonia's acting chargé d'affaires in Moscow and lodged a formal protest over the closure, while again accusing Tallinn of letting Ukrainian drones use Estonian airspace — a claim Estonia denies. The closure is the most drastic step yet by a Baltic state to seal its Russian frontier, and it follows similar moves elsewhere in the region as governments brace for further escalation. For the thousands of people who cross the Narva-Ivangorod checkpoint for work, family and trade, December 1 will cut one of the last remaining direct links between the two countries.

articles.title: Lithuanian SIM cards found in Russian drones that attacked Ukraine
articles.description: Lithuanian prepaid SIM cards have been found in Russian drones that attacked Ukraine in 2025, the Lithuanian outlet 15min reported, citing data from Ukrainian military intelligence. The discovery shows how Russia sources ordinary consumer electronics from EU countries for its weapons. It raises fresh questions about sanctions enforcement on dual-use goods.
articles.body: Lithuanian prepaid SIM cards have been found in Russian drones that attacked Ukraine in 2025, the Lithuanian outlet 15min reported, citing data from Ukrainian military intelligence. The cards were recovered from downed drones and traced to Lithuanian mobile operators, illustrating how Russia's weapons programme relies on ordinary consumer electronics bought in the European Union and smuggled through third countries. Drones such as the Shahed use mobile networks for navigation and communication, and a local SIM card lets them connect to civilian infrastructure in the country they are attacking. The finding is the latest in a long series of cases in which Western-made components — chips, sensors, engines and now SIM cards — have turned up in Russian missiles and drones despite sweeping sanctions. For Lithuania, a frontline NATO state that has been one of Ukraine's staunchest supporters, the discovery is politically sensitive: it suggests sanctions loopholes are operating inside the EU itself, not just through distant intermediaries. Ukrainian intelligence has been systematically cataloguing the foreign parts in captured Russian weapons, and its findings have repeatedly embarrassed Western governments into tightening export controls. The case is likely to add pressure on the EU to close gaps in its sanctions regime, particularly for dual-use goods that are easy to buy in bulk and hard to trace.

articles.title: Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov's son granted Serbian citizenship
articles.description: Serbian authorities have granted citizenship to Ali Kadyrov, the second son of Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, according to the Navalny-founded Anti-Corruption Foundation, which found the decision in official records. The grant gives a member of one of Russia's most powerful families an EU-candidate country's passport. It is likely to draw scrutiny in Belgrade and Brussels.
articles.body: Serbian authorities granted citizenship to Ali Kadyrov, the second son of Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, according to the Navalny-founded Anti-Corruption Foundation, which found the decision in official records. Ali Kadyrov is the younger brother of Akhmat Kadyrov, who has been groomed as a possible successor to his father, and the family sits at the centre of the Kremlin's power structure in Chechnya. Serbian citizenship gives a member of that family the passport of an EU candidate country — and with it, easier travel and business access across Europe — at a time when the EU has sanctioned Ramzan Kadyrov himself for human rights abuses and his role in the war in Ukraine. It is not clear on what grounds the citizenship was granted, or whether Ali Kadyrov applied through ordinary naturalisation, investment or a discretionary government decision, and Serbian officials have not publicly commented. The Anti-Corruption Foundation, founded by the late Alexei Navalny, has made a practice of tracing the foreign assets and passports of Russian elites and their families. The revelation is likely to embarrass Belgrade, which has tried to balance its EU accession ambitions with close ties to Moscow, and to prompt questions in Brussels about how the citizenship was awarded. For the Kadyrov family, it adds another foothold in Europe at a moment when the West is trying to close such doors.

articles.title: Pentagon has not approved transfer of about 60 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine, FT reports
articles.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to sign off on the transfer of roughly 60 Patriot interceptor missiles already allocated to Ukraine, the Financial Times reports. Four scheduled PAC-3 batches and about 20 PAC-2 missiles are in limbo, even though Kyiv's Western allies have already paid for them. Ukrainian officials link the delay to a broader US strategy of pressuring Kyiv into concessions toward Russia.
articles.body: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to authorise the transfer of around 60 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptor missiles for Patriot air defence systems to Ukraine, the Financial Times reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. The missiles were already allocated to Kyiv and paid for by Ukraine's Western allies, but four scheduled PAC-3 batches and about 20 PAC-2 missiles are now stuck awaiting Pentagon approval. A separate initiative to enable Ukraine to manufacture its own Patriot interceptors has also been delayed, according to the report. The Pentagon says US support policy has not changed, but Ukrainian officials link the hold-up to a broader American strategy of pressuring Kyiv into concessions toward Russia as Washington pushes for a negotiated end to the war. The delay matters acutely because Patriot interceptors are Ukraine's only reliable defence against Russian ballistic missiles, and Russia has sharply increased its missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure this autumn — launching 153 ballistic missiles and more than 4,000 jet-powered drones in October alone, according to Defence Minister Yevhen Khmara. With winter approaching and Russia systematically targeting power plants, every interceptor counts. The report lands the same day Ukraine and Germany reached a preliminary agreement on additional interceptor missiles, underlining how Kyiv is scrambling to plug the gap from multiple directions at once.

articles.title: Russia attacks Ukraine with 96 drones overnight, 73 neutralised
articles.description: Russia attacked Ukraine with 96 strike drones overnight from November 23 into November 24, Ukraine's Air Force reported. By 08:00, air defences had shot down or jammed 73 of them, including 45 jet-powered Shaheds, but impacts were recorded at 13 locations. Two people were killed in Zaporizhzhia, and Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr regions reported injuries and damage to critical infrastructure.
articles.body: Russia attacked Ukraine with 96 strike drones overnight from 18:00 on November 23 into November 24, Ukraine's Air Force reported. The wave included 64 jet-powered Shahed drones as well as Gerbera attack drones and Parodiya decoy UAVs, reflecting Russia's shift toward faster, harder-to-intercept weapons. By 08:00 on November 24, Ukrainian air defences had shot down or suppressed 73 of the 96 drones, but impacts were recorded at 13 locations across the country. The heaviest toll was in Zaporizhzhia, where two people were killed and dozens injured after strikes hit residential buildings. In Vinnytsia, a critical infrastructure facility was hit, and in Zhytomyr region six people were injured and a railway station in Korosten was attacked, killing one person and wounding two. The overnight barrage was part of a sustained Russian campaign against Ukraine's energy system and cities ahead of winter: Russia has already damaged five major thermal power plants in recent weeks, and emergency power outages are in effect in several regions. Ukrainian officials say the jet-powered Shaheds are a particular problem, because they fly faster and lower than earlier models, giving air defences less time to react. President Zelenskyy said after a meeting of the military command that Ukraine needs more F-16 and Swedish Gripen fighter jets to counter the new drone threat, and that countering it is the central task for this year and next.

articles.title: UPDATE: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine behind drone strike on Russian cargo ship Sparta II in Gulf of Finland
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that Ukraine was behind the drone strike on the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, saying the vessel, which was carrying weapons, was a legitimate target for the Ukrainian military. Two drones hit the ship on the morning of November 21 as it sailed from St Petersburg to Kaliningrad. Finland's coast guard was notified of the incident.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that Ukraine was behind the drone strike on the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland, saying the vessel, which was carrying weapons, was a legitimate target for the Ukrainian military. Two drones hit the Russian-flagged cargo ship on the morning of November 21 while it sailed from St Petersburg to Kaliningrad, and Finland's coast guard was notified at 08:50 local time. The Sparta II is a Defence Ministry-linked vessel used to carry military cargo between Russia and its Kaliningrad exclave, and Ukraine's strike extends its targeting of Russian maritime logistics into NATO-adjacent waters. The confirmation marks a shift: Kyiv had previously left the attack unattributed, and an open claim of responsibility in the Baltic is a deliberate signal that Russian supply routes are not safe even far from the Black Sea. Finland now faces the delicate task of managing the precedent — a Ukrainian strike in waters near its coast, against a Russian military cargo ship, with Helsinki needing rules for how to respond to such incidents. The attack follows Ukraine's sinking of the Russian corvette Merkury in the Libyan port of Benghazi days earlier, and together the two operations show Kyiv's growing willingness to hit Russian naval and logistics targets wherever they operate. Russia has not publicly acknowledged the Sparta II strike in detail, and it remains unclear how badly the vessel was damaged.

articles.title: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar visits Ukraine's Zakarpattia region
articles.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar arrived in Ukraine's Zakarpattia region on November 24 for talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. It is the first visit to Ukraine by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015. The trip follows Budapest's decision to allow the opening of two additional EU accession negotiation clusters for Ukraine.
articles.body: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar arrived in Ukraine's Zakarpattia region on November 24 for talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in the first visit to Ukraine by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015. The trip marks a notable thaw in a relationship that has been strained for years: Hungary, under its previous leadership, repeatedly blocked or slowed EU aid and sanctions against Russia and obstructed Ukraine's EU accession talks, citing the rights of the ethnic Hungarian minority in Zakarpattia. Magyar is also scheduled to meet representatives of that Hungarian community during the visit, a constituency that has been at the centre of the bilateral dispute. The visit follows Budapest's decision to allow the opening of two additional EU accession negotiation clusters for Ukraine — a concession that unblocked a key step in Kyiv's path toward membership. For Zelenskyy, the meeting is an opportunity to lock in the improved tone and to press for continued Hungarian support, particularly on energy and EU funding. For Magyar, who took office promising a more constructive European policy, the trip is a visible signal that Hungary's approach to its neighbour has changed. The two leaders are expected to discuss minority rights, cross-border cooperation and Ukraine's EU accession, though no major announcements were expected before the talks concluded.

articles.title: Russian overnight strikes cut power in five Ukrainian regions
articles.description: Russian overnight strikes cut power in five Ukrainian regions, with emergency and scheduled outages in effect as repair crews work to restore supply. Energy facilities in the Rivne region were hit on Tuesday morning, and a heating facility was damaged in an attack on Bila Tserkva in the Kyiv region. The strikes are part of Russia's systematic campaign against Ukraine's energy system ahead of winter.
articles.body: Russian overnight strikes cut power in five Ukrainian regions, with emergency and scheduled outages in effect as repair crews work to restore electricity. Energy facilities in the northern Rivne region were attacked on Tuesday morning, causing power outages, and a heating facility was damaged in an enemy attack on Bila Tserkva in the Kyiv region, the city council reported. The blackouts are the latest damage in Russia's systematic campaign against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, which has already knocked out five major thermal power plants in recent weeks — in Kharkiv, Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Ivano-Frankivsk and Dnipropetrovsk regions — and left cities such as Odesa facing the prospect of weeks without power. President Zelenskyy held a meeting on the electricity situation in the regions on November 24, and DTEK chief executive Maksym Tymchenko presented proposals on energy, infrastructure and the organisation of repair work, which the president said the government would support. The government has also approved additional measures to keep water utilities running, including backup power, equipment reserves and water deliveries if infrastructure is destroyed. For Ukrainians, the outages mean more nights in the dark and cold as winter sets in, and the authorities are urging households to prepare for prolonged scheduled blackouts. Repair teams are working around the clock, but each new wave of strikes undoes days of restoration work.

articles.title: Jet-powered drone flew 20 km into Poland overnight, Polish media report
articles.description: Polish media have learned that the unmanned aerial vehicle that violated Polish airspace on the night of November 23–24 was equipped with a jet engine and flew 20 kilometres into Polish territory. Polish air defences were activated during the incident, but the military held fire after the drone changed course eastward. It is the latest Russian drone incursion into NATO airspace during strikes on Ukraine.
articles.body: Polish media have learned that the unmanned aerial vehicle that violated Polish airspace on the night of November 23–24 was equipped with a jet engine and flew 20 kilometres into Polish territory, according to the radio station RMF24, as reported by European Pravda. Polish air defences were activated during the incident, but after the drone changed course eastward, the military refrained from firing, citing the risk of harm from debris. The incursion happened during another night of Russian strikes on Ukraine, and it is the latest in a series of Russian drones and missiles crossing into NATO territory — just days after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles fell in Poland during the November 20 attack, prompting Warsaw to summon the Russian envoy. Poland confirmed the new violation, and the episode adds to the pressure on NATO to decide how to respond to repeated airspace breaches that stop short of a direct attack. Each incident forces a split-second decision: shoot the object down and risk debris falling on populated areas, or let it pass and accept the violation. Warsaw has warned that it will defend its airspace, but the repeated incursions show how the war in Ukraine keeps spilling over its borders. The jet-powered drone is also a sign of Russia's upgraded arsenal — the same fast Shahed-type weapons that are now straining Ukraine's own air defences.

articles.title: Sky News film '24 Hours in the Kill Zone' about Ukraine's National Guard wins International Emmy
articles.description: Sky News's film '24 Hours in the Kill Zone', about Ukrainian National Guard service members, has won an International Emmy Award in the News category. The film follows guardsmen through a day on the front line. It is a rare major international award for frontline reporting from Ukraine's war.
articles.body: Sky News's film '24 Hours in the Kill Zone', about Ukrainian National Guard service members, has won an International Emmy Award in the News category. The film follows guardsmen through a single day on the front line, capturing the routine and the danger of their service in close, unflinching detail. The award is one of the most prestigious honours in international television journalism, and the win puts the daily reality of Ukraine's war in front of a global audience that has, in many countries, begun to tune the conflict out. For Sky News, it is recognition of the risks its crews have taken reporting from the front since 2022; for the National Guard, it is a tribute to soldiers whose work rarely makes headlines. The film's title reflects its structure — a full day embedded with a unit, from dawn briefings to night patrols — and its power comes from the ordinary moments as much as the combat: the waiting, the jokes, the calls home. Ukrainian media welcomed the award as a reminder that the war is still being fought, and still being witnessed, nearly five years after the full-scale invasion began. The International Emmys, held annually in New York, honour television made outside the United States, and the News category is one of its most competitive.

articles.title: Ukraine says attacks on ports threaten global food security
articles.description: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said Russian strikes on Ukrainian ports and export routes threaten global food security, speaking after a UN Security Council meeting. Russia has repeatedly targeted Odesa's port infrastructure and grain shipping in recent weeks. Ukraine is one of the world's largest grain exporters, and disruption to its exports pushes up food prices far beyond Europe.
articles.body: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has stated following a UN Security Council meeting that Russian strikes on Ukrainian ports and export routes threaten global food security. Russia has repeatedly attacked Odesa's port infrastructure, grain terminals and the shipping lanes Ukraine uses to export its harvests, most recently striking port facilities and a cargo vessel in the Black Sea. Ukraine is one of the world's largest exporters of wheat, corn and sunflower oil, and its grain feeds countries across the Middle East, Africa and Asia — so every attack on its export chain ripples into global food prices and supply. Kyiv has kept a shipping corridor running from Odesa despite the attacks, but insurers and shipowners grow warier with each strike, and freight costs rise. Sybiha's warning at the UN was aimed at countries that have treated the war as a distant European conflict: the food-security argument is Kyiv's way of telling the Global South that Russia's war reaches their dinner tables too. The Security Council meeting heard similar warnings from UN officials, who have repeatedly said that attacks on food infrastructure risk tipping vulnerable countries toward crisis. Russia, for its part, has framed the port strikes as attacks on military logistics, a claim Ukraine rejects. With the harvest season over and winter shipping under way, the coming weeks will test whether Ukraine's export corridor can keep functioning under fire.

articles.title: GTA VI posts the biggest PlayStation launch ever — over 39 million players on PS5 in four days
articles.description: Grand Theft Auto VI has delivered the biggest launch in the history of all five PlayStation generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment has announced. From November 19 to 22, more than 39 million players played the Rockstar crime epic on PlayStation 5, setting an all-time record for concurrent players on the platform. It matters because it confirms GTA VI as the largest entertainment launch ever, and it is already moving hardware: seven in ten new PS5 buyers launched GTA VI first.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI has delivered the biggest launch in the history of all five PlayStation generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment has announced. According to Sony's internal figures, the Rockstar Games crime epic attracted more than 39 million players on PlayStation 5 between November 19 and 22 inclusive. The game also set an absolute record for concurrent players on PlayStation consoles, beating every other title in history, including multiplayer and free-to-play hits. In the first four days, players spent a combined 683 million hours in the state of Leonida — an average of 17.4 hours per person. The launch drove a surge in console sales: the November 19–22 period included the record day for new systems connecting to the network, and seven out of ten new PlayStation 5 owners launched GTA VI first on their console. Demand had been building since October — in the first week of November, US PS5 sales rose 2.4 times year on year, according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, while Xbox Series X|S sales rose 2.3 times. Sony's Tim Turi congratulated Rockstar, noting the partnership dates back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2. The figures dwarf the already record-breaking first-day sales of 32.5 million copies reported at launch.

articles.title: Rockstar releases the first GTA VI patch, fixing crashes, weather and wanted-level bugs
articles.description: Rockstar Games has released the first post-launch update for Grand Theft Auto VI, patch 01.002.002, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The update targets performance and a clutch of early bugs, including broken autosaves, weather that could get stuck, missing story phone calls and a wanted level players could not shake. It is a small download — around 604 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox — and arrives just four days after the game's record-breaking launch.
articles.body: Rockstar Games released the first update for Grand Theft Auto VI on November 23, patch 01.002.002, available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The download is around 604 MB on Sony's console and about 1.6 GB on Microsoft's systems. The patch is focused on performance improvements and fixing several early bugs reported since launch. Rockstar fixed crashes, a bug that could leave the weather unchanged for long stretches, and problems with the autosave system. It also repaired issues that stopped players receiving phone calls, including calls needed to advance the story or unlock new missions. Other fixes cover a wanted level that players could not clear, a gym bug that prevented the character from using the barbell for deadlifts, and an issue where partners failed to hand over bags of items for selling to fences. The quick turnaround shows Rockstar moving fast on post-launch support for a game that drew more than 39 million PS5 players in its first four days, with more fixes expected as the studio works through launch-week reports.

articles.title: Microsoft slashes Gears of War: E-Day price by a third, just six weeks after launch
articles.description: Microsoft has cut the price of Gears of War: E-Day by 30% on PC and Xbox Series X|S, a Thanksgiving promotion running until December 2. A one-third cut barely six weeks after the October 6 global launch is highly unusual for a AAA release, and GameMAG links it to weak sales — analysts put total sales at around 400,000 copies by late October — and to competition from Grand Theft Auto VI. Players have also been criticising the developers for ignoring problems and a lack of feedback, echoing the situation around Forza Horizon 6.
articles.body: Microsoft has temporarily cut the price of Gears of War: E-Day by 30% on PC and Xbox Series X|S, GameMAG reports. The Thanksgiving-tied offer runs until December 2. The game's global release was on October 6, so a price cut of a third after just a month and a half is a very unusual move for a AAA title. GameMAG links the discount to soft sales: analysts estimated combined sales of all versions at around 400,000 copies by the end of October, while media reports put the production budget at about $500 million. Another factor is the release of Grand Theft Auto VI — other publishers are running sales and bonus-experience events to hold players' attention, while some have publicly pleaded with users not to delete their games to make room for Rockstar's hit. Active E-Day players have also been voicing frustration, criticising the developers for ignoring problems and a lack of communication, with balance issues and network problems in Horde mode among the complaints, particularly in Europe. GameMAG draws a parallel with the reaction around Forza Horizon 6, where players have raised similar grievances.

articles.title: AI-trailer backlash pushes Shift Up to a 'made by hand' rule for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain
articles.description: South Korean studio Shift Up has reworked its approach to AI after fans slammed a music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain that was made with generative AI. Studio head Kim Hyung-tae told a G-Star 2026 conference that the team has adopted a new principle — creating everything 'by hand from start to finish' — though AI will still assist with lighting tests, texture wear, polygon reduction and code checks. It is a notable public climbdown in the industry's hottest debate, and Kim warned a flood of AI-made 'slop' games is coming in 2027.
articles.body: South Korean studio Shift Up has changed its approach to artificial intelligence after a backlash over a promotional music video for Stellar Blade: Blood Rain that was made with generative AI, GameMAG reports. Many fans criticised the roughly three-and-a-half-minute K-pop-style video, centred on new protagonist Evie singing and dancing in a futuristic city, and questioned why the developers had served them what they called 'slop'. Studio head Kim Hyung-tae addressed the controversy at the G-Con conference during G-Star 2026, saying the team has adopted a new working principle: 'creating everything by hand from start to finish.' In an interview with Inven Global, Kim clarified that AI is not banned outright — it will still help with lighting tests, adding wear to textures, reducing polygon counts for optimisation, testing code and hunting bugs. But the creative core — scripts, design, level construction and game systems — is made by people, and artists create the concept and finish the final graphics. Kim initially defended the video, noting Evie herself was designed by humans, but ultimately said the studio would take fans' concerns seriously. He argued that games built mainly on automation will be seen as lower quality, and predicted a wave of cheap AI-made clones in 2027 — which, he believes, will make genuine human-made art more valued. Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami, who discussed AI with Kim, also uses neural networks to pre-check 3D models and sees AI NPCs as a promising direction. Shift Up is also reportedly interested in bringing Stellar Blade to Xbox, and plans to show its new flagship Project Spirits in 2027.

articles.title: Hellraiser: Revival beats Resident Evil Requiem to horror Game of the Year at the Horror Game Awards 2026
articles.description: Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival has been named Game of the Year at The Horror Game Awards 2026, beating favourite Resident Evil Requiem in an upset. The Saber Interactive horror game, which received no nominations at The Game Awards 2026, also won best acting for Doug Bradley's return as Pinhead. Requiem still took home the most awards overall — four, including scariest horror, best narrative and players' choice.
articles.body: The Horror Game Awards 2026, held on the evening of November 20, named Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival its Game of the Year in a surprise result, GameMAG reports. The Saber Interactive horror game beat Resident Evil Requiem, the favourite, for the top prize — despite having received no nominations at all at The Game Awards 2026. Hellraiser: Revival also won best acting, for Doug Bradley's return to the role of Pinhead, which he first played in Clive Barker's 1987 film. Critics were lukewarm on the game — it holds a 69% on Metacritic — but players rated it far more warmly, at 8.2 out of 10. Resident Evil Requiem still finished as the night's biggest winner with four awards: best narrative, scariest horror, most accessible horror and players' choice. Elsewhere, Tenebris Somnia won best indie horror and best art direction, with its makers Saibot Studios named best independent studio; Bloober Team took best developer; Silent Hill: Townfall won the critics' prize; the Silent Hill remake was named most anticipated horror; Akira Yamaoka received a lifetime achievement award; and Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film won best adaptation. The ceremony also premiered around ten trailers, including new footage for the realistic horror ILL and a Dead by Daylight collaboration with Terrifier.

articles.title: ILL shows off a gruesome new trailer at the Horror Game Awards, still on track for 2027
articles.description: The long-awaited realistic survival horror ILL received a new trailer at The Horror Game Awards 2026, and it is not for the faint-hearted — the footage is described as particularly violent. The game from Team Clout remains set for release in 2027. It was one of around ten trailers shown at the ceremony, alongside new reveals including Painted in Blood and Sker: The Bleeding Veil.
articles.body: The realistic survival horror ILL got a new trailer at The Horror Game Awards 2026, GameMAG reports, and it is not for the faint-hearted — coverage of the ceremony warns the footage is particularly violent to watch. ILL, developed by Team Clout, has been one of the most anticipated horror games since its reveal, built around photorealistic body horror and grotesque biomechanical monsters, and it remains on track for release in 2027. The trailer was one of around ten shown during the November 20 ceremony in London, which also featured new content for existing games and fresh announcements from small and mid-sized studios. Among the other reveals were Painted in Blood, a boomer shooter inspired by Doom 3 and Clive Barker's Undying; Sker: The Bleeding Veil, a new game from Stormind Games and Wales Interactive following on from Sker Ritual and Maid of Sker; and Shadow Sacrament, a gothic pixel-art Metroidvania in the Castlevania mould. The ceremony also gave 1666: Amsterdam a story update coming in December, and showed a new Dead by Daylight trailer tied to its Terrifier collaboration.

articles.title: Konami files trademarks for Silent Scope and Thrill Drive, reviving two classic arcade series
articles.description: Konami is registering trademarks for the names of two of its classic arcade series, Silent Scope and Thrill Drive, GameMAG reports. No games have been announced, and a trademark filing alone guarantees nothing — but it has fans speculating about revivals of the sniper light-gun series and the driving arcade series. Konami has been mining its back catalogue in recent years, with a Silent Hill remake already named the most anticipated horror at the Horror Game Awards.
articles.body: Konami is registering trademarks for the names of two of its classic arcade series, Silent Scope and Thrill Drive, GameMAG reports. Silent Scope was the sniper light-gun arcade series that debuted in 1999, famous for its rifle controller with a built-in scope, while Thrill Drive was Konami's arcade driving series. No games have been announced, and trademark registrations are often filed defensively, so the filings alone do not confirm new entries. But they have set fans speculating about revivals, especially as Konami has been actively mining its back catalogue in recent years — the Silent Hill remake from Bloober Team was just named the most anticipated horror game at The Horror Game Awards 2026, and Silent Hill: Townfall won the critics' prize at the same ceremony. The trademark news comes as the publisher continues to lean on its legacy franchises alongside new projects.

articles.title: Persona 6 won't end the series — Atlus promises faster sequels after the long wait
articles.description: Persona 6 will not be the end of the franchise, Atlus producer Kazuhisa Wada has said, and the studio is working to shorten the long gaps between numbered entries. Persona 6 was unveiled at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026 — a decade after Persona 5 — and still has no release date, though it is planned for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Switch 2, on Game Pass at launch. Fans waited more than ten years between mainline entries, and Wada says the team is working on various things so the next wait is not so long.
articles.body: Persona 6 will not be the end of the series, Atlus producer Kazuhisa Wada has said, and the studio is already planning for what comes after it. In an interview with Sega Sammy's internal publication, translated by GamesRadar+, Wada said: 'Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things so that you will not have to wait so long for the next installment.' The comments, first reported on November 20, amount to an early tease of Persona 7 before Persona 6 even has a release date. Wada stressed that Persona 6 remains the team's top priority and expressed confidence in its direction, saying 'we are creating something even better than before,' despite challenges during production. He acknowledged that big RPGs like Persona take five years or more to develop — Persona 6's production began in 2021, after the global launch of Persona 5 Royal — and said the studio is exploring ways to cut the wait, possibly through parallel development or new tools, though he did not say how. Fans have waited over a decade since Persona 5 launched in 2016; the sixth entry was finally unveiled at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026 with a moody, green-hued graveyard teaser suggesting a darker tone, and is planned for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2, with availability on Xbox Game Pass at launch. Sega has also confirmed a physical edition on PS5 and Switch 2, suggesting a release before 2028, when Sony stops producing new game discs. Atlus says fans will hear more after Persona 4 Revival launches early next year.

articles.title: From the DOJ to Nvidia, Trump's presidency enters a new age of impunity
articles.description: President Donald Trump's summit last week with the rulers of Russia and China implied powerful men can do as they please — and on Monday, he proved it, CNN's analysis argues. Trump used his influence to restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, visited the Justice Department to condemn California Governor Gavin Newsom's commutation of hundreds of death sentences, and is expected to award Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday. With Democrats about to take power in Congress, the piece frames a presidency increasingly unconstrained by norms.
articles.body: President Donald Trump's summit last week with the rulers of Russia and China implied that powerful men can do exactly as they please, and on Monday he proved it, CNN's analysis argues. Trump described how he used his influence to restore AI king Jensen Huang to his job running Nvidia, which by most estimates is the world's most critical company, just 11 days after Huang resigned under pressure. Huang's restoration was followed by a sharp spike in share prices that eased the president's concerns over crashing stock markets. Trump's flexing of power on Monday was hardly limited to Nvidia. He made the short trip from the White House to the Justice Department to condemn California's outgoing Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom for his commutation of hundreds of death sentences, giving voice to relatives of victims of Death Row inmates — but the choice of venue seemed a deliberate reminder that he has demolished the wall between the White House and an agency traditionally seen as dispensing justice above the political fray. He also temporarily halted a US Army plan to blow up nearly five tons of hazardous material in Iowa, while warning that if the chemicals spontaneously combusted it would be the fault of incoming Democratic Governor Rob Sand. And in another display almost designed to outrage his foes, Trump is expected to award Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday — Giuliani announced the award on Steve Bannon's podcast and led Trump's legal team in the bid to overturn the 2020 election. Meanwhile, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on CNN's 'State of the Union' on Sunday that China had illicitly obtained advanced Nvidia chips despite US export controls. 'We're living in something like a monarchical corporate state where the corporations have their way with the government, and then the president of the United States decides he's going to weigh in on the meeting of a corporate board of directors,' Representative Jamie Raskin, incoming chair of the House Judiciary Committee, told CNN.

articles.title: UPDATE: Army set to detonate explosives in Iowa on Wednesday after court lifts pause over lead fears
articles.description: The US Army will go ahead with the controlled detonation of degraded explosive material at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday morning, after a federal appeals court on Monday lifted a pause environmental groups had sought over fears of lead contamination. President Trump had temporarily halted the operation amid a public outcry, and the Army had postponed it to November 23 before settling on November 24 — now the detonation is set for Wednesday. The new development is the court ruling clearing the legal hurdle, not a repeat of the earlier pause story.
articles.body: The US Army said it will move forward with the controlled detonation of degraded explosive material at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday morning, after a federal appeals court lifted a pause that environmental groups had sought over fears of lead contamination. The Army plans to detonate deteriorating explosives — nearly five tons of hazardous material, including lead azide — at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant after the appeals court on Monday rejected the environmental groups' bid to stop it, clearing a legal hurdle for the operation. The detonation had become a political flashpoint: President Trump temporarily halted the Army's plan amid a public outcry over fears of lead contamination, then warned that if the chemicals spontaneously combusted in the meantime, it would be the fault of incoming Democratic Governor Rob Sand. Court filings show the Army then postponed the operation to November 23, before settling on November 24, and the operation is now scheduled for Wednesday morning. Environmental groups had argued the blast could spread lead contamination; the Army maintains the controlled detonation is the safe way to dispose of the degraded material.

articles.title: Inside the Trump pressure campaign that restored Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
articles.description: President Donald Trump spent days stewing over the US stock market's deepening sell-off before deciding there was only one way to stop the slide: put Jensen Huang back atop Nvidia. His conclusion late last week sparked an unprecedented West Wing pressure campaign to convince the tech giant to reinstate its CEO just 11 days after he resigned under pressure, people familiar with the matter told CNN. Trump said on CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to the board 'directly and indirectly' — and Nvidia announced the reinstatement based on 'input from senior levels' of the government.
articles.body: President Donald Trump had been stewing for days over the US stock market's deepening sell-off when he decided there was only one way to stop the slide: put Jensen Huang back atop Nvidia. Trump's conclusion late last week sparked an unprecedented West Wing pressure campaign orchestrated by the president to convince the tech giant to reinstate its scandal-ridden CEO just 11 days after he resigned under pressure, several people familiar with the matter told CNN. 'I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,' Trump said Monday on CNBC, shortly after Nvidia announced that, based on 'input from senior levels' of the government, it was reinstating Huang as CEO. The intervention is without modern precedent: a sitting president leaning on the board of the world's most valuable company — and by most estimates the world's most critical company, at the centre of the AI boom — to reverse a corporate governance decision. It also comes as Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on CNN's 'State of the Union' on Sunday that China had illicitly obtained advanced Nvidia chips despite US export controls meant to prevent such transfers. Huang's return immediately supercharged a market rally, with the Nasdaq Composite surging 6.5% on Monday, its best day in 19 months. Critics, including incoming House Judiciary chair Jamie Raskin, called the episode a sign of a 'monarchical corporate state' in which the president weighs in on a corporate board meeting; supporters in the administration frame it as a defence of American technological leadership and market stability.

articles.title: AI's most powerful CEO is back. But how long will the market confidence last?
articles.description: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia has revived hopes for an AI industry badly shaken in recent weeks. Stocks rebounded early Monday, but Huang's return supercharged the rally — the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, its best day in 19 months — and shares in Nvidia-backed 'neoclouds' like CoreWeave jumped 22%. Analysts caution the bounce rests on the idea that Nvidia's role as the 'central bank of AI' is intact, and the underlying questions about the AI boom's financing have not gone away.
articles.body: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia has revived hopes for an AI industry that has been badly shaken in recent weeks, CNN reports. Stocks were rebounding early Monday, but Huang's return supercharged the rally: the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, its best day in 19 months. Huang's return 'gives some hope to the idea that Nvidia's role as the central bank of AI is still intact,' Jay Goldberg, senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners, told CNN. The rally spread well beyond Nvidia itself. It caused a sharp jump in the so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave, which rent out compute power for the AI boom and are backed by Nvidia — CoreWeave shares had closed on Friday at $39.51, below their 2025 IPO price and down 35% since Huang's initial ousting, but jumped 22% on Monday as his return cleared up uncertainty for investors. The question now is how durable the confidence is. The AI financing boom that powered the rally has also raised concerns about leverage and valuations, and the circumstances of Huang's exit and return — a boardroom episode that wiped $1.5 trillion in value and drew direct presidential intervention — have left governance questions hanging over the world's most critical chipmaker. For now, though, markets have taken the reinstatement as a signal that the AI trade is back on.

articles.title: Army auditors fear key units are unprepared to deploy in a Pacific war scenario
articles.description: The US Army's internal audit agency fears the service may not be able to quickly deploy forces from its Hawaii bases as planned in the event of war with China in the western Pacific, according to a report CNN obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request. The Army Audit Agency report, completed in April, found 'unaddressed infrastructure and equipment issues' and administrative confusion over the responsibilities of a field support battalion charged with supporting deployments from Hawaii. The findings land as the Pentagon's planning focus shifts squarely to a possible Pacific conflict.
articles.body: The US Army's internal audit agency fears the service may not be able to quickly deploy forces from its Hawaii bases as planned in the event of war with China in the western Pacific, according to a report that CNN obtained via the Freedom of Information Act. The report by the Army Audit Agency, completed in April, found 'unaddressed infrastructure and equipment issues' and administrative confusion over the responsibilities of a field support battalion charged with supporting deployments from Hawaii. Hawaii is the hub for the Army's Pacific posture, home to units that would be among the first sent west in a conflict with China, so delays in moving troops and equipment out of the islands would matter in the opening days of a war. The audit's findings point to gaps between the Pentagon's war plans and the practical ability to execute them — the kind of readiness shortfall that auditors are meant to catch before a crisis exposes it. The report's emergence comes as the Trump administration's defence planning has put a possible Pacific conflict at the centre of US military strategy, and as the Army's role in deterring China faces growing scrutiny in Congress.

articles.title: UPDATE: Storms to hit both coasts, threatening Thanksgiving travel for millions and Macy's 100th parade
articles.description: Two storms will hit the US coasts this Thanksgiving week, threatening travel for millions and the Macy's parade in New York. The East Coast storm forms off the Southeast on Wednesday, bringing heavy rain, winds up to 60 mph and serious coastal flooding from the Carolinas to New Jersey, with the worst in the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day itself. The new details since the earlier report: a high wind watch now covers New York City, Long Island and northeastern New Jersey from Thursday morning, and the parade's 100th anniversary could see gusts over 40 mph — the threshold that grounds balloons.
articles.body: Mother Nature could crash Thanksgiving this year, with storms on the East and West coasts set to amplify king tide problems and snarl travel and holiday plans. Both storms will deliver heavy rain, snow, strong winds and severe coastal flooding. The East Coast storm will get itself together on Wednesday when it forms just off the Southeast, giving travellers a window early this week to beat its worst impacts. It will be the second storm to cross the East Coast since last week, when the first set off disastrous flooding along Florida's Atlantic coast. The new storm will not produce rainfall as extreme as last week's, but it will coincide with the highest tides of the month and produce serious coastal flooding from the Carolinas northward. Major flooding is possible in Charleston, South Carolina, during Wednesday morning's high tide, and moderate to major coastal flooding is likely as far north as the Chesapeake Bay. A high wind watch is in effect for most of the New Jersey coast, where gusts of up to 60 mph are possible, and the National Weather Service has issued a high wind watch for New York City, Long Island and parts of northeastern New Jersey from 10 a.m. Thursday until 1 a.m. Friday. Wednesday night into Thanksgiving morning will see wet and windy conditions expand into the Tennessee and Ohio valleys and parts of the Midwest, with a few inches of snow possible from central Missouri to central Indiana. The timing puts the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade — its 100th anniversary — at risk: gusts over 40 mph stretching from Washington, D.C., through Philadelphia and New York into New England on Thursday could ground the balloons. The FAA is preparing for its busiest Thanksgiving period in 16 years, with more than 417,000 flights forecast over the nine-day holiday and Tuesday, November 24, expected to be the busiest day, with over 52,000 flights. A separate storm and atmospheric river are bringing repeated rain and mountain snow to the West, with Washington State Ferries already announcing cancellations due to extreme tides.

articles.title: UPDATE: San Francisco braces for near-record tides as a storm collides with Thanksgiving travel
articles.description: San Francisco Bay could rise to near-record levels this week as a strong storm meets some of the year's highest tides, threatening flooding and travel disruption on the busiest travel days of the year. The National Weather Service has issued a rare coastal flood warning for Monday through Thanksgiving Day, with peak flooding around each morning's high tide and the highest water expected Wednesday. New since the earlier report: Mayor Daniel Lurie says floodwaters are not expected to reach the tarmac at SFO, though high winds could still trigger a ground stop, and United Airlines is waiving change fees for SFO flights through November 28.
articles.body: San Francisco Bay could rise to near-record levels this week, as a strong storm coupled with some of the year's highest tides moves ashore, threatening travel disruptions and flooding along city streets on some of the busiest travel days of the year. The National Weather Service issued a rare coastal flood warning for Monday through Thanksgiving Day, with peak flooding around each morning's high tide and the highest water expected Wednesday. Water levels may reach as much as 2.8 feet above a normal high tide, approaching the record set in 1983, Dylan Flynn, a lead meteorologist with the National Weather Service's San Francisco Bay Area office, told CNN. 'Another storm, a cold front, is coming that's stronger than what we dealt with last couple days … on top of king tides, on top of El Niño, all of that bumps the water level up,' Flynn said, adding that Thanksgiving week 'just happens to be unfortunately lining up with the highest tides we've seen in 40 years.' San Francisco International Airport, which had more than 1.8 million passengers pass through its gates in the 12 days around Thanksgiving last year, and Oakland-San Francisco Bay Airport, which expects about 250,000, both sit on low-lying land right along the bay. In a video update posted on Facebook late Monday, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie assured travellers that SFO is not expecting floodwaters to reach onto the tarmac. 'At this moment we're not expecting floodwaters to reach onto the tarmac at SFO, which is a positive development,' Lurie said, while warning that high winds could prompt a ground stop. SFO has staged sandbags and portable flood barriers in high-risk areas. United Airlines is waiving change fees and fare differences out of SFO for new flights departing between November 22 and November 28. Forecasters are in regular contact with both airports' emergency operations centres, and Flynn said the airports have known about the king tides well in advance and are well prepared — though drivers should expect numerous road closures getting to the airports.

articles.title: Warner Music Group tops $2B in a quarter for the first time as subscription streaming jumps 14.7%
articles.description: Warner Music Group generated $2.001 billion in revenue in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 — the first time its quarterly revenues have crossed the $2 billion mark, beating the previous record of $1.868 billion set a year earlier. Recorded music subscription streaming rose 14.7% year-on-year to $804 million, and full-year fiscal 2026 revenues hit an all-time high of $7.437 billion. CEO Robert Kyncl credited a multi-year transformation strategy, while the company pointed to AI licensing as a growth vector for fiscal 2027.
articles.body: Warner Music Group published results on Thursday, November 19, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 — calendar Q3 and the company's fiscal Q4 — showing total revenues of $2.001 billion, up 7.5% year-on-year at constant currency. It is the first time WMG's quarterly revenues have crossed $2 billion, beating the previous record of $1.868 billion set in calendar Q3 2025. Recorded music revenues rose 7.3% to $1.639 billion, with total streaming up 13.2% to $1.056 billion and subscription streaming up 14.7% to $804 million — an acceleration from 10.8% growth in the prior quarter, helped by price and wholesale rate increases, market share gains and a $7 million DSP audit payment. Physical revenue jumped 30.5% to $167 million on strong releases, while artist services and expanded-rights revenue fell 19.9% to $257 million, largely because the year-ago quarter included heavy Oasis merchandising. Music publishing at Warner Chappell rose 7.4% to $363 million. Net income nearly doubled to $179 million from $109 million, and adjusted OIBDA rose 17.2% to $477 million, a 23.8% margin. For the full fiscal year, revenues reached a record $7.437 billion, with net income of $735 million versus $370 million a year earlier. Top sellers in the quarter included Madonna, Number_i, Charli XCX, Bruno Mars and Linkin Park. Looking ahead, WMG said its fiscal 2027 outlook is supported by healthy industry trends, improved DSP terms and new growth vectors including AI licensing.

articles.title: ATC Music Group to acquire the UK's One Media iP for $20M, securing a facility of up to $133M to buy more music rights
articles.description: London-headquartered ATC Music Group has agreed to acquire UK music rights company One Media iP for £15 million (about $20 million), funded largely by a new facility from US-based Corrum Capital. The deal gives ATC a music rights and digital distribution operation at scale for the first time, and the conditional facility can grow to £100 million (about $133 million) for future catalog acquisitions. The acquired business will be rebranded ATC Rights, led by former Round Hill Music global COO Steve Clark.
articles.body: ATC Music Group announced on Monday, November 23, that it has agreed to acquire UK-based music rights company One Media iP for £15 million (approximately $20 million). The majority of the price, £12 million, will be funded from a new acquisition facility provided by funds managed by US-based Corrum Capital Management, which lends to music, entertainment and sports companies. The conditional facility comprises £12 million of committed financing, with the ability to add further uncommitted facilities up to a total of £100 million (about $133 million) for future acquisitions of music rights and catalogs. ATC also conditionally raised about £3.1 million (about $4.1 million) through an oversubscribed share placing, around £2 million of which will go toward the purchase price. The acquired business will be rebranded as ATC Rights, with former Round Hill Music Global COO Steve Clark joining as Managing Director. One Media iP, established in 2005, owns a catalog of more than 400,000 assets, including master recordings, composition rights and producer royalties, and generated revenues of £4.8 million and profit before tax of £0.9 million in the year to October 31, 2025. The sale requires approval from One Media iP Group shareholders at a general meeting on December 11, with holders of 32.2% of shares already giving irrevocable undertakings in support. ATC CEO Adam Driscoll said the acquisition completes the platform the company has spent five years building: it now represents artists, services their commercial lives, promotes live work, and owns and distributes rights. ATC's management arm represents more than 100 artists, writers and producers, including Radiohead, Nick Cave and Robbie Williams.

articles.title: Cinq Music Group signs multi-year deal with TikTok, bringing around 600 songs to the platform's Commercial Music Library
articles.description: Cinq Music Group has signed a multi-year deal with TikTok covering the platform's Commercial Music Library, the pre-cleared catalog brands use in organic posts, video ads and branded content. About 600 songs from Cinq's catalog are now available in the library, starting with a first wave of titles, with more to come including releases from its Nashville country imprint Orinda. Early placements already include a banner for 3Ball MTY's 'Besos Al Aire' and playlist spots for Los Socios del Ritmo and LDNE.
articles.body: Cinq Music Group announced on Monday, November 23, that it has signed a multi-year deal with TikTok covering the platform's Commercial Music Library (CML). Approximately 600 songs from Cinq's catalog are now available for use in content via the CML, TikTok's library of pre-cleared music that businesses can use in organic posts, video ads and branded content. The company says the rollout begins with a first wave of titles, and more music is on the way, including releases from Orinda, GoDigital Music's Nashville-based country imprint. Eligible tracks can be placed in playlists and banners within the CML, and Cinq says it has already secured early placements, including a banner placement for 3Ball MTY's 'Besos Al Aire', playlist placements for Los Socios del Ritmo's 'A Que Hora Sales Por El Pan' and LDNE's 'Labios Rojos', and recommendations for Marisela's 'Mi Problema' and a remix of Griss Romero's 'Cómo Tú'. Cinq's Head of Sync Licensing, Leslie Arredondo-Cordero, said micro-licensing has become an important element of modern sync strategies. TikTok's Commercial Music Lead, Chris Marion, said bringing more of Cinq's diverse global catalog into the CML gives brands greater choice while opening commercial opportunities for independent artists. The deal follows TikTok's multi-year agreement with licensing technology company Chordal in July 2025, which integrated its InstantClear technology into the CML. Cinq, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Los Angeles, manages a catalog of more than 80,000 assets spanning Latin music, Afrobeats, hip-hop and regional Mexican, and has worked with artists including Janet Jackson, Jason Derulo, T.I. and Daddy Yankee. Its parent company GoDigital raised $230 million in November 2025, bringing its total funding to more than $1 billion.

articles.title: Super-premium tiers accounted for two-thirds of China's net music subscriber additions last year, says Universal Music Group
articles.description: Super-premium streaming tiers drove two-thirds of net subscriber additions in China's music market last year, according to Universal Music Group's Michael Nash, speaking at Morgan Stanley's European TMT conference. Adoption of Tencent Music's Super VIP tier, priced at three to five times the basic rate, is now approaching or passing 20% — the threshold UMG identified as the market opportunity. Nash said UMG hopes other platforms will copy China's tiering success, and he also revealed UMG has been windowing new releases in India for paying subscribers since late August.
articles.body: Super-premium streaming tiers accounted for two-thirds of net subscriber additions in China's music market last year, according to Universal Music Group, whose EVP and Chief Digital Officer Michael Nash cited the company's research at Morgan Stanley's European Technology, Media & Telecom Conference on Wednesday, November 18. Nash also said UMG expects adoption of the Super VIP (SVIP) tier at Tencent Music Entertainment to now be approaching or surpassing the 20% threshold the company has identified as the market opportunity for super-premium tiers. Tencent Music reported on November 17 that SVIP recorded another quarter of growth in both paying users and average revenue per paying user, and the tier had already surpassed 20 million subscribers by the end of 2025 — about 15.7% of the company's 127.4 million paying music subscribers at the time. SVIP subscribers pay approximately RMB 40 ($5.97) per month, compared with RMB 8 ($1.19) for a standard subscription. Nash stressed the trend is not limited to Tencent, naming rival Chinese platforms NetEase Cloud Music and ByteDance-owned Soda Music, and called China the world's No. 2 digital market, on a major growth spurt. IFPI data shows China overtook Germany to become the world's fourth-largest recorded music market overall in 2025, with revenues up 20.1% year-on-year. Nash also tied UMG's China experience to its decision to window new releases in India: since the end of August, UMG's new releases from major domestic and international artists have been available only to paying streaming subscribers for their first 72 hours, with early results described as encouraging. The success in China contrasts with slower progress elsewhere: Spotify launched a higher-priced Premium Platinum tier in five emerging markets in November 2025, but in Western markets super-premium tiers are being built around AI tools, including an AI covers and remixes product Spotify plans to launch in the first quarter of 2027 at a reported $4 to $5 per month on top of existing subscriptions.

articles.title: NetEase Cloud Music's Q3 revenues fell 0.9% to $290m as subscription growth slowed sharply
articles.description: NetEase Cloud Music's revenues fell 0.9% year-on-year to RMB 1.95 billion ($290.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, its controlling shareholder NetEase disclosed on November 19. Subscription revenue growth has slowed to roughly a third of its pace a year earlier — up 5.3% in the first half of 2026 versus 15.2% in the first half of 2025. The platform has now re-signed with all three major music companies in 2026, most recently Sony, but its rival Tencent Music grew membership revenues 9.2% in the same quarter.
articles.body: NetEase Cloud Music's revenues fell 0.9% year-on-year to RMB 1.95 billion ($290.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, down from RMB 1.96 billion in Q3 2025 and down 1.6% quarter-over-quarter from RMB 1.98 billion in Q2 2026. The figures were disclosed by the streaming platform's controlling shareholder, NetEase, which published its Q3 results on Thursday, November 19. Gross profit rose 0.5% year-on-year to RMB 698.0 million ($104.1 million), with gross margin broadly stable at 35.9%, and across the first nine months of 2026 revenues rose 2.0% to RMB 5.90 billion ($880.7 million). The Q3 release did not include a subscription revenue breakdown, but the platform's most recent figures, from its first-half results in August, showed membership subscription revenues of RMB 2.60 billion ($381.8 million), up 5.3% year-on-year — a sharp slowdown from 15.2% growth in the first half of 2025 and 13.3% across full-year 2025. The company attributed the moderation partly to dilution in average revenue per paying user as its subscriber mix changed, while saying retention and renewal rates improved. The results follow Sony Music Entertainment's renewal of its licensing agreement with NetEase Cloud Music earlier this month, meaning the platform has now re-signed with all three major music companies in 2026, after Universal in January and Warner in July. Rival Tencent Music Entertainment reported on November 17 that its membership services revenues rose 9.2% year-on-year to RMB 4.99 billion ($744 million) in Q3, its first full quarter including Ximalaya, the audio platform it acquired for $2.4 billion in May. NetEase Cloud Music describes itself as having over 200 million monthly active users, though research firm QuestMobile put it at 147 million in March, behind ByteDance-owned Soda Music's 156 million.

articles.title: Pophouse appoints Oak View Group's Kristina Heney and Netflix's Greg Lombardo as Presidents
articles.description: Pophouse Entertainment, the ABBA Voyage backer co-founded by ABBA's Björn Ulvaeus, has appointed Kristina Heney as President, Commercial & Marketing, and Greg Lombardo as President, Pophouse Avatar Network. Heney joins from Oak View Group, where she led marketing across around 400 venues, and previously ran global branding at Cirque du Soleil. Lombardo joins from Netflix, where he spent seven and a half years building its experiences business to more than 300 cities, including Netflix House venues.
articles.body: Pophouse Entertainment has appointed Kristina Heney and Greg Lombardo as Presidents, the company announced. Heney joins as President, Commercial & Marketing, from Oak View Group, and will be based in New York, leading commercial growth, marketing, data strategy, ticketing and sponsorship across Pophouse's brands, productions and experiences. Lombardo joins as President, Pophouse Avatar Network, from Netflix, and will be based in Los Angeles, leading creative development, production and operations for the company's technology-led live productions, plus the strategy and delivery of avatar venues. Heney most recently served as EVP, Marketing, Media and Conferences at Oak View Group, leading brand, marketing, communications, data and business analytics across around 400 owned and serviced venues in North America, Europe and the Middle East. She was previously Chief Marketing & Experience Officer of Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group, leading global branding and revenue performance for ten brands across 65 countries, working with IP owners including Disney, Lionel Messi, Michael Jackson, The Beatles and Soda Stereo, and earlier spent 15 years at Madison Square Garden Entertainment. Lombardo was VP and Global Head of Experiences at Netflix for seven and a half years, launching the company's experiences business and scaling it to more than 300 cities, with shows including The Queen's Ball: A Bridgerton Experience and Squid Game: Survive the Trials, and he conceived Netflix House, the company's permanent entertainment venues in Dallas and Philadelphia, with a Las Vegas location opening in 2027. Pophouse CEO Jessica Koravos said the two bring the combination of commercial discipline and creative ambition the company needs for its next chapter. Pophouse, co-founded in 2014 by ABBA's Björn Ulvaeus and EQT founder Conni Jonsson, specializes in music catalog investments, with a portfolio including Sia, Iron Maiden, Tina Turner, KISS, Cyndi Lauper, Avicii and Swedish House Mafia, and is a founding investor in ABBA Voyage. The appointments follow a string of big catalog deals, including Sia selling a 50% stake in her catalog to Pophouse for a reported $180 million in October, a stake in Iron Maiden's catalog in July, and the KISS deal reported at more than $300 million.

articles.title: Vevo names first batch of dscvr Artists to Watch for 2027
articles.description: Vevo has unveiled the first batch of its Artists to Watch for 2027, its annual dscvr program spotlighting emerging talent: Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes and Die Spitz. The five acts open the year's list, with more names to follow. The dscvr program has become one of Vevo's flagship discovery platforms for rising artists.
articles.body: Vevo has introduced the first batch of its Artists to Watch for 2027, opening the next edition of its annual dscvr discovery program. The first five names are Dalvin La Melodía, Conep, Devon Again, Mari Froes and Die Spitz, a deliberately varied group spanning Latin music, indie and rock. Vevo's dscvr Artists to Watch is one of the platform's flagship emerging-talent programs, using filmed live performances and editorial support to introduce rising acts to Vevo's global audience. The first batch sets the tone for the 2027 list, with further artists expected to be announced as the program rolls out. For the five acts named, the nod puts them in front of the music-video platform's audience at a moment when Vevo's discovery franchises remain a key route for new artists to reach mainstream attention. The selection continues Vevo's pattern of mixing genres and geographies in its annual list, rather than concentrating on a single scene.

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter and Billy Strings to headline Hinterland 2027
articles.description: Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter and Billy Strings will headline Iowa's three-day Hinterland Music Festival next summer, Rolling Stone reports. The festival takes place in Saint Charles, Iowa, from July 30 to August 1, 2027. The bill also includes Remi Wolf, Malcolm Todd, Stephen Wilson Jr. and Caroline Polachek, with Haywire slated to perform in a cornfield.
articles.body: Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter and Billy Strings will headline Iowa's three-day Hinterland Music Festival next summer, Rolling Stone reports. The festival will take place in Saint Charles, Iowa, from July 30 to August 1, 2027, and the three headliners anchor a bill that mixes indie, pop and bluegrass. Other performers announced include Remi Wolf, Malcolm Todd, Stephen Wilson Jr., Caroline Polachek and Westside Cowboy, with Haywire slated to perform in a cornfield — a nod to the festival's rural Iowa setting. Bridgers tops the bill as she continues her Lost Tour into 2027, while Slayyyter and Billy Strings bring pop and bluegrass audiences to the same weekend. Hinterland has built a reputation as a destination festival that pairs big names with a laid-back, small-town atmosphere, and the 2027 lineup leans into that mix. The announcement adds another major summer festival date to the 2027 calendar, which is filling up fast with headliner reveals.

articles.title: Staind announce new album 'The Space Between the Darkness and the Light' and share single 'Watch Me Break'
articles.description: Staind have announced a new album, 'The Space Between the Darkness and the Light', arriving March 5, 2027, and shared the single 'Watch Me Break'. The release coincides with the launch of the second North American leg of the band's Break the Cycle 25th Anniversary Tour, which kicks off March 4 in Manchester, New Hampshire. It is the band's next full-length since their 2023 reunion album 'Confessions of the Fallen'.
articles.body: Staind have announced a new album titled 'The Space Between the Darkness and the Light', set to arrive March 5, 2027, Rolling Stone reports, and in advance of its release the band has unleashed the single 'Watch Me Break'. The album's release coincides with the launch of the recently announced second North American leg of Staind's Break the Cycle 25th Anniversary Tour, which kicks off March 4 in Manchester, New Hampshire. The tour celebrates the 25th anniversary of 'Break the Cycle', the 2001 album that made Staind one of the biggest rock bands of the early 2000s with hits like 'It's Been Awhile'. The new album follows the band's 2023 reunion record 'Confessions of the Fallen', their first in 12 years, and signals that the reunited lineup is now operating as an ongoing concern rather than a one-off nostalgia run. 'Watch Me Break' gives fans a first taste of the new material ahead of the spring tour. The announcement continues a busy stretch of legacy rock acts pairing new albums with anniversary tours.

articles.title: Bruce Dickinson already has a new solo album and tour dates lined up for Iron Maiden's break
articles.description: Iron Maiden frontman Bruce Dickinson already has a new solo album and tour dates on deck for the band's break, Rolling Stone reports.
